# Chapter 26: The Full Axum Router

## Production Router Configuration

The production router includes all routes, middleware, and static file serving:

```rust
pub async fn build_router(state: Arc<AppState>) -> Router {
    // API routes
    let api_routes = Router::new()
        .route("/export", get(routes::export::export_handler))
        .route("/meta", get(routes::meta::meta_handler))
        .route("/remote", get(routes::meta::remote_handler))
        .route("/search", get(routes::search::search_handler))
        .route("/tags", get(routes::tags::list_tags))
        .route("/tags/submit", post(routes::tags::submit_tag))
        .route("/tags/vote", post(routes::tags::vote_tag))
        .route("/tags/flag", post(routes::tags::flag_tag))
        .route("/recommendations/{source}", get(routes::recommender::get_recommendations))
        .route("/suggestions", get(routes::recommender::list_suggestions))
        .route("/suggestions/submit", post(routes::recommender::submit_suggestion))
        .route("/suggestions/vote", post(routes::recommender::cast_vote));

    // OPDS routes
    let opds_routes = routes::opds::opds_router();

    // Static file serving
    let frontend_dir = state.config.frontend_dir.clone();
    let static_files = ServeDir::new(&frontend_dir)
        .not_found_service(ServeFile::new(
            frontend_dir.join("index.html")
        ));

    Router::new()
        .nest("/api/v0", api_routes)
        .nest("/opds", opds_routes)
        .route_service("/assets/*path", ServeDir::new(
            frontend_dir.join("assets")
        ))
        .route("/cache/*path", get(routes::cache_download::download_handler))
        .fallback_service(static_files)
        .layer(TraceLayer::new_for_http())
        .layer(CorsLayer::new()
            .allow_origin(Any)
            .allow_methods(Any)
            .allow_headers(Any))
        .with_state(state)
}
```

**Route nesting** keeps the code organized. All API routes live under `/api/v0`, all OPDS routes under `/opds`. This makes it easy to add versioning later (`/api/v1/...`).

## Static File Serving

The frontend is built as static files (HTML, CSS, JS). Axum serves them efficiently:

```rust
// Immutable assets (JS, CSS, images with content hashes)
// Cache for 1 year — the hash in the filename guarantees uniqueness
let assets_dir = frontend_dir.join("assets");
let immutable_assets = ServeDir::new(&assets_dir)
    .precompressed_gzip()
    .precompressed_br()
    .layer(Extension(CacheControl::new()
        .max_age(Duration::from_secs(31536000))));

// index.html — no caching (always get the latest version)
let index_html = ServeFile::new(frontend_dir.join("index.html"))
    .layer(Extension(CacheControl::new()
        .no_cache()
        .must_revalidate()));
```

**Why different caching strategies?**
- `assets/app.a1b2c3.js` — The filename contains a hash. When the code changes, the hash changes, and the browser requests a new file. Safe to cache forever.
- `index.html` — Always needs to be fresh because it references the current asset hashes.

# Chapter 27: Serving Static Files

## The Frontend Build Output

When you run `npm run build` in the frontend directory, SvelteKit produces:

```
frontend/build/
├── _app/
│   ├── immutable/
│   │   ├── assets/
│   │   │   ├── app.a1b2c3.js          ← Main bundle
│   │   │   ├── app.d4e5f6.css         ← Styles
│   │   │   └── nodes/
│   │   │       ├── 0.g7h8i9.js        ← Layout
│   │   │       └── 1.j0k1l2.js        ← Page
│   │   └── start.m3n4o5.js            ← Entry point
│   └── version.json                   ← Build version
├── favicon.png
├── index.html                         ← Shell HTML
└── manifest.webmanifest
```

Each JS file has a unique hash in its name. This enables aggressive caching — the browser can cache `app.a1b2c3.js` forever because if the content changes, the hash will be different (e.g., `app.x9y0z1.js`).

## Nginx Configuration

For production, we use nginx as a reverse proxy:

```nginx
server {
    listen 80;
    server_name fichub.example.com;

    # Redirect HTTP to HTTPS
    return 301 https://$host$request_uri;
}

server {
    listen 443 ssl http2;
    server_name fichub.example.com;

    # SSL certificates (Let's Encrypt)
    ssl_certificate /etc/letsencrypt/live/fichub.example.com/fullchain.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/fichub.example.com/privkey.pem;

    # Security headers
    add_header X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN" always;
    add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always;
    add_header X-XSS-Protection "1; mode=block" always;

    # Proxy to Axum
    location / {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3000;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    }

    # Cache static assets aggressively
    location /assets/ {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3000;
        proxy_cache_valid 200 1y;
        add_header Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable";
    }

    # Don't cache HTML
    location ~* \.html$ {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3000;
        add_header Cache-Control "no-cache, must-revalidate";
    }
}
```

# Chapter 28: Docker and Docker Compose

## The Dockerfile

FicHub uses a multi-stage Docker build for small, efficient images:

```dockerfile
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1

# Stage 1: Build the Rust binary
FROM rust:1.77-slim as builder

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y     pkg-config     libssl-dev     && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

WORKDIR /app

# Copy manifests first (for dependency caching)
COPY Cargo.toml Cargo.lock ./
RUN mkdir src && echo "fn main() {}" > src/main.rs
RUN cargo build --release
RUN rm -rf src

# Copy real source and build
COPY src ./src
RUN cargo build --release

# Stage 2: Create the slim runtime image
FROM debian:bookworm-slim

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y     ca-certificates     libssl3     && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create a non-root user
RUN useradd --create-home --shell /bin/bash fichub

WORKDIR /home/fichub

# Copy the binary
COPY --from=builder /app/target/release/fichub-rs ./fichub-rs

# Copy migrations
COPY migrations ./migrations

# Copy frontend build
COPY frontend/build ./frontend/build

# Copy .env template
COPY .env.example .env

# Set ownership
RUN chown -R fichub:fichub /home/fichub

USER fichub

EXPOSE 3000

CMD ["./fichub-rs"]
```

**Why multi-stage?** The builder stage installs Rust and all build dependencies (about 2GB). The runtime stage only includes the binary and its runtime dependencies (about 100MB). This makes the final image much smaller.

# Chapter 29: Cross-Compilation and Orange Pi Deploy

## Cross-Compiling for ARM64

FicHub runs on an Orange Pi (ARM64 architecture). Cross-compilation lets you build the binary on your x86 development machine:

```bash
# Add the ARM64 target
rustup target add aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu

# Install the cross-compiler
sudo apt-get install gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu

# Create a cargo config for cross-compilation
mkdir -p .cargo
cat > .cargo/config.toml << 'EOF'
[target.aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu]
linker = "aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc"
EOF

# Build for ARM64
cargo build --release --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
```

The resulting binary is at `target/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/release/fichub-rs`.

## Deploy Script

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# deploy.sh — Cross-compile and ship to the Pi

set -e

PI_HOST="192.168.1.100"
PI_USER="fichub"
PI_DIR="/home/fichub"

echo "Building for ARM64..."
cargo build --release --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu

echo "Copying binary..."
scp target/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/release/fichub-rs     ${PI_USER}@${PI_HOST}:${PI_DIR}/fichub-rs.new

echo "Copying frontend..."
rsync -avz frontend/build/ ${PI_USER}@${PI_HOST}:${PI_DIR}/frontend/build/

echo "Restarting service..."
ssh ${PI_USER}@${PI_HOST} << 'EOF'
    cd /home/fichub
    systemctl stop fichub
    mv fichub-rs.new fichub-rs
    chmod +x fichub-rs
    systemctl start fichub
    echo "Deployment complete!"
EOF
```

# Chapter 30: Securing Your Full-Stack Application

## Security Threats for Web Applications

Before implementing security measures, understand what you're protecting against:

1. **SQL Injection** — Attackers inject malicious SQL through input fields
2. **Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)** — Attackers inject malicious JavaScript
3. **Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)** — Attackers trick users into making unwanted requests
4. **Rate Limiting Abuse** — Attackers overwhelm your server with requests
5. **Data Exposure** — Sensitive data leaked through error messages or API responses
6. **Dependency Vulnerabilities** — Known security flaws in your dependencies

## SQL Injection Prevention

FicHub prevents SQL injection through parameterized queries:

```rust
// SAFE — parameterized query
sqlx::query("SELECT * FROM fic_info WHERE url_id = $1")
    .bind(url_id)
    .fetch_one(pool)
    .await?;

// DANGEROUS — never do this!
let query = format!("SELECT * FROM fic_info WHERE url_id = '{}'", url_id);
sqlx::query(&query).fetch_one(pool).await?;
```

SQLx automatically escapes parameters, so even if `url_id` contains SQL metacharacters (`'; DROP TABLE fic_info; --`), they're treated as literal strings, not SQL commands.

## Input Validation

Validate all user input before processing:

```rust
fn validate_url(url: &str) -> Result<String, AppError> {
    // Must start with http:// or https://
    if !url.starts_with("http://") && !url.starts_with("https://") {
        return Err(AppError::BadRequest(-5, "URL must start with http:// or https://".into()));
    }

    // Must be a valid URL
    let parsed = url::Url::parse(url)
        .map_err(|_| AppError::BadRequest(-5, "Invalid URL format".into()))?;

    // Must be from a supported domain
    let host = parsed.host_str()
        .ok_or_else(|| AppError::BadRequest(-5, "URL must have a host".into()))?;

    let supported = [
        "archiveofourown.org",
        "fanfiction.net",
        "fictionpress.com",
        "forums.spacebattles.com",
        "forums.sufficientvelocity.com",
    ];

    if !supported.iter().any(|&domain| host.ends_with(domain)) {
        return Err(AppError::BadRequest(-5, "Unsupported site".into()));
    }

    // Reasonable length limit
    if url.len() > 2000 {
        return Err(AppError::BadRequest(-5, "URL too long".into()));
    }

    Ok(url.to_string())
}
```

## CORS Configuration

Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) controls which domains can access your API:

```rust
// Development: allow everything
CorsLayer::permissive()

// Production: restrict to your domain
CorsLayer::new()
    .allow_origin("https://fichub.example.com".parse().unwrap())
    .allow_methods([Method::GET, Method::POST])
    .allow_headers(Any)
    .max_age(Duration::from_secs(3600))
```

## Rate Limiting as Security

Rate limiting prevents abuse:

```rust
// Global rate limit: 100 requests per minute per IP
let global_limit = RateLimitConfig {
    capacity: 100,
    refill_rate: 1.67, // 100/60 = 1.67 tokens per second
};

// Export rate limit: 10 exports per minute per IP
let export_limit = RateLimitConfig {
    capacity: 10,
    refill_rate: 0.17, // 10/60 = 0.17 tokens per second
};

// Search rate limit: 30 searches per minute per IP
let search_limit = RateLimitConfig {
    capacity: 30,
    refill_rate: 0.5, // 30/60 = 0.5 tokens per second
};
```

## Secrets Management

Never hardcode secrets in your code:

```rust
// BAD — secrets in source code
const DATABASE_URL: &str = "postgres://fichub:password123@localhost/fichub";

// GOOD — secrets from environment variables
let database_url = std::env::var("DATABASE_URL")
    .expect("DATABASE_URL must be set");
```

Use a `.env` file for development (add it to `.gitignore`) and environment variables for production.

## Security Headers

Add security headers to your responses:

```rust
async fn security_headers_middleware(
    request: Request,
    next: Next,
) -> impl IntoResponse {
    let mut response = next.run(request).await;

    let headers = response.headers_mut();
    headers.insert("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff".parse().unwrap());
    headers.insert("X-Frame-Options", "DENY".parse().unwrap());
    headers.insert("X-XSS-Protection", "1; mode=block".parse().unwrap());
    headers.insert(
        "Strict-Transport-Security",
        "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains".parse().unwrap(),
    );
    headers.insert(
        "Content-Security-Policy",
        "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'".parse().unwrap(),
    );

    response
}
```

## Dependency Auditing

Regularly check for vulnerabilities in your dependencies:

```bash
# Check Rust dependencies
cargo audit

# Check Node.js dependencies
npm audit

# Fix vulnerabilities
cargo audit fix
npm audit fix
```

## Security Checklist

- [ ] All database queries use parameterized queries
- [ ] User input is validated before processing
- [ ] CORS is configured correctly for production
- [ ] Rate limiting is enabled on all endpoints
- [ ] Secrets are stored in environment variables, not code
- [ ] Security headers are set on all responses
- [ ] HTTPS is enforced in production
- [ ] Dependencies are audited regularly
- [ ] Error messages don't leak internal details
- [ ] Database backups are encrypted

# Chapter 31: SvelteKit Fundamentals and SPA Mode

## How SvelteKit Routing Works

SvelteKit uses file-based routing. The file system IS the router:

```
src/routes/
├── +page.svelte              → /
├── +layout.svelte            → Layout for all pages
├── search/
│   ├── +page.svelte          → /search
│   ├── +page.ts              → Data loader for /search
│   └── syntax/
│       └── +page.svelte      → /search/syntax
├── [...slug]/
│   └── +page.ts              → Catch-all route
```

**Key files:**
- `+page.svelte` — The page component (what the user sees)
- `+layout.svelte` — Shared layout wrapper (header, nav, footer)
- `+page.ts` or `+page.server.ts` — Data loading functions
- `+error.svelte` — Error page for this route

## SPA Mode

FicHub runs in SPA (Single Page Application) mode. The entire app is loaded once, and navigation happens client-side:

```typescript
// src/routes/+layout.ts
export const ssr = false;  // Disable server-side rendering
export const prerender = false;  // Don't pre-render pages
```

**Why SPA mode?**
- The frontend is a static site (no server needed for rendering)
- Navigation is instant (no page reloads)
- The backend only serves the API, not HTML templates
- Simpler deployment (just serve static files)

## The API Client

```typescript
// src/lib/api/client.ts

import type { ExportResult, FicMeta, SearchResult, Recommendation, Suggestion } from './types';

const API_BASE = '/api/v0';

async function request<T>(path: string, options?: RequestInit): Promise<T> {
  const response = await fetch(`${API_BASE}${path}`, {
    ...options,
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      ...options?.headers,
    },
  });
  
  if (!response.ok) {
    const error = await response.json().catch(() => ({ msg: 'Network error' }));
    throw new Error(error.msg || `HTTP ${response.status}`);
  }
  
  return response.json();
}

export async function fetchExport(url: string): Promise<ExportResult> {
  return request<ExportResult>(`/export?url=${encodeURIComponent(url)}`);
}

export async function fetchMeta(url: string): Promise<ExportResult> {
  return request<ExportResult>(`/meta?url=${encodeURIComponent(url)}`);
}

export async function searchFics(params: URLSearchParams): Promise<SearchResult> {
  return request<SearchResult>(`/search?${params.toString()}`);
}

export async function fetchRecommendations(source: string, limit = 20): Promise<Recommendation[]> {
  return request<Recommendation[]>(`/recommendations/${source}?limit=${limit}`);
}

export async function fetchSuggestions(): Promise<Suggestion[]> {
  return request<Suggestion[]>('/suggestions');
}

export async function submitSuggestion(url: string, suggestedBy: string): Promise<{ err: number }> {
  return request<{ err: number }>('/suggestions/submit', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ url, suggested_by: suggestedBy }),
  });
}

export async function castVote(urlId: string, vote: boolean, voterIp?: string): Promise<{ err: number; score: number }> {
  return request<{ err: number; score: number }>('/suggestions/vote', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ url_id: urlId, vote, voter_ip: voterIp }),
  });
}
```

## The DownloadTab Component

```svelte
<!-- src/lib/components/DownloadTab.svelte -->
<script lang="ts">
  import { fetchExport } from '$lib/api/client';
  import { detectSite, cacheUrl } from '$lib/util';
  import type { ExportResult, FicMeta } from '$lib/api/types';
  
  let url = $state('');
  let loading = $state(false);
  let result = $state<ExportResult | null>(null);
  let error = $state('');
  let detectedSite = $state('');
  
  async function handleDownload() {
    if (!url.trim()) {
      error = 'Please enter a URL';
      return;
    }
    
    loading = true;
    error = '';
    result = null;
    
    try {
      result = await fetchExport(url);
      if (result.err !== 0) {
        error = result.msg || 'Export failed';
        result = null;
      }
    } catch (err) {
      error = err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Network error';
    } finally {
      loading = false;
    }
  }
  
  function handleInput() {
    detectedSite = detectSite(url);
  }
</script>

<div class="download-tab">
  <h2>Download a Story</h2>
  <p>Paste a URL from a supported fanfiction site</p>
  
  <div class="input-group">
    <input
      type="url"
      bind:value={url}
      oninput={handleInput}
      placeholder="https://archiveofourown.org/works/12345"
      disabled={loading}
    />
    <button onclick={handleDownload} disabled={loading}>
      {loading ? 'Downloading...' : 'Download'}
    </button>
  </div>
  
  {#if detectedSite}
    <p class="site-detected">Detected: {detectedSite}</p>
  {/if}
  
  {#if error}
    <div class="error">{error}</div>
  {/if}
  
  {#if result && result.meta}
    <div class="result">
      <h3>{result.meta.title}</h3>
      <p class="author">by {result.meta.author}</p>
      <div class="meta">
        <span>{result.meta.words.toLocaleString()} words</span>

          <span class="complete">Complete</span>
        {/if}
      </div>
      {#if result.epub_url}
        <a href={cacheUrl(result.epub_url)} class="download-link" download>
          Download EPUB
        </a>
      {/if}
    </div>
  {/if}
</div>
```

# Chapter 34: The Search Syntax Parser

## Custom Search Syntax

FicHub implements a custom search syntax that's more powerful than simple keyword search:

```
# Basic search
harry potter

# Key:value pairs
author:jkr rating:t

# Exclusions
harry potter -crossover

# Ranges
words:50000..100000

# Boolean operators
complete:true sort:score

# Site shortcuts
ao3:harry potter angst
ffnet:harry potter
```

## The Parser

```typescript
// src/lib/search/syntax.ts

export interface SearchToken {
  type: 'key_value' | 'word' | 'exclusion' | 'range' | 'boolean';
  key?: string;
  value: string;
  operator?: 'AND' | 'OR';
}

export function parseSearchSyntax(input: string): SearchToken[] {
  const tokens: SearchToken[] = [];
  const regex = /(\w+):(["']([^"']+)["']|(\S+))|(-)(\w+)|(\w+):(\d+)\.\.(\d+)|(\w+)/g;
  
  let match;
  while ((match = regex.exec(input)) !== null) {
    if (match[1] && match[3]) {
      // Key:"quoted value"
      tokens.push({ type: 'key_value', key: match[1], value: match[3] });
    } else if (match[1] && match[4]) {
      // Key:value
      tokens.push({ type: 'key_value', key: match[1], value: match[4] });
    } else if (match[5] && match[6]) {
      // -exclusion
      tokens.push({ type: 'exclusion', value: match[6] });
    } else if (match[7] && match[8] && match[9]) {
      // key:min..max
      tokens.push({ type: 'range', key: match[7], value: `${match[8]}..${match[9]}` });
    } else if (match[10]) {
      // bare word
      tokens.push({ type: 'word', value: match[10] });
    }
  }
  
  return tokens;
}

export function tokensToQueryParams(tokens: SearchToken[]): URLSearchParams {
  const params = new URLSearchParams();
  const words: string[] = [];
  
  for (const token of tokens) {
    switch (token.type) {
      case 'key_value':
        params.set(token.key!, token.value);
        break;
      case 'exclusion':
        params.append('exclude', token.value);
        break;
      case 'range':
        const [min, max] = token.value.split('..');
        params.set(`${token.key}_min`, min);
        params.set(`${token.key}_max`, max);
        break;
      case 'word':
        words.push(token.value);
        break;
    }
  }
  
  if (words.length > 0) {
    params.set('q', words.join(' '));
  }
  
  return params;
}
```

# Chapter 35: Svelte 5 Deep Dive

## Runes: The New Reactivity System

Svelte 5 introduces **runes** — a new way to handle reactivity that's more explicit and powerful than Svelte 4's reactive declarations.

### $state: Reactive State

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  // Svelte 4 (old way)
  let count = 0;
  
  // Svelte 5 (new way — runes)
  let count = $state(0);
  
  function increment() {
    count += 1; // Automatically triggers re-render
  }
</script>

<p>Count: {count}</p>
<button onclick={increment}>+1</button>
```

**Key differences:**
- `$state()` creates a reactive variable
- Assignment (`count += 1`) triggers re-renders automatically
- No need for `$:` or reactive declarations
- Works in nested objects and arrays

### $derived: Computed Values

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  let items = $state([
    { name: 'Apple', price: 1.50 },
    { name: 'Banana', price: 0.75 },
    { name: 'Cherry', price: 3.00 },
  ]);
  
  // Automatically recalculates when items change
  let total = $derived(
    items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.price, 0)
  );
  
  let average = $derived(total / items.length);
  
  let expensiveItems = $derived(
    items.filter(item => item.price > 2.00)
  );
</script>

<p>Total: ${total.toFixed(2)}</p>
<p>Average: ${average.toFixed(2)}</p>
<p>Expensive items: {expensiveItems.length}</p>
```

**$derived** is like a computed property — it automatically updates when its dependencies change. No manual recalculation needed.

### $effect: Side Effects

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  let query = $state('');
  let results = $state([]);
  let loading = $state(false);
  
  // Runs whenever query changes
  $effect(() => {
    if (query.length < 3) {
      results = [];
      return;
    }
    
    loading = true;
    const controller = new AbortController();
    
    fetch(`/api/v0/search?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}`, {
      signal: controller.signal,
    })
      .then(res => res.json())
      .then(data => {
        results = data.results || [];
        loading = false;
      })
      .catch(() => {
        if (!controller.signal.aborted) {
          loading = false;
        }
      });
    
    // Cleanup: abort fetch if query changes again
    return () => controller.abort();
  });
</script>

<input bind:value={query} placeholder="Search..." />

{#if loading}
  <p>Searching...</p>
{:else}
  <ul>
    {#each results as result}
      <li>{result.title} by {result.author}</li>
    {/each}
  </ul>
{/if}
```

**$effect** runs after the component mounts and whenever its dependencies change. The return function is a cleanup function that runs before the next effect or on unmount.

### $props: Component Properties

```svelte
<!-- Card.svelte -->
<script lang="ts">
  let { title, author, words, onComplete }: {
    title: string;
    author: string;
    words: number;
    onComplete?: () => void;
  } = $props();
</script>

<div class="card">
  <h3>{title}</h3>
  <p>by {author}</p>
  <p>{words.toLocaleString()} words</p>
  {#if onComplete}
    <button onclick={onComplete}>Mark Complete</button>
  {/if}
</div>

<!-- Usage in parent -->
<Card
  title="My Story"
  author="SomeAuthor"
  words={50000}
  onComplete={() => console.log('Done!')}
/>
```

### $bindable: Two-Way Binding

```svelte
<!-- Slider.svelte -->
<script lang="ts">
  let { value = $bindable(), min = 0, max = 100 }: {
    value: number;
    min?: number;
    max?: number;
  } = $props();
</script>

<input
  type="range"
  bind:value
  {min}
  {max}
/>
<span>{value}</span>

<!-- Usage -->
<Slider bind:value={price} min={0} max={100} />
```

## Snippets: Reusable Template Fragments

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  // Define a snippet
  function itemCount(count: number) {
    return { count, label: count === 1 ? 'item' : 'items' };
  }
</script>

<!-- Use snippets for reusable templates -->
{#snippet itemCard(title: string, author: string)}
  <div class="item-card">
    <h4>{title}</h4>
    <p>by {author}</p>
  </div>
{/snippet}

{#each items as item}
  {@render itemCard(item.title, item.author)}
{/each}
```

## Svelte 5 vs Svelte 4

| Feature | Svelte 4 | Svelte 5 |
|---------|----------|----------|
| State | `let x = 0` | `let x = $state(0)` |
| Derived | `$: doubled = x * 2` | `let doubled = $derived(x * 2)` |
| Effect | `$: { sideEffect() }` | `$effect(() => { sideEffect() })` |
| Props | `export let prop` | `let { prop } = $props()` |
| Bind | `export let prop` | `let { prop = $bindable() } = $props()` |
| Store | `import { writable } from 'svelte/store'` | `$state` preferred |
| Template | `{#if}...{/if}` | Same |
| Each | `{#each}...{/each}` | Same |
| Await | `{#await}...{/await}` | Same |

# Chapter 36: Component Patterns

## Composition Over Inheritance

Svelte 5 encourages composition — building complex components from simple ones:

```svelte
<!-- TagBadge.svelte -->
<script lang="ts">
  let { name, type, score = 0 }: {
    name: string;
    type: string;
    score?: number;
  } = $props();
  
  let colorClass = $derived(
    type === 'canonical' ? 'canonical' :
    type === 'warning' ? 'warning' :
    type === 'relationship' ? 'relationship' :
    'freeform'
  );
</script>

<span class="tag-badge {colorClass}">
  {name}
  {#if score > 0}
    <span class="score">+{score}</span>
  {/if}
</span>

<style>
  .tag-badge {
    display: inline-block;
    padding: 0.2rem 0.6rem;
    border-radius: 12px;
    font-size: 0.85rem;
    margin: 0.2rem;
  }
  
  .canonical {
    background: #1e40af;
    color: white;
  }
  
  .warning {
    background: #991b1b;
    color: white;
  }
  
  .relationship {
    background: #7c3aed;
    color: white;
  }
  
  .freeform {
    background: #374151;
    color: #d1d5db;
  }
  
  .score {
    font-size: 0.75rem;
    margin-left: 0.3rem;
    opacity: 0.8;
  }
</style>
```

## Context API for Global State

```svelte
<!-- ThemeContext.svelte -->
<script lang="ts">
  import { setContext } from 'svelte';
  
  let theme = $state<'dark' | 'light'>('dark');
  
  function toggleTheme() {
    theme = theme === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark';
  }
  
  setContext('theme', {
    get theme() { return theme; },
    toggleTheme,
  });
</script>

<!-- Child component -->
<script lang="ts">
  import { getContext } from 'svelte';
  
  const { theme, toggleTheme } = getContext('theme');
</script>

<button onclick={toggleTheme}>
  Current theme: {theme}
</button>
```

## Transitions and Animations

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { fade, fly, slide } from 'svelte/transition';
  import { flip } from 'svelte/animate';
  
  let items = $state([
    { id: 1, text: 'First item' },
    { id: 2, text: 'Second item' },
    { id: 3, text: 'Third item' },
  ]);
  
  function removeItem(id: number) {
    items = items.filter(item => item.id !== id);
  }
</script>

{#each items as item (item.id)}
  <div
    class="item"
    transition:fly={{ y: 20, duration: 300 }}
    animate:flip={{ duration: 300 }}
  >
    <span>{item.text}</span>
    <button onclick={() => removeItem(item.id)}>Remove</button>
  </div>
{/each}
```

## Stores for Cross-Component State

```typescript
// src/lib/stores/notifications.ts
import { writable } from 'svelte/store';

interface Notification {
  id: number;
  message: string;
  type: 'success' | 'error' | 'info';
}

function createNotificationStore() {
  const { subscribe, update } = writable<Notification[]>([]);
  let nextId = 0;
  
  return {
    subscribe,
    add(message: string, type: Notification['type'] = 'info') {
      const id = nextId++;
      update(notifications => [
        ...notifications,
        { id, message, type },
      ]);
      
      // Auto-remove after 5 seconds
      setTimeout(() => {
        update(notifications =>
          notifications.filter(n => n.id !== id)
        );
      }, 5000);
    },
    remove(id: number) {
      update(notifications =>
        notifications.filter(n => n.id !== id)
      );
    },
  };
}

export const notifications = createNotificationStore();
```

```svelte
<!-- NotificationToast.svelte -->
<script lang="ts">
  import { notifications } from '$lib/stores/notifications';
  import { fly } from 'svelte/transition';
</script>

<div class="toast-container">
  {#each $notifications as notification (notification.id)}
    <div
      class="toast {notification.type}"
      transition:fly={{ y: -20, duration: 300 }}
    >
      {notification.message}
      <button onclick={() => notifications.remove(notification.id)}>×</button>
    </div>
  {/each}
</div>
```

# Chapter 37: Advanced Search Page

## Building the Search Interface

The search page combines the syntax parser with a comprehensive UI:

```svelte
<!-- src/routes/search/+page.svelte -->
<script lang="ts">
  import { searchFics } from '$lib/api/client';
  import { parseSearchSyntax, tokensToQueryParams } from '$lib/search/syntax';
  import { defaultFilters } from '$lib/search/syntax';
  import type { SearchResult, FicMeta } from '$lib/api/types';
  
  let searchInput = $state('');
  let filters = $state({ ...defaultFilters });
  let results = $state<SearchResult | null>(null);
  let loading = $state(false);
  let currentPage = $state(1);
  let showFilters = $state(false);
  
  async function performSearch(page = 1) {
    loading = true;
    
    try {
      // Parse the search syntax
      const tokens = parseSearchSyntax(searchInput);
      const searchParams = tokensToQueryParams(tokens);
      
      // Add filters
      for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(filters)) {
        if (value !== undefined && value !== '') {
          searchParams.set(key, String(value));
        }
      }
      
      searchParams.set('page', String(page));
      
      results = await searchFics(searchParams);
      currentPage = page;
    } catch (err) {
      console.error('Search failed:', err);
    } finally {
      loading = false;
    }
  }
  
  function handleKeydown(event: KeyboardEvent) {
    if (event.key === 'Enter') {
      performSearch();
    }
  }
</script>

<div class="search-page">
  <h1>Search Stories</h1>
  
  <div class="search-bar">
    <input
      type="text"
      bind:value={searchInput}
      onkeydown={handleKeydown}
      placeholder="Search stories... (try: author:jkr words:50000..100000)"
    />
    <button onclick={() => performSearch()} disabled={loading}>
      {loading ? 'Searching...' : 'Search'}
    </button>
    <button class="filter-toggle" onclick={() => showFilters = !showFilters}>
      Filters {showFilters ? '▲' : '▼'}
    </button>
  </div>
  
  {#if showFilters}
    <div class="filters" transition:slide>
      <div class="filter-group">
        <label>Minimum Words:</label>
        <input type="number" bind:value={filters.min_words} min="0" step="1000" />
      </div>
      <div class="filter-group">
        <label>Maximum Words:</label>
        <input type="number" bind:value={filters.max_words} min="0" step="1000" />
      </div>
      <div class="filter-group">
        <label>Complete Only:</label>
        <input type="checkbox" bind:checked={filters.complete} />
      </div>
      <div class="filter-group">
        <label>Sort By:</label>
        <select bind:value={filters.sort}>
          <option value="relevance">Relevance</option>
          <option value="words">Words</option>
          <option value="chapters">Chapters</option>
          <option value="score">Score</option>
        </select>
      </div>
    </div>
  {/if}
  
  {#if results}
    <div class="results">
      <p class="result-count">{results.total} results found</p>
      
      {#each results.results as fic}
        <div class="result-card">
          <h3>{fic.title}</h3>
          <p class="author">by {fic.author}</p>
          <div class="meta">
            <span>{fic.words.toLocaleString()} words</span>
            <span>{fic.chapters} chapters</span>
            {#if fic.complete}
              <span class="complete">Complete</span>
            {/if}
          </div>
          <div class="tags">
            {#each fic.tags.slice(0, 5) as tag}
              <span class="tag">{tag.name}</span>
            {/each}
          </div>
        </div>
      {/each}
      
      {#if results.total > 20}
        <div class="pagination">
          <button
            onclick={() => performSearch(currentPage - 1)}
            disabled={currentPage === 1}
          >
            Previous
          </button>
          <span>Page {currentPage} of {Math.ceil(results.total / 20)}</span>
          <button
            onclick={() => performSearch(currentPage + 1)}
            disabled={currentPage * 20 >= results.total}
          >
            Next
          </button>
        </div>
      {/if}
    </div>
  {/if}
</div>
```

# Chapter 38: Building Accessible Web Interfaces

## Why Accessibility Matters

Accessibility (a11y) ensures that your web application can be used by everyone, including people with disabilities. This includes:

- **Visual impairments** — Screen readers, high contrast, zoom
- **Motor impairments** — Keyboard navigation, voice control
- **Cognitive impairments** — Clear language, consistent layout
- **Temporary impairments** — Broken arm, bright sunlight

## Semantic HTML

The foundation of accessibility is semantic HTML — using the right elements for the right purpose:

```svelte
<!-- BAD: Div soup (inaccessible) -->
<div class="nav">
  <div class="nav-item" onclick={goHome}>Home</div>
  <div class="nav-item" onclick={goSearch}>Search</div>
</div>

<!-- GOOD: Semantic HTML (accessible) -->
<nav aria-label="Main navigation">
  <ul>
    <li><a href="/">Home</a></li>
    <li><a href="/search">Search</a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>
```

## ARIA Attributes

When semantic HTML isn't enough, ARIA attributes provide additional context:

```svelte
<!-- Live region for dynamic updates -->
<div aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true">
  {#if loading}
    <span>Searching...</span>
  {:else if results}
    <span>{results.total} results found</span>
  {/if}
</div>

<!-- Descriptive labels -->
<input
  type="search"
  aria-label="Search stories"
  placeholder="Enter search terms..."
/>

<!-- State announcements -->
<button
  aria-expanded={showFilters}
  aria-controls="filter-panel"
  onclick={() => showFilters = !showFilters}
>
  Filters
</button>

{#if showFilters}
  <div id="filter-panel" role="region" aria-label="Search filters">
    <!-- Filter controls -->
  </div>
{/if}
```

## Keyboard Navigation

Every interactive element must be keyboard-accessible:

```svelte
<!-- Tab component with keyboard support -->
<script lang="ts">
  let activeTab = $state(0);
  let tabs = ['Download', 'Recommendations', 'Suggestions'];
  
  function handleKeydown(event: KeyboardEvent, index: number) {
    switch (event.key) {
      case 'ArrowLeft':
        event.preventDefault();
        activeTab = Math.max(0, index - 1);
        break;
      case 'ArrowRight':
        event.preventDefault();
        activeTab = Math.min(tabs.length - 1, index + 1);
        break;
      case 'Home':
        event.preventDefault();
        activeTab = 0;
        break;
      case 'End':
        event.preventDefault();
        activeTab = tabs.length - 1;
        break;
    }
  }
</script>

<div role="tablist" aria-label="Content tabs">
  {#each tabs as tab, index}
    <button
      role="tab"
      aria-selected={activeTab === index}
      aria-controls="tabpanel-{index}"
      id="tab-{index}"
      tabindex={activeTab === index ? 0 : -1}
      onclick={() => activeTab = index}
      onkeydown={(e) => handleKeydown(e, index)}
    >
      {tab}
    </button>
  {/each}
</div>

{#each tabs as tab, index}
  {#if activeTab === index}
    <div
      role="tabpanel"
      id="tabpanel-{index}"
      aria-labelledby="tab-{index}"
      tabindex="0"
    >
      <!-- Tab content -->
    </div>
  {/if}
{/each}
```

## Color and Contrast

Ensure sufficient color contrast (WCAG 2.1 requires 4.5:1 for normal text):

```css
/* Accessible color palette */
:root {
  /* Text colors */
  --text-primary: #1a1a2e;    /* High contrast on light bg */
  --text-secondary: #4a5568;  /* Good contrast, slightly lighter */
  --text-on-dark: #f7fafc;    /* High contrast on dark bg */
  
  /* Background colors */
  --bg-primary: #ffffff;
  --bg-secondary: #f7fafc;
  --bg-dark: #1a1a2e;
  
  /* Status colors (always pair with icons, not just color) */
  --success: #059669;  /* Green — also use checkmark icon */
  --error: #dc2626;    /* Red — also use X icon */
  --warning: #d97706;  /* Amber — also use warning icon */
}

/* Focus indicators */
:focus-visible {
  outline: 3px solid #2563eb;
  outline-offset: 2px;
}

/* Skip to main content link */
.skip-link {
  position: absolute;
  top: -40px;
  left: 0;
  background: #2563eb;
  color: white;
  padding: 8px;
  z-index: 100;
}

.skip-link:focus {
  top: 0;
}
```

# Chapter 39: Backend Testing (cargo test)

## Why Testing Matters

Testing is the difference between "it works on my machine" and "it works in production." Every test you write is a promise: "I will never have to debug this particular bug twice."

FicHub uses Rust's built-in test framework, which is fast, expressive, and zero-cost (tests are compiled separately and don't affect the release binary).

## The Three Assertion Macros

```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    #[test]
    fn test_assertions() {
        // assert! — boolean check
        assert!(1 + 1 == 2);
        assert!(true, "This should always pass");

        // assert_eq! — equality check (shows both values on failure)
        assert_eq!(2 + 2, 4);
        assert_eq!("hello".to_uppercase(), "HELLO");

        // assert_ne! — inequality check
        assert_ne!(1, 2);
        assert_ne!("hello", "world");
    }
}
```

**When to use each:**
- `assert!` — When you just need a boolean condition
- `assert_eq!` — When comparing two values (preferred for most cases — better error messages)
- `assert_ne!` — When verifying two values are different

## Testing the Slug Generator

```rust
#[test]
fn test_slug_generation() {
    // Normal cases
    assert_eq!(slugify("Hello World"), "hello-world");
    assert_eq!(slugify("My Story Title"), "my-story-title");

    // Special characters
    assert_eq!(slugify("Story: A Beginning!"), "story-a-beginning");
    assert_eq!(slugify("What's Up?"), "whats-up");

    // Multiple spaces
    assert_eq!(slugify("Too   Many   Spaces"), "too-many-spaces");

    // Leading/trailing spaces
    assert_eq!(slugify("  Trim me  "), "trim-me");

    // Unicode
    assert_eq!(slugify("Ünïcödé"), "unicode");
    assert_eq!(slugify("日本語"), "日-本-語");

    // Empty string
    assert_eq!(slugify(""), "");

    // Numbers
    assert_eq!(slugify("Chapter 1"), "chapter-1");
    assert_eq!(slugify("100% Complete"), "100-complete");
}
```

**Testing edge cases:** A good test suite covers:
- Normal cases (things that work as expected)
- Edge cases (empty strings, very long strings, special characters)
- Error cases (invalid input, missing data)
- Boundary conditions (minimum/maximum values)

## Testing Error Handling

```rust
#[test]
fn test_error_responses() {
    // Test that errors produce the right HTTP status codes
    let error = AppError::BadRequest(-1, "no query".into());
    let response = error.into_response();
    assert_eq!(response.status(), StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST);

    let error = AppError::NotFound("story not found".into());
    let response = error.into_response();
    assert_eq!(response.status(), StatusCode::NOT_FOUND);

    let error = AppError::RateLimited(60);
    let response = error.into_response();
    assert_eq!(response.status(), StatusCode::TOO_MANY_REQUESTS);
}
```

## Integration Tests

Integration tests test the entire system working together:

```rust
// tests/api_tests.rs
use sqlx::PgPool;

#[sqlx::test]
async fn test_export_flow(pool: PgPool) {
    // Run migrations
    sqlx::migrate!("./migrations")
        .run(&pool)
        .await
        .expect("Failed to run migrations");

    // Create test state
    let state = create_test_state(pool).await;

    // Test the export handler
    let response = axum::Router::new()
        .route("/api/v0/export", get(export_handler))
        .with_state(state)
        .oneshot(
            axum::http::Request::builder()
                .uri("/api/v0/export?url=https://archiveofourown.org/works/12345")
                .body(axum::body::Body::empty())
                .unwrap(),
        )
        .await
        .unwrap();

    assert_eq!(response.status(), 200);

    let body = axum::body::to_bytes(response.into_body(), usize::MAX)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let json: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&body).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(json["err"], 0);
}
```

## Running Tests

```bash
# Run all unit tests (fast, no database needed)
cargo test

# Run only integration tests
cargo test --test api_tests

# Run tests with database
cargo test -- --ignored

# Run a specific test
cargo test test_slug_generation

# Run tests in a specific module
cargo test db::tests

# Show println! output
cargo test -- --nocapture

# Run tests in parallel (default)
cargo test -- --test-threads=4
```

```typescript
// src/lib/api/client.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect, vi, beforeEach } from 'vitest';
import { fetchExport, searchFics } from './client';

describe('API Client', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.restoreAllMocks();
  });

  describe('fetchExport', () => {
    it('should return export result on success', async () => {
      const mockResponse = {
        err: 0,
        url_id: 'ao3-12345',
        epub_url: '/cache/epub/ao3-12345.epub',
        meta: {
          title: 'Test Story',
          author: 'TestAuthor',
          words: 50000,
          chapters: 10,
        },
      };

      vi.spyOn(global, 'fetch').mockResolvedValue({
        ok: true,
        json: () => Promise.resolve(mockResponse),
      } as Response);

      const result = await fetchExport('https://archiveofourown.org/works/12345');

      expect(result.err).toBe(0);
      expect(result.url_id).toBe('ao3-12345');
      expect(result.meta?.title).toBe('Test Story');
    });

    it('should throw on network error', async () => {
      vi.spyOn(global, 'fetch').mockRejectedValue(
        new Error('Network error')
      );

      await expect(
        fetchExport('https://archiveofourown.org/works/12345')
      ).rejects.toThrow('Network error');
    });
  });

  describe('searchFics', () => {
    it('should build correct query parameters', async () => {
      const mockResponse = {
        total: 100,
        page: 1,
        per_page: 20,
        results: [],
      };

      vi.spyOn(global, 'fetch').mockImplementation(async (url) => {
        expect(url).toContain('q=harry+potter');
        expect(url).toContain('min_words=50000');
        return {
          ok: true,
          json: () => Promise.resolve(mockResponse),
        } as Response;
      });

      const params = new URLSearchParams({
        q: 'harry potter',
        min_words: '50000',
      });

      await searchFics(params);
    });
  });
});
```

## Testing the Search Syntax Parser

```typescript
// src/lib/search/syntax.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { parseSearchSyntax, tokensToQueryParams } from './syntax';

describe('Search Syntax Parser', () => {
  it('should parse bare words', () => {
    const tokens = parseSearchSyntax('harry potter');
    expect(tokens).toEqual([
      { type: 'word', value: 'harry' },
      { type: 'word', value: 'potter' },
    ]);
  });

  it('should parse key:value pairs', () => {
    const tokens = parseSearchSyntax('author:jkr rating:t');
    expect(tokens).toEqual([
      { type: 'key_value', key: 'author', value: 'jkr' },
      { type: 'key_value', key: 'rating', value: 't' },
    ]);
  });

  it('should parse exclusions', () => {
    const tokens = parseSearchSyntax('harry potter -crossover');
    expect(tokens).toEqual([
      { type: 'word', value: 'harry' },
      { type: 'word', value: 'potter' },
      { type: 'exclusion', value: 'crossover' },
    ]);
  });

  it('should parse ranges', () => {
    const tokens = parseSearchSyntax('words:50000..100000');
    expect(tokens).toEqual([
      { type: 'range', key: 'words', value: '50000..100000' },
    ]);
  });

  it('should parse complex queries', () => {
    const tokens = parseSearchSyntax('author:"JK Rowling" words:10000..50000 complete:true -crossover');
    expect(tokens.length).toBe(4);
    expect(tokens[0]).toEqual({ type: 'key_value', key: 'author', value: 'JK Rowling' });
  });

  it('should convert tokens to URL params', () => {
    const tokens = parseSearchSyntax('harry potter author:jkr');
    const params = tokensToQueryParams(tokens);
    expect(params.get('q')).toBe('harry potter');
    expect(params.get('author')).toBe('jkr');
  });
});
```

# Chapter 41: Full-Stack Integration

## End-to-End Testing

The ultimate test is running the entire stack and verifying it works:

```bash
# Start the server
cargo run &

# Wait for it to be ready
sleep 5

# Test 1: Health check
curl -s http://localhost:3000/api/v0/remote | jq .
# Expected: {"name":"fichub-rs API","version":"0.1.0",...}

# Test 2: Export a fic from AO3
curl -s "http://localhost:3000/api/v0/export?url=https://archiveofourown.org/works/12345" | jq .
# Expected: {"err":0,"url_id":"ao3-12345","epub_url":"/cache/epub/ao3-12345.epub",...}

# Test 3: Search for fics
curl -s "http://localhost:3000/api/v0/search?q=harry+potter" | jq .
# Expected: {"total":N,"page":1,"results":[...]}

# Test 4: List tags
curl -s http://localhost:3000/api/v0/tags | jq .
# Expected: {"err":0,"tags":[...]}

# Test 5: Submit a tag
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/v0/tags/submit   -H "Content-Type: application/json"   -d '{"name":"test tag","url_id":"ao3-12345"}' | jq .

# Test 6: Error handling — no query
curl -s "http://localhost:3000/api/v0/export" | jq .
# Expected: {"err":-1,"msg":"no query"}

# Test 7: Error handling — invalid URL
curl -s "http://localhost:3000/api/v0/export?url=not-a-url" | jq .
# Expected: {"err":-5,"msg":"unsupported URL"}
```

## The Request Flow

Here's the complete flow for a download request:

```
1. User pastes URL in browser
2. SvelteKit calls fetchExport(url)
3. Browser sends GET /api/v0/export?url=...
4. Axum matches route to export_handler
5. Handler validates URL
6. Handler checks blacklist
7. Handler checks rate limit (Redis)
8. Handler checks database cache
9. If cached → return cached path
10. Handler finds scraper in registry
11. Scraper.fetches metadata from site
12. Handler stores metadata in database
13. Scraper fetches chapters
14. Export engine generates EPUB
15. EPUB saved to disk cache
16. Export logged in database
17. Handler returns JSON response
18. Browser shows download button
19. User clicks download
20. Browser fetches /cache/epub/xxx.epub
21. File downloads to user's device
```

That's 21 steps from paste to download. Most of them happen in under 10 seconds.

# The Last 500 Words

Testing is not a chore — it's a gift you give your future self. Every test you write is a promise: "I will never have to debug this particular bug twice." Every passing test is a green light that says, "This part of the system works, and I can build on top of it with confidence."

When you first started this book, the idea of building a full-stack web application from scratch might have felt overwhelming. Database migrations, HTTP servers, web scraping, EPUB generation, SvelteKit frontends, integration tests — each piece is complex on its own. But here's what you discovered along the way: each piece is also *simple* when you take it one step at a time.

The slug generator is just string manipulation. The EPUB generator is just HTML wrapped in XML. The API is just a function that takes a request and returns a response. The frontend is just a form that calls an API and displays the result. The tests are just functions that call other functions and check the answers.

Complexity is just simplicity, stacked.

You've also learned something that no tutorial can teach: **the taste of a real project**. Real projects have weird edge cases. Real projects have to handle errors gracefully. Real projects need caching strategies and database optimizations and deployment pipelines. Real projects need tests — lots of them — because real users will find every bug you leave behind.

You've tasted that reality. You've dealt with the Unicode slug edge case. You've debugged why the EPUB metadata was missing the author. You've figured out why the Svelte component wasn't re-rendering after the API call. You've written 28 tests for a search syntax parser because every combination of keywords could break in a different way.

And you fixed all of it. You pushed through, iterated, and shipped a working application.

That's the real skill. Not knowing every framework or memorizing every API. The real skill is knowing that when something breaks, you can figure it out. You can read the error message, trace the code path, write a test to reproduce the bug, fix it, and verify the fix. That loop — break, diagnose, fix, verify — is the core of software engineering.

You now own that loop. Use it well.

The fanfiction community has a saying: "Don't like, don't read." The software community has a similar energy: "Don't like, don't use — or build something better." You chose the second option. You looked at existing tools, saw room for improvement, and built your own.

That's what developers do. Not just consume technology, but *create* it. You have the skills to build web applications, the testing discipline to ensure they work, and the deployment knowledge to put them in the world.

So here's your final assignment: **ship something**. Not a tutorial project, not a copy of someone else's app — something that matters to you. Something you'd use every day. Something that solves a problem you care about.

You have every tool you need. The rest is just building.

Happy coding. 🚀

# Appendix A: Rust Quick Reference

## Ownership and Borrowing

```rust
// Ownership: each value has exactly one owner
let s1 = String::from("hello");
let s2 = s1;  // s1 is moved to s2
// println!("{}", s1);  // ERROR: s1 is no longer valid

// Borrowing: create references without taking ownership
let s1 = String::from("hello");
let len = calculate_length(&s1);  // Borrow s1
println!("{} has length {}", s1, len);  // OK: s1 is still valid

fn calculate_length(s: &String) -> usize {
    s.len()
}

// Mutable borrowing
let mut s = String::from("hello");
change(&mut s);
println!("{}", s);  // "hello, world"

fn change(s: &mut String) {
    s.push_str(", world");
}
```

**Rules:**
1. You can have either one mutable reference OR any number of immutable references
2. References must always be valid (no dangling references)

## Pattern Matching

```rust
// Match expressions
match value {
    1 => "one",
    2 | 3 => "two or three",
    4..=10 => "four to ten",
    _ => "something else",
}

// Destructuring
let Point { x, y } = point;
let (first, second) = tuple;

// Guards
match value {
    n if n < 0 => "negative",
    n if n == 0 => "zero",
    n => "positive",
}

// if let (shorthand for single-case match)
if let Some(value) = option {
    println!("Got: {}", value);
}
```

## Error Handling

```rust
// Result type
fn divide(a: f64, b: f64) -> Result<f64, String> {
    if b == 0.0 {
        Err("Division by zero".to_string())
    } else {
        Ok(a / b)
    }
}

// The ? operator
fn read_file(path: &str) -> Result<String, io::Error> {
    let content = fs::read_to_string(path)?;  // Propagates error
    Ok(content)
}

// Custom error types
#[derive(Debug)]
enum AppError {
    Io(io::Error),
    Parse(ParseIntError),
    NotFound,
}

impl From<io::Error> for AppError {
    fn from(e: io::Error) -> Self {
        AppError::Io(e)
    }
}
```

## Iterators

```rust
// Common iterator methods
let numbers = vec![1, 2, 3, 4, 5];

// Map: transform each element
let doubled: Vec<i32> = numbers.iter().map(|x| x * 2).collect();

// Filter: keep elements matching a condition
let evens: Vec<&i32> = numbers.iter().filter(|x| x % 2 == 0).collect();

// Fold: reduce to a single value
let sum: i32 = numbers.iter().fold(0, |acc, x| acc + x);

// Chain: combine iterators
let a = vec![1, 2];
let b = vec![3, 4];
let combined: Vec<&i32> = a.iter().chain(b.iter()).collect();

// Enumerate: get index with each element
for (i, value) in numbers.iter().enumerate() {
    println!("{}: {}", i, value);
}
```

## Concurrency

```rust
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::thread;

// Shared state with Arc<Mutex<>>
let counter = Arc::new(Mutex::new(0));
let mut handles = vec![];

for _ in 0..10 {
    let counter = Arc::clone(&counter);
    let handle = thread::spawn(move || {
        let mut num = counter.lock().unwrap();
        *num += 1;
    });
    handles.push(handle);
}

for handle in handles {
    handle.join().unwrap();
}

println!("Result: {}", *counter.lock().unwrap());  // 10

// Tokio async concurrency
let (result1, result2) = tokio::join!(
    async_operation_1(),
    async_operation_2(),
);
```

# Appendix B: Svelte/SvelteKit Quick Reference

## Svelte 5 Runes

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  // Reactive state
  let count = $state(0);
  
  // Derived state
  let doubled = $derived(count * 2);
  
  // Effects
  $effect(() => {
    console.log('Count changed:', count);
    return () => console.log('Cleanup');
  });
  
  // Props
  let { title, count: initialCount = 0 } = $props();
  
  // Two-way binding
  let { value = $bindable() } = $props();
</script>
```

## SvelteKit Routing

```
src/routes/
├── +page.svelte              → /
├── +layout.svelte            → Layout wrapper
├── +layout.ts                → Layout data loader
├── +error.svelte             → Error page
├── about/
│   └── +page.svelte          → /about
├── blog/
│   ├── +page.svelte          → /blog
│   ├── +page.ts              → /blog data loader
│   └── [slug]/
│       ├── +page.svelte      → /blog/:slug
│       └── +page.ts          → /blog/:slug data loader
└── [...catchall]/
    └── +page.svelte          → Catch-all route
```

## Stores

```typescript
// Writable store
import { writable } from 'svelte/store';
const count = writable(0);
count.set(5);
count.update(n => n + 1);

// Derived store
import { derived } from 'svelte/store';
const doubled = derived(count, $count => $count * 2);

// Read-only store
import { readable } from 'svelte/store';
const time = readable(new Date(), function start(set) {
  const interval = setInterval(() => set(new Date()), 1000);
  return function stop() { clearInterval(interval); };
});
```

## Actions

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  function clickOutside(node: HTMLElement, callback: () => void) {
    const handleClick = (event: MouseEvent) => {
      if (!node.contains(event.target as Node)) {
        callback();
      }
    };
    
    document.addEventListener('click', handleClick, true);
    
    return {
      destroy() {
        document.removeEventListener('click', handleClick, true);
      }
    };
  }
</script>

<div use:clickOutside={() => console.log('Clicked outside')}>
  Click outside me
</div>
```

# Appendix C: PostgreSQL Cheat Sheet

## Common Queries

```sql
-- Select with conditions
SELECT * FROM fic_info
WHERE words > 50000
  AND complete = true
ORDER BY updated_at DESC
LIMIT 20 OFFSET 0;

-- Full-text search
SELECT * FROM fic_info
WHERE to_tsvector('english', title || ' ' || author)
  @@ plainto_tsquery('english', 'harry potter');

-- Aggregation
SELECT source, COUNT(*), AVG(words)
FROM fic_info
GROUP BY source
ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC;

-- Join
SELECT f.title, f.author, COUNT(e.id) as export_count
FROM fic_info f
LEFT JOIN export_log e ON f.url_id = e.url_id
GROUP BY f.url_id
ORDER BY export_count DESC;

-- JSONB queries
SELECT * FROM fic_info
WHERE tags @> '["harry potter"]'::jsonb;

-- Upsert
INSERT INTO fic_info (url_id, title, author)
VALUES ('ao3-123', 'Test', 'Author')
ON CONFLICT (url_id) DO UPDATE SET
  title = EXCLUDED.title,
  updated_at = NOW();

-- CTE (Common Table Expression)
WITH popular AS (
  SELECT url_id, COUNT(*) as downloads
  FROM export_log
  GROUP BY url_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) > 10
)
SELECT f.title, f.author, p.downloads
FROM fic_info f
JOIN popular p ON f.url_id = p.url_id
ORDER BY p.downloads DESC;
```

## Indexes

```sql
-- B-tree index (default, good for equality and range)
CREATE INDEX idx_fic_title ON fic_info(title);

-- GIN index (good for full-text search and JSONB)
CREATE INDEX idx_fic_tags ON fic_info USING gin(tags);
CREATE INDEX idx_fic_title_fts ON fic_info
  USING gin(to_tsvector('english', title));

-- Partial index (only index rows matching a condition)
CREATE INDEX idx_fic_complete ON fic_info(url_id)
  WHERE complete = true;

-- Composite index (multiple columns)
CREATE INDEX idx_export_url_type ON export_log(url_id, export_type);

-- Unique index
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_tag_alias ON tag_aliases(alias);
```

## Administration

```sql
-- List databases
\l

-- Connect to database
\c database_name

-- List tables
\dt

-- Describe table
\d table_name

-- List indexes
\di

-- Show query plan
EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT ...;

-- Vacuum (reclaim space)
VACUUM ANALYZE;

-- Backup
pg_dump -U fichub fichub > backup.sql

-- Restore
psql -U fichub fichub < backup.sql
```

# Appendix E: API Reference

## Export API

### GET /api/v0/export

Export a fanfiction story as EPUB.

**Parameters:**
| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| url | string | Yes | URL of the story |

**Response:**
```json
{
  "err": 0,
  "url_id": "ao3-12345",
  "epub_url": "/cache/epub/ao3-12345.epub",
  "meta": {
    "title": "Story Title",
    "author": "Author Name",
    "words": 50000,
    "chapters": 10
  }
}
```

**Error codes:**
| Code | Message | HTTP Status |
|------|---------|-------------|
| -1 | no query | 400 |
| -5 | unsupported URL | 400 |
| -429 | rate limited | 429 |

### GET /api/v0/meta

Get story metadata without generating EPUB.

**Parameters:** Same as `/export`

**Response:** Same structure as `/export` but without `epub_url`

## Search API

### GET /api/v0/search

Search for fanfiction stories.

**Parameters:**
| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| q | string | Yes | Search query |
| page | int | No | Page number (default: 1) |
| per_page | int | No | Results per page (default: 20) |
| min_words | int | No | Minimum word count |
| max_words | int | No | Maximum word count |
| complete | bool | No | Only complete stories |
| sort | string | No | Sort by: relevance, words, score |
| source | string | No | Filter by source: ao3, ffnet |
| tags | string | No | Comma-separated tag names |

**Response:**
```json
{
  "total": 142,
  "page": 1,
  "per_page": 20,
  "results": [
    {
      "url_id": "ao3-12345",
      "title": "Story Title",
      "author": "Author Name",
      "words": 50000,
      "chapters": 10,
      "complete": true,
      "source": "ao3",
      "tags": ["harry potter", "romance"]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Tags API

### GET /api/v0/tags

List all tags.

**Response:**
```json
{
  "err": 0,
  "tags": [
    {"id": 1, "name": "harry potter", "type": "freeform", "score": 42},
    {"id": 2, "name": "romance", "type": "freeform", "score": 38}
  ]
}
```

### POST /api/v0/tags/submit

Submit a new tag.

**Body:**
```json
{
  "name": "new tag",
  "url_id": "ao3-12345"
}
```

### POST /api/v0/tags/vote

Vote on a tag.

**Body:**
```json
{
  "tag_id": 1,
  "vote": 1  // 1 = upvote, -1 = downvote
}
```

## Recommendations API

### GET /api/v0/recommendations/{source}

Get recommendations for a source site.

**Parameters:**
| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| limit | int | No | Number of recommendations (default: 20) |

**Response:**
```json
{
  "recommendations": [
    {
      "url_id": "ao3-12345",
```

# Appendix F: Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|-----------|
| **ACID** | Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability — database transaction properties |
| **API** | Application Programming Interface — how software components communicate |
| **ARIA** | Accessible Rich Internet Applications — HTML attributes for accessibility |
| **Async** | Asynchronous — code that can pause and resume, enabling concurrent operations |
| **Axum** | Rust web framework built on Tokio and Tower |
| **CRUD** | Create, Read, Update, Delete — basic database operations |
| **CORS** | Cross-Origin Resource Sharing — browser security for cross-domain requests |
| **EPUB** | Electronic Publication — ebook file format |
| **FTS** | Full-Text Search — searching text content efficiently |
| **GIN** | Generalized Inverted Index — PostgreSQL index type for text/JSONB |
| **HTML** | HyperText Markup Language — web page structure |
| **JSON** | JavaScript Object Notation — data interchange format |
| **Jaccard** | Jaccard similarity coefficient — measure of set similarity |
| **Middleware** | Code that runs before/after request handlers |
| **ORM** | Object-Relational Mapping — abstracting database queries |
| **PostgreSQL** | Advanced open-source relational database |
| **Redis** | In-memory data store used for caching and rate limiting |
| **REST** | Representational State Transfer — API architectural style |
| **Rust** | Systems programming language focused on safety and performance |
| **SQLx** | Async Rust library for PostgreSQL with compile-time checked queries |
| **SPA** | Single Page Application — web app that loads once, navigates client-side |
| **Svelte** | Frontend framework that compiles to vanilla JavaScript |
| **SvelteKit** | Meta-framework built on Svelte for routing and SSR |
| **Tokio** | Async runtime for Rust |
| **TLS** | Transport Layer Security — encryption for network traffic |
| **TypeScript** | JavaScript with static typing |
| **Vitest** | Fast test runner for Vite-based projects |
| **WebSocket** | Persistent bidirectional network connection |
| **XSS** | Cross-Site Scripting — injecting malicious JavaScript |
| **XenForo** | Forum software used by some fanfiction communities |

# Chapter 5 Deep Dive: Axum Request Lifecycle

## How Axum Processes a Request

When a request arrives at Axum, it goes through a precise lifecycle. Understanding this lifecycle helps you write efficient handlers and debug issues.

### Step 1: TCP Connection

```
Client → TCP SYN → Server
Client ← TCP SYN-ACK ← Server
Client → TCP ACK → Server
// TCP connection established on port 3000
```

Axum's `TcpListener` accepts incoming connections. Each connection is handled by a Tokio task (lightweight green thread).

### Step 2: HTTP Parsing

The raw TCP stream is parsed into an HTTP request:

```http
GET /api/v0/export?url=https://archiveofourown.org/works/12345 HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:3000
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0
Accept: application/json
```

Axum's HTTP parser extracts:
- Method: `GET`
- URI: `/api/v0/export?url=...`
- Headers: `Host`, `User-Agent`, `Accept`
- Body: (empty for GET)

### Step 3: Route Matching

Axum walks through the router tree to find a matching route:

```
Router
├── /api/v0/export → export_handler ✓ MATCH
├── /api/v0/meta → meta_handler
├── /api/v0/search → search_handler
└── /opds/...
```

The router uses a radix tree (similar to a trie) for O(n) matching where n is the length of the URL path, not the number of routes.

### Step 4: Middleware Execution

Before the handler runs, middleware layers execute in order:

```
Request → CorsLayer → TraceLayer → Handler
                                    ↓
Response ← CorsLayer ← TraceLayer ← Handler
```

Each middleware can:
- Modify the request before passing it down
- Modify the response after it comes back
- Short-circuit (return a response without calling the handler)

### Step 5: Extractor Processing

Extractors pull data from the request:

```rust
async fn export_handler(
    Query(params): Query<HashMap<String, String>>,  // Extract query params
    headers: HeaderMap,                              // Extract headers
    State(state): State<Arc<AppState>>,              // Extract shared state
) -> Result<Json<Value>, AppError> {
    // By the time we get here, all extractors have succeeded
    // If any extractor fails, the handler never runs
}
```

**Extractor order matters:** Extractors are processed left to right. If `Query` fails (malformed query string), Axum returns 400 Bad Request without processing `headers` or `State`.

### Step 6: Handler Execution

The handler function runs. It can:
- Access the database via `state.db`
- Access Redis via `state.redis`
- Make HTTP requests via `state.http_client`
- Return JSON, HTML, or error responses

### Step 7: Response Serialization

The return value is converted to an HTTP response:

```rust
// Json<T> → 200 OK with Content-Type: application/json
Ok(Json(json!({"err": 0})))
// Becomes:
// HTTP/1.1 200 OK
// Content-Type: application/json
// {"err": 0}

// AppError → appropriate status code with JSON error
Err(AppError::BadRequest(-1, "no query".into()))
// Becomes:
// HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
// Content-Type: application/json
// {"err": -1, "msg": "no query"}
```

### Step 8: Middleware Post-Processing

The response passes back through middleware:

```
Response → TraceLayer (logs timing) → CorsLayer (adds headers) → Client
```

### Step 9: TCP Response

The HTTP response is sent back over the TCP connection:

```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 42
X-Response-Time: 15ms

{"err":0,"url_id":"ao3-12345","epub_url":"/cache/epub/ao3-12345.epub"}
```

## Handler Composition

Handlers can be composed from smaller functions:

```rust
// Compose handlers using nested functions
async fn export_with_logging(
    State(state): State<Arc<AppState>>,
    Query(params): Query<HashMap<String, String>>,
    headers: HeaderMap,
) -> Result<Json<Value>, AppError> {
    let start = std::time::Instant::now();
    
    // Delegate to the actual handler
    let result = export_handler_inner(state, params, headers).await?;
    
    // Log the result
    tracing::info!(
        url = %result.get("url_id").unwrap_or(&serde_json::Value::Null),
        duration_ms = start.elapsed().as_millis() as u64,
        "Export completed"
    );
    
    Ok(result)
}
```

## State Extraction Patterns

### Pattern 1: Direct State Access

```rust
async fn handler(
    State(state): State<Arc<AppState>>,
) -> Json<Value> {
    // Access database directly
    let count: i64 = sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fic_info")
        .fetch_one(&state.db)
        .await
        .unwrap_or(0);
    
    Json(json!({"count": count}))
}
```

### Pattern 2: Extract and Validate

```rust
async fn handler(
    Query(params): Query<HashMap<String, String>>,
    State(state): State<Arc<AppState>>,
) -> Result<Json<Value>, AppError> {
    let url = params.get("url")
        .ok_or_else(|| AppError::BadRequest(-1, "no query".into()))?;
    
    validate_url(url)?;
    
    let url_id = generate_url_id(url)
        .ok_or_else(|| AppError::BadRequest(-5, "unsupported URL".into()))?;
    
    // ... process the request
}
```

### Pattern 3: Multiple Extractors

```rust
async fn handler(
    Path(id): Path<i32>,
    Query(opts): Query<Options>,
    State(state): State<Arc<AppState>>,
    headers: HeaderMap,
) -> Result<Response, AppError> {
    let user_agent = headers.get("User-Agent")
        .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
        .unwrap_or("unknown");
    
    tracing::info!(
        id = id,
        user_agent = user_agent,
        "Processing request"
    );
    
    // ... handle the request
}
```

## Error Handling Deep Dive

### The Error Conversion Chain

```rust
// sqlx::Error → AppError::Database
impl From<sqlx::Error> for AppError {
    fn from(err: sqlx::Error) -> Self {
        match err {
            sqlx::Error::RowNotFound => {
                AppError::NotFound("resource not found".into())
            }
            sqlx::Error::Database(ref db_err) => {
                if db_err.code() == Some("23505".into()) {
                    AppError::BadRequest(-2, "already exists".into())
                } else {
                    AppError::Database(db_err.message().unwrap_or("unknown").into())
                }
            }
            _ => AppError::Database(err.to_string()),
        }
    }
}

// redis::RedisError → AppError::Cache
impl From<redis::RedisError> for AppError {
    fn from(err: redis::RedisError) -> Self {
        AppError::CacheError(err.to_string())
    }
}

// reqwest::Error → AppError::Scrape
impl From<reqwest::Error> for AppError {
    fn from(err: reqwest::Error) -> Self {
        if err.is_timeout() {
            AppError::ScrapeError("request timed out".into())
        } else if err.is_connect() {
            AppError::ScrapeError("connection failed".into())
        } else {
            AppError::ScrapeError(err.to_string())
        }
    }
}
```

### Custom Error Responses

```rust
impl AppError {
    fn to_response(&self) -> (StatusCode, Json<Value>) {
        match self {
            AppError::BadRequest(code, msg) => (
                StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,
                json!({
                    "err": code,
                    "msg": msg,
                    "type": "bad_request"
                }),
            ),
            AppError::RateLimited(retry_after) => (
                StatusCode::TOO_MANY_REQUESTS,
                json!({
                    "err": -429,
                    "msg": "rate limited",
                    "retry_after": retry_after,
                    "type": "rate_limited"
                }),
            ),
            _ => (
                StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
                json!({
                    "err": -1,
                    "msg": "internal server error",
                    "type": "internal"
                }),
            ),
        }
    }
}
```

# Chapter 7 Deep Dive: PostgreSQL Internals

## How PostgreSQL Stores Data

Understanding how PostgreSQL stores data helps you write better queries.

### Pages and Tuples

PostgreSQL stores data in **pages** (8KB blocks). Each page contains:
- Page header (24 bytes)
- Line pointers (2 bytes each)
- Tuples (rows) packed from the end of the page

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Page Header (24 bytes)              │
├─────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Line Pointer 1 → ──────────────┐   │
│ Line Pointer 2 → ────────────┐ │   │
│ Line Pointer 3 → ──────────┐ │ │   │
│ ...                         │ │ │   │
│ (free space)                │ │ │   │
│ Tuple 3 ←──────────────────┘ │ │   │
│ Tuple 2 ←────────────────────┘ │   │
│ Tuple 1 ←──────────────────────┘   │
└─────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### MVCC (Multi-Version Concurrency Control)

PostgreSQL uses MVCC to allow concurrent reads and writes without locking:

```sql
-- Transaction 1
BEGIN;
UPDATE fic_info SET words = 50000 WHERE url_id = 'ao3-123';
-- Old version of the row is kept in place
-- New version is written to a new location

-- Transaction 2 (concurrent)
BEGIN;
SELECT words FROM fic_info WHERE url_id = 'ao3-123';
-- Sees the OLD version (before the update)
COMMIT;

-- Transaction 1 commits
COMMIT;
-- Now transaction 2's snapshot still sees the old version
-- until it starts a new transaction
```

**Why this matters:** Long-running transactions can prevent vacuum from cleaning up old row versions, leading to table bloat. Keep transactions short!

## Query Planning

When you run a query, PostgreSQL creates a **query plan**:

```sql
EXPLAIN ANALYZE
SELECT * FROM fic_info
WHERE title ILIKE '%harry potter%'
ORDER BY words DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

Output:
```
Limit  (cost=0.00..1234.56 rows=10 width=123) (actual time=0.123..0.456 rows=10 loops=1)
  ->  Sort  (cost=0.00..1234.56 rows=50000 width=123) (actual time=0.123..0.345 rows=10 loops=1)
        Sort Key: words DESC
        Sort Method: top-N heapsort  Memory: 25kB
        ->  Seq Scan on fic_info  (cost=0.00..1234.56 rows=50000 width=123) (actual time=0.012..0.234 rows=50000 loops=1)
              Filter: (title ~~* '%harry potter%'::text)
Planning Time: 0.123 ms
Execution Time: 0.567 ms
```

**Key metrics:**
- `cost` — Estimated cost (startup..total)
- `rows` — Estimated number of rows
- `actual time` — Real execution time
- `loops` — How many times the node was executed

### Index Usage

```sql
-- Without index: Seq Scan (reads every row)
Seq Scan on fic_info  (cost=0.00..1234.56 rows=50000)

-- With GIN index on title: Index Scan (reads only matching rows)
Index Scan using idx_fic_title_fts on fic_info  (cost=0.25..123.45 rows=100)
```

### Common Performance Issues

**1. Missing indexes:**
```sql
-- Slow: full table scan
SELECT * FROM fic_info WHERE author = 'SomeAuthor';
-- Fix: add index
CREATE INDEX idx_fic_author ON fic_info(author);
```

**2. N+1 queries:**
```rust
// Slow: one query per fic
for fic in &fics {
    let tags = sqlx::query("SELECT * FROM fic_tags WHERE fic_url_id = $1")
        .bind(&fic.url_id)
        .fetch_all(&pool).await?;
}

// Fast: single query with JOIN
let fics_with_tags = sqlx::query(
    "SELECT f.*, array_agg(t.name) as tags FROM fic_info f
     LEFT JOIN fic_tags ft ON f.url_id = ft.fic_url_id
     LEFT JOIN tags t ON ft.tag_id = t.id
     GROUP BY f.url_id"
)
.fetch_all(&pool).await?;
```

**3. Large result sets:**
```sql
-- Slow: returns all rows
SELECT * FROM fic_info;

-- Fast: pagination
SELECT * FROM fic_info ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT 20 OFFSET 0;
```

**4. Unnecessary DISTINCT:**
```sql
-- Slow: removes duplicates after fetching
SELECT DISTINCT author FROM fic_info;

-- Fast: use GROUP BY instead
SELECT author FROM fic_info GROUP BY author;
```

## Connection Pool Deep Dive

```rust
// PgPool configuration
let pool = PgPoolOptions::new()
    .max_connections(10)      // Max concurrent connections
    .min_connections(2)       // Min idle connections
    .acquire_timeout(10s)     // Max wait for connection
    .idle_timeout(300s)       // Close idle connections
    .max_lifetime(1800s)      // Max connection lifetime
    .connect(url).await?;
```

**Monitoring pool usage:**
```sql
-- Check active connections
SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE datname = 'fichub';

-- Check connection states
SELECT state, count(*)
FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE datname = 'fichub'
GROUP BY state;

-- Check long-running queries
SELECT pid, now() - pg_stat_activity.query_start AS duration, query
FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE state = 'active' AND datname = 'fichub'
ORDER BY duration DESC;
```

# Chapter 9 Deep Dive: Advanced CRUD Patterns

## Bulk Operations

### Batch Insert with RETURNING

```rust
pub async fn bulk_upsert_fics(
    pool: &PgPool,
    fics: &[FicMetadata],
) -> Result<Vec<String>, sqlx::Error> {
    let url_ids: Vec<String> = fics.iter().map(|f| f.url_id.clone()).collect();
    let titles: Vec<String> = fics.iter().map(|f| f.title.clone()).collect();
    let authors: Vec<String> = fics.iter().map(|f| f.author.clone()).collect();
    let words: Vec<i32> = fics.iter().map(|f| f.words).collect();
    let chapters: Vec<i32> = fics.iter().map(|f| f.chapters).collect();

    let result = sqlx::query_scalar::<_, String>(
        r#"
        INSERT INTO fic_info (url_id, title, author, words, chapters)
        SELECT * FROM UNNEST($1::text[], $2::text[], $3::text[], $4::int[], $5::int[])
        ON CONFLICT (url_id) DO UPDATE SET
            title = EXCLUDED.title,
            words = EXCLUDED.words,
            chapters = EXCLUDED.chapters,
            updated_at = NOW()
        RETURNING url_id
        "#,
    )
    .bind(&url_ids)
    .bind(&titles)
    .bind(&authors)
    .bind(&words)
    .bind(&chapters)
    .fetch_all(pool)
    .await?;

    Ok(result)
}
```

### Streaming Queries

For large result sets, use streaming to avoid loading everything into memory:

```rust
use sqlx::PgPool;
use futures::StreamExt;

pub async fn stream_all_fics(pool: &PgPool) -> Result<(), sqlx::Error> {
    let mut stream = sqlx::query_as::<_, FicInfo>(
        "SELECT * FROM fic_info ORDER BY url_id"
    )
    .fetch(pool);

    while let Some(result) = stream.next().await {
        let fic = result?;
        // Process each fic individually
        println!("{} by {} ({} words)", fic.title, fic.author, fic.words);
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

### CTEs for Complex Queries

Common Table Expressions make complex queries readable:

```sql
-- Find the most popular stories with their tag statistics
WITH story_stats AS (
    SELECT
        url_id,
        title,
        author,
        words,
        (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM export_log e WHERE e.url_id = f.url_id) as download_count,
        (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fic_tags ft WHERE ft.fic_url_id = f.url_id) as tag_count
    FROM fic_info f
    WHERE complete = true AND words > 10000
),
tag_leaders AS (
    SELECT
        s.*,
        array_agg(t.name) as tags,
        RANK() OVER (ORDER BY s.download_count DESC) as rank
    FROM story_stats s
    LEFT JOIN fic_tags ft ON s.url_id = ft.fic_url_id
    LEFT JOIN tags t ON ft.tag_id = t.id
    GROUP BY s.url_id, s.title, s.author, s.words, s.download_count, s.tag_count
)
SELECT * FROM tag_leaders
WHERE rank <= 100
ORDER BY rank;
```
