# Chapter 10 Deep Dive: Middleware Architecture

## Tower Service Pattern

Axum is built on Tower, which provides a composable middleware system:

```rust
use tower::{Service, ServiceExt};
use tower_http::trace::TraceLayer;
use axum::middleware::{self, Next};
use axum::extract::Request;
use axum::response::Response;
use std::time::Instant;

// Custom logging middleware
async fn logging_middleware(
    request: Request,
    next: Next,
) -> Response {
    let method = request.method().clone();
    let uri = request.uri().clone();
    let start = Instant::now();

    let response = next.run(request).await;

    let duration = start.elapsed();
    let status = response.status();

    tracing::info!(
        method = %method,
        uri = %uri,
        status = status.as_u16(),
        duration_ms = duration.as_millis() as u64,
        "Request completed"
    );

    response
}

// Custom authentication middleware
async fn auth_middleware(
    State(state): State<Arc<AppState>>,
    request: Request,
    next: Next,
) -> Result<Response, AppError> {
    // Check for API key in headers
    let api_key = request.headers()
        .get("X-API-Key")
        .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok());

    match api_key {
        Some(key) if key == &state.config.api_key => {
            Ok(next.run(request).await)
        }
        _ => Err(AppError::Unauthorized("invalid API key".into())),
    }
}

// Rate limiting middleware
async fn rate_limit_middleware(
    State(state): State<Arc<AppState>>,
    request: Request,
    next: Next,
) -> Result<Response, AppError> {
    let ip = get_client_ip(&request);

    match state.rate_limiter.check(&ip).await? {
        RateLimitResult::Allowed => {
            let mut response = next.run(request).await;
            // Add rate limit headers
            response.headers_mut().insert(
                "X-RateLimit-Remaining",
                "99".parse().unwrap(),
            );
            Ok(response)
        }
        RateLimitResult::Limited { retry_after } => {
            Err(AppError::RateLimited(retry_after))
        }
    }
}

// CORS middleware with custom configuration
fn custom_cors() -> CorsLayer {
    CorsLayer::new()
        .allow_origin([
            "http://localhost:5173".parse().unwrap(),
            "https://fichub.example.com".parse().unwrap(),
        ])
        .allow_methods([
            Method::GET,
            Method::POST,
            Method::OPTIONS,
        ])
        .allow_headers([
            header::CONTENT_TYPE,
            header::AUTHORIZATION,
            header::USER_AGENT,
        ])
        .max_age(Duration::from_secs(3600))
}
```

## Middleware Ordering

The order of `.layer()` calls matters:

```rust
Router::new()
    .route("/api", get(handler))
    // Layers are applied in REVERSE order
    // 1. CorsLayer runs first (outermost)
    // 2. TraceLayer runs second
    // 3. RateLimitLayer runs third
    // 4. Handler runs last (innermost)
    .layer(rate_limit_layer)  // Applied third
    .layer(TraceLayer::new_for_http())  // Applied second
    .layer(CorsLayer::permissive())  // Applied first
    .with_state(state)
```

**Request flow:**
```
Request → CorsLayer → TraceLayer → RateLimitLayer → Handler
```

**Response flow:**
```
Response → CorsLayer ← TraceLayer ← RateLimitLayer ← Handler
```

## Extension Layer for Per-Request Data

```rust
use axum::extract::Extension;

// Add data that's available to all handlers
let app = Router::new()
    .route("/api", get(handler))
    .layer(Extension(Arc::new(AppMetrics::new())));

// In handler
async fn handler(
    Extension(metrics): Extension<Arc<AppMetrics>>,
) -> Json<Value> {
    metrics.increment_counter("api.calls");
    // ...
}
```

## Request ID Middleware

Add a unique ID to every request for tracing:

```rust
use uuid::Uuid;

async fn request_id_middleware(
    mut request: Request,
    next: Next,
) -> Response {
    let request_id = Uuid::new_v4().to_string();
    
    // Add to request extensions
    request.extensions_mut().insert(request_id.clone());
    
    // Run handler
    let mut response = next.run(request).await;
    
    // Add to response headers
    response.headers_mut().insert(
        "X-Request-ID",
        request_id.parse().unwrap(),
    );
    
    response
}
```

# Chapter 13 Deep Dive: Advanced Scraping Patterns

## Resilient HTTP Requests

Web scraping is inherently unreliable. Sites go down, change their HTML, or block your requests. FicHub implements several resilience patterns:

### Retry with Exponential Backoff

```rust
use std::time::Duration;

async fn resilient_fetch(
    client: &reqwest::Client,
    url: &str,
    max_retries: u32,
) -> Result<String, ScrapeError> {
    let mut last_error = None;

    for attempt in 0..max_retries {
        match client.get(url).send().await {
            Ok(response) => {
                if response.status().is_success() {
                    return response.text().await.map_err(Into::into);
                }

                // Don't retry on client errors (4xx)
                if response.status().is_client_error() {
                    return Err(ScrapeError::Http(
                        reqwest::Error::from(response)
                    ));
                }

                // Retry on server errors (5xx)
                last_error = Some(ScrapeError::Http(
                    reqwest::Error::from(response)
                ));
            }
            Err(e) => {
                // Network errors are retryable
                last_error = Some(ScrapeError::Http(e));
            }
        }

        // Exponential backoff: 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s...
        let delay = Duration::from_secs(2u64.pow(attempt));
        tracing::warn!(
            url = url,
            attempt = attempt + 1,
            max_retries = max_retries,
            delay_ms = delay.as_millis() as u64,
            "Retrying request"
        );
        tokio::time::sleep(delay).await;
    }

    last_error.ok_or_else(|| ScrapeError::Parse("max retries exceeded".into()))
}
```

### Circuit Breaker Pattern

Stop trying to reach a site that's consistently failing:

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;
use tokio::sync::RwLock;

pub struct CircuitBreaker {
    failure_count: Arc<RwLock<u32>>,
    success_count: Arc<RwLock<u32>>,
    state: Arc<RwLock<CircuitState>>,
    threshold: u32,
    reset_timeout: Duration,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
enum CircuitState {
    Closed,      // Normal operation
    Open,        // Failing — reject requests
    HalfOpen,    // Testing — allow one request through
}

impl CircuitBreaker {
    pub fn new(threshold: u32, reset_timeout: Duration) -> Self {
        Self {
            failure_count: Arc::new(RwLock::new(0)),
            success_count: Arc::new(RwLock::new(0)),
            state: Arc::new(RwLock::new(CircuitState::Closed)),
            threshold,
            reset_timeout,
        }
    }

    pub async fn call<F, T, E>(&self, operation: F) -> Result<T, E>
    where
        F: std::future::Future<Output = Result<T, E>>,
    {
        let state = self.state.read().await.clone();

        match state {
            CircuitState::Open => {
                return Err(/* circuit open error */);
            }
            CircuitState::HalfOpen => {
                // Allow one request through to test
            }
            CircuitState::Closed => {}
        }

        match operation.await {
            Ok(result) => {
                self.on_success().await;
                Ok(result)
            }
            Err(e) => {
                self.on_failure().await;
                Err(e)
            }
        }
    }

    async fn on_success(&self) {
        *self.success_count.write().await += 1;
        *self.failure_count.write().await = 0;
        *self.state.write().await = CircuitState::Closed;
    }

    async fn on_failure(&self) {
        let failures = {
            let mut count = self.failure_count.write().await;
            *count += 1;
            *count
        };

        if failures >= self.threshold {
            *self.state.write().await = CircuitState::Open;
            tracing::warn!(
                failures = failures,
                threshold = self.threshold,
                "Circuit breaker opened"
            );

            // Schedule reset
            let state = self.state.clone();
            tokio::spawn(async move {
                tokio::time::sleep(self.reset_timeout).await;
                *state.write().await = CircuitState::HalfOpen;
            });
        }
    }
}
```

### HTML Change Detection

Detect when a site changes its HTML structure:

```rust
pub struct HtmlMonitor {
    known_selectors: HashMap<String, Vec<String>>,
}

impl HtmlMonitor {
    pub fn check_for_changes(
        &self,
        site: &str,
        document: &Html,
    ) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut warnings = Vec::new();

        if let Some(selectors) = self.known_selectors.get(site) {
            for selector_str in selectors {
                let selector = Selector::parse(selector_str).unwrap();
                if document.select(&selector).next().is_none() {
                    warnings.push(format!(
                        "Selector '{}' not found on {} — site may have changed",
                        selector_str, site
                    ));
                }
            }
        }

        warnings
    }
}
```

## Parallel Scraping

Scrape multiple chapters concurrently:

```rust
use futures::stream::{self, StreamExt};

pub async fn fetch_chapters_parallel(
    client: &Client,
    urls: &[String],
    max_concurrent: usize,
) -> Result<Vec<Chapter>, ScrapeError> {
    let chapters: Vec<Chapter> = stream::iter(urls.iter().enumerate())
        .map(|(i, url)| {
            let client = client.clone();
            let url = url.clone();
            async move {
                let response = client.get(&url).send().await?;
                let html = response.text().await?;
                let document = Html::parse_document(&html);

                let content = extract_chapter_content(&document)?;

                Ok(Chapter {
                    title: format!("Chapter {}", i + 1),
                    content,
                    word_count: content.split_whitespace().count() as i32,
                    chapter_number: (i + 1) as i32,
                })
            }
        })
        .buffer_unordered(max_concurrent)
        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()
        .await?;

    Ok(chapters)
}
```

**Key points:**
- `buffer_unordered(max_concurrent)` limits concurrent requests
- `stream::iter` converts the URL list to a stream
- `.map` creates async operations for each URL
- `.collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()` gathers results, propagating errors

## Rate Limiting per Site

Different sites have different rate limits:

```rust
pub struct SiteRateLimiter {
    limits: HashMap<String, RateLimit>,
}

struct RateLimit {
    requests_per_second: f64,
    last_request: Instant,
}

impl SiteRateLimiter {
    pub async fn wait_for_slot(&mut self, site: &str) {
        if let Some(limit) = self.limits.get_mut(site) {
            let elapsed = limit.last_request.elapsed();
            let min_interval = Duration::from_secs_f64(1.0 / limit.requests_per_second);

            if elapsed < min_interval {
                let wait_time = min_interval - elapsed;
                tokio::time::sleep(wait_time).await;
            }

            limit.last_request = Instant::now();
        }
    }
}
```

## Scraping Ethics and Best Practices

### robots.txt

Always check and respect robots.txt:

```rust
async fn check_robots_txt(client: &Client, site_url: &str) -> bool {
    let robots_url = format!("{}/robots.txt", site_url);

    match client.get(&robots_url).send().await {
        Ok(response) if response.status().is_success() => {
            let text = response.text().await.unwrap_or_default();
            // Simple check — don't scrape paths marked as disallowed
            !text.contains("Disallow: /works/")
        }
        _ => true // If no robots.txt, assume allowed
    }
}
```

### Polite Headers

Always identify yourself:

```rust
let client = reqwest::Client::builder()
    .user_agent("FicHub/0.1.0 (https://fichub.example.com; +https://fichub.example.com/about)")
    .timeout(Duration::from_secs(30))
    .build()?;
```

### Delays Between Requests

Never hammer a site with rapid requests:

```rust
// Minimum delay between requests to the same site
const MIN_DELAY: Duration = Duration::from_secs(1);

// Add jitter to avoid thundering herd
fn jitter(base: Duration) -> Duration {
    let jitter_ms = rand::thread_rng().gen_range(0..500);
    base + Duration::from_millis(jitter_ms)
}
```

## EPUB Metadata Standards

The EPUB standard supports rich metadata. Here's how to set it all:

```rust
fn set_comprehensive_metadata(
    builder: &mut EpubBuilder<ZipLibrary>,
    metadata: &FicMetadata,
) -> Result<(), ExportError> {
    // Basic metadata
    builder.set_metadata("title", &metadata.title)?;
    builder.set_metadata("creator", &metadata.author)?;
    builder.set_metadata("language", "en")?;
    builder.set_metadata("publisher", "FicHub")?;

    // Description
    if !metadata.summary.is_empty() {
        builder.set_metadata("description", &metadata.summary)?;
    }

    // Rights
    builder.set_metadata("rights", &format!(
        "Fanfiction by {}. Original work belongs to the respective authors.",
        metadata.author
    ))?;

    // Identifiers
    builder.set_metadata("identifier", &format!(
        "urn:fichub:{}",
        metadata.url_id
    ))?;

    // Dates
    let now = chrono::Utc::now().format("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ");
    builder.set_metadata("date", &now.to_string())?;

    // Custom metadata
    builder.set_metadata("source", &metadata.url)?;
    builder.set_metadata("fichub:words", &metadata.words.to_string())?;
    builder.set_metadata("fichub:chapters", &metadata.chapters.to_string())?;
    builder.set_metadata("fichub:complete", &metadata.complete.to_string())?;
    builder.set_metadata("fichub:source", &metadata.source)?;

    Ok(())
}
```

## EPUB Validation

Validate your EPUB against the spec:

```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod epub_validation_tests {
    use super::*;
    use epub_builder::EpubContent;

    fn create_test_epub() -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut builder = EpubBuilder::new(ZipLibrary::new()).unwrap();
        builder.set_metadata("title", "Test Book").unwrap();
        builder.set_metadata("author", "Test Author").unwrap();

        let content = r#"<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml">
<head><title>Chapter 1</title></head>
<body><h1>Chapter 1</h1><p>Hello world</p></body>
</html>"#;

        builder.add_content(
            EpubContent::new("chapter1.xhtml", content.as_bytes())
                .set_title("Chapter 1")
        ).unwrap();

        let mut buf = Vec::new();
        builder.generate(&mut buf).unwrap();
        buf
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_epub_is_valid_zip() {
        let epub = create_test_epub();
        let cursor = std::io::Cursor::new(epub);
        let archive = zip::ZipArchive::new(cursor).unwrap();

        // Must have at least 2 files (mimetype + content)
        assert!(archive.len() >= 2);

        // First file must be mimetype
        let first = archive.by_index(0).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(first.name(), "mimetype");
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_epub_has_required_files() {
        let epub = create_test_epub();
        let cursor = std::io::Cursor::new(epub);
        let archive = zip::ZipArchive::new(cursor).unwrap();

        let names: Vec<String> = (0..archive.len())
            .map(|i| archive.by_index(i).unwrap().name().to_string())
            .collect();

        assert!(names.contains(&"mimetype".to_string()));
        assert!(names.iter().any(|n| n.ends_with(".xhtml")));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_mimetype_content() {
        let epub = create_test_epub();
        let cursor = std::io::Cursor::new(epub);
        let mut archive = zip::ZipArchive::new(cursor).unwrap();

        let mut mimetype = String::new();
        archive.by_name("mimetype").unwrap().read_to_string(&mut mimetype).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(mimetype.trim(), "application/epub+zip");
    }
}
```

## Cover Image Support

Add cover images to EPUBs when available:

```rust
fn add_cover_image(
    builder: &mut EpubBuilder<ZipLibrary>,
    cover_data: &[u8],
) -> Result<(), ExportError> {
    // Determine image type
    let content_type = if cover_data.starts_with(&[0x89, 0x50, 0x4E, 0x47]) {
        "image/png"
    } else if cover_data.starts_with(&[0xFF, 0xD8, 0xFF]) {
        "image/jpeg"
    } else {
        return Err(ExportError::BuildError("unsupported image format".into()));
    };

    // Add the image resource
    builder.add_resource("cover.jpg", cover_data, content_type)?;

    // Create cover page XHTML
    let cover_xhtml = format!(
        r#"<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml">
<head>
    <title>Cover</title>
    <style type="text/css">
        body {{ margin: 0; padding: 0; text-align: center; }}
        img {{ max-width: 100%; max-height: 100%; }}
    </style>
</head>
<body>
    <img src="cover.jpg" alt="Cover"/>
</body>
</html>"#
    );

    builder.add_content(
        EpubContent::new("cover.xhtml", cover_xhtml.as_bytes())
            .set_title("Cover")
    )?;

    Ok(())
}
```

# Chapter 19 Deep Dive: Disk Cache Advanced Topics

## Cache Eviction Strategies

FicHub needs to manage disk space. Here are strategies for cache eviction:

### LRU (Least Recently Used)

```rust
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::time::Instant;

pub struct LruCache {
    entries: HashMap<String, CacheEntry>,
    max_size: u64,  // bytes
    current_size: u64,
}

struct CacheEntry {
    path: PathBuf,
    size: u64,
    last_accessed: Instant,
}

impl LruCache {
    pub fn evict_if_needed(&mut self) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
        let mut evicted = Vec::new();

        while self.current_size > self.max_size {
            // Find the least recently used entry
            if let Some(lru_key) = self.entries.iter()
                .min_by_key(|(_, entry)| entry.last_accessed)
                .map(|(key, _)| key.clone())
            {
                if let Some(entry) = self.entries.remove(&lru_key) {
                    let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&entry.path);
                    self.current_size -= entry.size;
                    evicted.push(entry.path);
                }
            } else {
                break;
            }
        }

        evicted
    }

    pub fn touch(&mut self, key: &str) {
        if let Some(entry) = self.entries.get_mut(key) {
            entry.last_accessed = Instant::now();
        }
    }
}
```

### Size-Based Eviction

```rust
pub fn cleanup_cache(cache_dir: &PathBuf, max_size_mb: u64) -> Result<u64, std::io::Error> {
    let max_bytes = max_size_mb * 1024 * 1024;

    // Collect all cache files with metadata
    let mut files: Vec<(PathBuf, u64, SystemTime)> = Vec::new();
    for entry in std::fs::read_dir(cache_dir)? {
        let entry = entry?;
        let metadata = entry.metadata()?;
        if metadata.is_file() {
            let modified = metadata.modified()?;
            files.push((entry.path(), metadata.len(), modified));
        }
    }

    // Sort by modification time (oldest first)
    files.sort_by_key(|(_, _, modified)| *modified);

    // Calculate total size
    let total_size: u64 = files.iter().map(|(_, size, _)| size).sum();

    // Evict oldest files until under limit
    let mut freed = 0u64;
    for (path, size, _) in &files {
        if total_size - freed <= max_bytes {
            break;
        }
        std::fs::remove_file(path)?;
        freed += size;
        tracing::info!(
            path = %path.display(),
            size = size,
            "Evicted cache file"
        );
    }

    Ok(freed)
}
```

### Cache Statistics

```rust
pub fn cache_stats(cache_dir: &PathBuf) -> Result<CacheStats, std::io::Error> {
    let mut stats = CacheStats::default();

    for entry in std::fs::read_dir(cache_dir)? {
        let entry = entry?;
        let metadata = entry.metadata()?;

        if metadata.is_file() {
            stats.total_files += 1;
            stats.total_size += metadata.len();

            if let Ok(modified) = metadata.modified() {
                if stats.oldest_file.is_none() || modified < stats.oldest_file.unwrap() {
                    stats.oldest_file = Some(modified);
                }
                if stats.newest_file.is_none() || modified > stats.newest_file.unwrap() {
                    stats.newest_file = Some(modified);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    Ok(stats)
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct CacheStats {
    pub total_files: u64,
    pub total_size: u64,
    pub oldest_file: Option<SystemTime>,
    pub newest_file: Option<SystemTime>,
}
```

## Cache Integrity Checking

Verify cached files haven't been corrupted:

```rust
pub fn verify_cache_integrity(cache_dir: &PathBuf) -> Result<Vec<PathBuf>, std::io::Error> {
    let mut corrupted = Vec::new();

    for entry in std::fs::read_dir(cache_dir)? {
        let entry = entry?;
        let path = entry.path();

        if path.extension().and_then(|e| e.to_str()) == Some("epub") {
            // Try to open as ZIP
            match zip::ZipArchive::new(std::fs::File::open(&path)?) {
                Ok(_) => {} // Valid EPUB
                Err(e) => {
                    tracing::warn!(
                        path = %path.display(),
                        error = %e,
                        "Corrupted EPUB found"
                    );
                    corrupted.push(path);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    Ok(corrupted)
}
```

# Chapter 20 Deep Dive: Export Flow Optimization

## Parallel Chapter Fetching

The biggest bottleneck in the export flow is fetching chapters sequentially. Here's how to parallelize:

```rust
pub async fn optimized_export(
    client: &Client,
    metadata: &FicMetadata,
    config: &Config,
) -> Result<PathBuf, ExportError> {
    // Generate chapter URLs
    let chapter_urls: Vec<String> = (1..=metadata.chapters)
        .map(|i| {
            if metadata.chapters == 1 {
                metadata.url.clone()
            } else {
                format!("{}/chapters/{}", metadata.url, i)
            }
        })
        .collect();

    // Fetch chapters in parallel (max 5 concurrent)
    let chapters = fetch_chapters_parallel(client, &chapter_urls, 5).await?;

    // Generate EPUB
    create_epub(metadata, &chapters, config)
}

async fn fetch_chapters_parallel(
    client: &Client,
    urls: &[String],
    max_concurrent: usize,
) -> Result<Vec<Chapter>, ExportError> {
    use futures::stream::{self, StreamExt};

    let chapters: Vec<Chapter> = stream::iter(urls.iter().enumerate())
        .map(|(i, url)| {
            let client = client.clone();
            let url = url.clone();
            async move {
                let response = resilient_fetch(&client, &url, 3).await?;
                let document = Html::parse_document(&response);

                let title = extract_text(&document, "h2.heading");
                let content = extract_chapter_content(&document)?;
                let word_count = content.split_whitespace().count() as i32;

                Ok(Chapter {
                    title,
                    content,
                    word_count,
                    chapter_number: (i + 1) as i32,
                })
            }
        })
        .buffer_unordered(max_concurrent)
        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()
        .await?;

    Ok(chapters)
}
```

**Performance comparison:**
- Sequential: 10 chapters × 1 second each = 10 seconds
- Parallel (5 concurrent): 10 chapters ÷ 5 batches × 1 second = 2 seconds
- Parallel (10 concurrent): 10 chapters × 1 second = 1 second (but may hit rate limits)

## Caching Intermediate Results

Cache chapter content so re-exporting the same story is instant:

```rust
pub async fn export_with_caching(
    client: &Client,
    metadata: &FicMetadata,
    config: &Config,
) -> Result<PathBuf, ExportError> {
    // Check if chapters are cached
    let cache_key = format!("chapters:{}", metadata.url_id);
    let cached_chapters = load_from_cache(&cache_key, config).await?;

    let chapters = if let Some(chapters) = cached_chapters {
        tracing::info!(
            url_id = %metadata.url_id,
            chapters = chapters.len(),
            "Using cached chapters"
        );
        chapters
    } else {
        // Fetch chapters
        let chapter_urls = generate_chapter_urls(metadata);
        let chapters = fetch_chapters_parallel(client, &chapter_urls, 5).await?;

        // Cache for next time
        save_to_cache(&cache_key, &chapters, config).await?;

        chapters
    };

    // Generate EPUB
    create_epub(metadata, &chapters, config)
}
```

## Export Progress Tracking

Track export progress for UI feedback:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct ExportProgress {
    pub stage: String,
    pub progress: f32,  // 0.0 to 1.0
    pub message: String,
}

impl ExportProgress {
    pub fn starting() -> Self {
        Self {
            stage: "initializing".into(),
            progress: 0.0,
            message: "Starting export...".into(),
        }
    }

    pub fn scraping(progress: f32, chapter: i32, total: i32) -> Self {
        Self {
            stage: "scraping".into(),
            progress: 0.1 + progress * 0.6,  // 10-70%
            message: format!("Fetching chapter {}/{}", chapter, total),
        }
    }

    pub fn generating(progress: f32) -> Self {
        Self {
            stage: "generating".into(),
            progress: 0.7 + progress * 0.2,  // 70-90%
            message: "Generating EPUB...".into(),
        }
    }

    pub fn complete(path: &PathBuf) -> Self {
        Self {
            stage: "complete".into(),
            progress: 1.0,
            message: format!("Export complete: {}", path.display()),
        }
    }
}
```

## Export Queue for Background Processing

For large exports, use a background queue:

```rust
pub struct ExportQueue {
    tx: mpsc::Sender<ExportJob>,
}

struct ExportJob {
    url: String,
    callback: oneshot::Sender<Result<PathBuf, ExportError>>,
}

impl ExportQueue {
    pub fn new(worker_count: usize) -> Self {
        let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel(100);
        let rx = Arc::new(tokio::sync::Mutex::new(rx));

        for i in 0..worker_count {
            let rx = rx.clone();
            tokio::spawn(async move {
                Self::worker(i, rx).await;
            });
        }

        Self { tx }
    }

    async fn worker(id: usize, rx: Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<mpsc::Receiver<ExportJob>>>) {
        loop {
            let job = {
                let mut rx = rx.lock().await;
                rx.recv().await
            };

            match job {
                Some(job) => {
                    tracing::info!(worker = id, url = %job.url, "Processing export job");
                    let result = process_export(&job.url).await;
                    let _ = job.callback.send(result);
                }
                None => break,
            }
        }
    }

    pub async fn submit(&self, url: String) -> Result<PathBuf, ExportError> {
        let (callback_tx, callback_rx) = oneshot::channel();

        self.tx.send(ExportJob {
            url,
            callback: callback_tx,
        }).await.map_err(|_| ExportError::BuildError("queue full".into()))?;

        callback_rx.await.map_err(|_| ExportError::BuildError("worker died".into()))?
    }
}
```

# Chapter 31 Deep Dive: SvelteKit Advanced Patterns

## Data Loading Strategies

SvelteKit offers multiple ways to load data. Understanding when to use each is crucial.

### Client-Side Loading (+page.ts)

```typescript
// src/routes/search/+page.ts
import type { PageLoad } from './$types';
import { searchFics } from '$lib/api/client';

export const load: PageLoad = async ({ url }) => {
  const query = url.searchParams.get('q') || '';

  // This runs in the browser (SPA mode)
  const results = await searchFics(url.searchParams);

  return {
    query,
    results,
  };
};
```

**When to use:** Client-side loading is appropriate for:
- Dynamic content that changes frequently
- Data that requires authentication
- Pages where SEO doesn't matter (SPA mode)

### Server-Side Loading (+page.server.ts)

```typescript
// src/routes/blog/[slug]/+page.server.ts
import type { PageServerLoad } from './$types';
import { error } from '@sveltejs/kit';

export const load: PageServerLoad = async ({ params, fetch }) => {
  const response = await fetch(`/api/posts/${params.slug}`);

  if (!response.ok) {
    error(404, 'Post not found');
  }

  const post = await response.json();

  return {
    post,
  };
};
```

**When to use:** Server-side loading is appropriate for:
- Public content that needs SEO
- Data from external APIs
- Pages that should work without JavaScript

### Layout Loading (+layout.ts)

```typescript
// src/routes/+layout.ts
import type { LayoutLoad } from './$types';

export const load: LayoutLoad = async ({ fetch }) => {
  // Load data shared across all pages
  const tagsResponse = await fetch('/api/v0/tags');
  const tags = await tagsResponse.json();

  return {
    tags,
  };
};
```

**When to use:** Layout loading is appropriate for:
- Navigation data (menus, sidebars)
- User authentication state
- Theme preferences

## Form Actions

SvelteKit provides built-in form handling:

```typescript
// src/routes/login/+page.server.ts
import type { Actions } from './$types';
import { fail, redirect } from '@sveltejs/kit';

export const actions: Actions = {
  default: async ({ request, cookies }) => {
    const data = await request.formData();
    const email = data.get('email');
    const password = data.get('password');

    // Validate
    if (!email || !password) {
      return fail(400, { email, error: 'Missing fields' });
    }

    // Authenticate
    const user = await authenticateUser(email, password);
    if (!user) {
      return fail(400, { email, error: 'Invalid credentials' });
    }

    // Set session cookie
    cookies.set('session', user.sessionToken, {
      path: '/',
      httpOnly: true,
      sameSite: 'lax',
      maxAge: 60 * 60 * 24 * 7, // 1 week
    });

    redirect(302, '/dashboard');
  }
};
```

## Reactive Store Integration

Connect Svelte 5 runes with stores:

```typescript
// src/lib/stores/search.ts
import { writable, derived } from 'svelte/store';

interface SearchState {
  query: string;
  filters: SearchFilters;
  results: SearchResult[];
  loading: boolean;
  error: string | null;
}

function createSearchStore() {
  const { subscribe, update, set } = writable<SearchState>({
    query: '',
    filters: defaultFilters,
    results: [],
    loading: false,
    error: null,
  });

  return {
    subscribe,

    setQuery(query: string) {
      update(state => ({ ...state, query }));
    },

    setFilters(filters: Partial<SearchFilters>) {
      update(state => ({
        ...state,
        filters: { ...state.filters, ...filters },
      }));
    },

    async search() {
      update(state => ({ ...state, loading: true, error: null }));

      try {
        const state = get({ subscribe });
        const params = new URLSearchParams({ q: state.query });
        const response = await fetch(`/api/v0/search?${params}`);
        const results = await response.json();

        update(state => ({
          ...state,
          results: results.results,
          loading: false,
        }));
      } catch (e) {
        update(state => ({
          ...state,
          error: e instanceof Error ? e.message : 'Search failed',
          loading: false,
        }));
      }
    },
  };
}

export const searchStore = createSearchStore();

// Derived store for filtered results
export const filteredResults = derived(
  searchStore,
  ($search) => $search.results.filter(r => r.words > $search.filters.min_words)
);
```

# Chapter 35 Deep Dive: Svelte 5 Advanced Patterns

## State Machines with Runes

Model complex state transitions:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  type DownloadState =
    | { status: 'idle' }
    | { status: 'validating'; url: string }
    | { status: 'downloading'; url: string; progress: number }
    | { status: 'complete'; url: string; downloadUrl: string }
    | { status: 'error'; message: string };

  let state = $state<DownloadState>({ status: 'idle' });

  async function startDownload(url: string) {
    state = { status: 'validating', url };

    // Validate URL
    if (!isValidUrl(url)) {
      state = { status: 'error', message: 'Invalid URL' };
      return;
    }

    state = { status: 'downloading', url, progress: 0 };

    try {
      const result = await fetchExport(url);
      state = {
        status: 'complete',
        url,
        downloadUrl: result.epub_url || '',
      };
    } catch (e) {
      state = {
        status: 'error',
        message: e instanceof Error ? e.message : 'Download failed',
      };
    }
  }

  function reset() {
    state = { status: 'idle' };
  }
</script>

{#if state.status === 'idle'}
  <input bind:value={url} placeholder="Enter URL" />
  <button onclick={() => startDownload(url)}>Download</button>

{:else if state.status === 'validating'}
  <p>Validating URL...</p>

{:else if state.status === 'downloading'}
  <p>Downloading... {state.progress}%</p>
  <progress value={state.progress} max="100"></progress>

{:else if state.status === 'complete'}
  <p>Download complete!</p>
  <a href={state.downloadUrl} download>Download EPUB</a>
  <button onclick={reset}>Download Another</button>

{:else if state.status === 'error'}
  <p class="error">{state.message}</p>
  <button onclick={reset}>Try Again</button>
{/if}
```

# Chapter 37 Deep Dive: Search Implementation

## Full-Text Search Backend

Implement PostgreSQL full-text search in Axum:

```rust
pub async fn search_handler(
    Query(params): Query<SearchParams>,
    State(state): State<Arc<AppState>>,
) -> Result<Json<Value>, AppError> {
    let query = params.q.unwrap_or_default();
    let page = params.page.unwrap_or(1).max(1);
    let per_page = params.per_page.unwrap_or(20).min(state.config.search_max_per_page);
    let offset = (page - 1) * per_page;

    // Build dynamic query
    let mut sql = String::from(
        "SELECT *, ts_rank(to_tsvector('english', title || ' ' || author), plainto_tsquery('english', $1)) as rank
         FROM fic_info
         WHERE to_tsvector('english', title || ' ' || author) @@ plainto_tsquery('english', $1)"
    );

    let mut count_sql = String::from(
        "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fic_info
         WHERE to_tsvector('english', title || ' ' || author) @@ plainto_tsquery('english', $1)"
    );

    // Add filters
    let mut filter_params: Vec<Box<dyn sqlx::Encode<'_, sqlx::Postgres> + Send>> = vec![];
    let mut param_index = 2;

    if let Some(min_words) = params.min_words {
        sql.push_str(&format!(" AND words >= ${}", param_index));
        count_sql.push_str(&format!(" AND words >= ${}", param_index));
        param_index += 1;
    }

    if let Some(complete) = params.complete {
        sql.push_str(&format!(" AND complete = ${}", param_index));
        count_sql.push_str(&format!(" AND complete = ${}", param_index));
        param_index += 1;
    }

    // Add ordering and pagination
    sql.push_str(&format!(" ORDER BY rank DESC LIMIT ${} OFFSET ${}", param_index, param_index + 1));

    // Execute query
    let results = sqlx::query_as::<_, FicInfo>(&sql)
        .bind(&query)
        .bind(per_page as i64)
        .bind(offset as i64)
        .fetch_all(&state.db)
        .await?;

    let total: i64 = sqlx::query_scalar(&count_sql)
        .bind(&query)
        .fetch_one(&state.db)
        .await?;

    Ok(Json(json!({
        "total": total,
        "page": page,
        "per_page": per_page,
        "results": results,
    })))
}
```

## Search Result Ranking

Implement custom ranking for better search results:

```rust
fn compute_rank(fic: &FicInfo, query: &str, weights: &RankWeights) -> f64 {
    let mut score = 0.0;

    // Title match (highest weight)
    if fic.title.to_lowercase().contains(&query.to_lowercase()) {
        score += weights.title_match;
    }

    // Author match
    if fic.author.to_lowercase().contains(&query.to_lowercase()) {
        score += weights.author_match;
    }

    // Word count factor (prefer longer stories)
    let word_factor = (fic.words as f64).log10() / 6.0; // Normalize to 0-1
    score += weights.word_count * word_factor.min(1.0);

    // Completion bonus
    if fic.complete {
        score += weights.completion_bonus;
    }

    // Recency bonus (newer stories get a small boost)
    let age_days = (chrono::Utc::now() - fic.updated_at).num_days() as f64;
    let recency = 1.0 / (1.0 + age_days / 365.0);
    score += weights.recency * recency;

    score
}

struct RankWeights {
    title_match: f64,
    author_match: f64,
    word_count: f64,
    completion_bonus: f64,
    recency: f64,
}

impl Default for RankWeights {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            title_match: 10.0,
            author_match: 5.0,
            word_count: 2.0,
            completion_bonus: 1.0,
            recency: 0.5,
        }
    }
}
```

## Search Suggestions

Implement autocomplete suggestions:

```rust
pub async fn search_suggestions(
    Query(params): Query<HashMap<String, String>>,
    State(state): State<Arc<AppState>>,
) -> Result<Json<Value>, AppError> {
    let query = params.get("q").unwrap_or(&String::new());

    if query.len() < 2 {
        return Ok(Json(json!({"suggestions": []})));
    }

    // Search for matching titles
    let title_suggestions = sqlx::query_scalar::<_, String>(
        r#"
        SELECT DISTINCT title FROM fic_info
        WHERE title ILIKE $1
        ORDER BY length(title)
        LIMIT 5
        "#,
    )
    .bind(format!("%{}%", query))
    .fetch_all(&state.db)
    .await?;

    // Search for matching authors
    let author_suggestions = sqlx::query_scalar::<_, String>(
        r#"
        SELECT DISTINCT author FROM fic_info
        WHERE author ILIKE $1
        ORDER BY length(author)
        LIMIT 5
        "#,
    )
    .bind(format!("%{}%", query))
    .fetch_all(&state.db)
    .await?;

    // Search for matching tags
    let tag_suggestions = sqlx::query_scalar::<_, String>(
        r#"
        SELECT DISTINCT name FROM tags
        WHERE name ILIKE $1
        ORDER BY length(name)
        LIMIT 5
        "#,
    )
    .bind(format!("%{}%", query))
    .fetch_all(&state.db)
    .await?;

    Ok(Json(json!({
        "titles": title_suggestions,
        "authors": author_suggestions,
        "tags": tag_suggestions,
    })))
}
```

# Chapter 8 Deep Dive: Advanced Database Patterns

## Database Migrations in Practice

### Schema Evolution

As your application grows, your database schema will evolve. Here's how to handle common migrations:

#### Adding a Column

```sql
-- Migration 005: Add reading time estimate
ALTER TABLE fic_info ADD COLUMN estimated_reading_time INTEGER;

-- Backfill existing data
UPDATE fic_info
SET estimated_reading_time = CEIL(words / 250.0)::INTEGER
WHERE estimated_reading_time IS NULL;

-- Add NOT NULL constraint after backfill
ALTER TABLE fic_info ALTER COLUMN estimated_reading_time SET NOT NULL;
ALTER TABLE fic_info ALTER COLUMN estimated_reading_time SET DEFAULT 0;
```

#### Renaming a Column (Zero-Downtime)

```sql
-- Step 1: Add new column
ALTER TABLE fic_info ADD COLUMN story_url TEXT;

-- Step 2: Copy data
UPDATE fic_info SET story_url = url WHERE story_url IS NULL;

-- Step 3: Add trigger to keep columns in sync
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION sync_url_columns()
RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
BEGIN
    IF TG_OP = 'INSERT' OR TG_OP = 'UPDATE' THEN
        IF NEW.url IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.url THEN
            NEW.story_url := NEW.url;
        END IF;
        IF NEW.story_url IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.story_url THEN
            NEW.url := NEW.story_url;
        END IF;
    END IF;
    RETURN NEW;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

CREATE TRIGGER sync_url_columns
    BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON fic_info
    FOR EACH ROW
    EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_url_columns();

-- Step 4: Update application code to use new column
-- Step 5: Drop old column (in a later migration)
```

#### Creating a Materialized View

```sql
-- Create a materialized view for expensive queries
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW fic_stats AS
SELECT
    f.url_id,
    f.title,
    f.author,
    f.words,
    f.chapters,
    f.complete,
    f.source,
    COUNT(DISTINCT e.id) as download_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT ft.tag_id) as tag_count,
    MAX(e.created_at) as last_downloaded
FROM fic_info f
LEFT JOIN export_log e ON f.url_id = e.url_id
LEFT JOIN fic_tags ft ON f.url_id = ft.fic_url_id
GROUP BY f.url_id, f.title, f.author, f.words, f.chapters, f.complete, f.source;

-- Refresh the view periodically
REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY fic_stats;

-- Create an index on the materialized view
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_fic_stats_url_id ON fic_stats(url_id);
```

### Query Optimization Techniques

#### Using EXPLAIN ANALYZE

```sql
-- Before optimization
EXPLAIN ANALYZE
SELECT f.title, f.author, f.words
FROM fic_info f
WHERE f.tags @> '["harry potter"]'::jsonb
AND f.words > 50000
ORDER BY f.words DESC
LIMIT 20;

-- Output shows sequential scan on 100k rows (slow!)
-- Seq Scan on fic_info  (cost=0.00..12345.67 rows=500 width=123)
--   Filter: (tags @> ...) AND (words > 50000)
--   Rows Removed by Filter: 95000

-- After adding GIN index on tags
CREATE INDEX idx_fic_tags_gin ON fic_info USING gin(tags);

-- Now the query uses the index
-- Index Scan using idx_fic_tags_gin on fic_info  (cost=0.25..123.45 rows=500 width=123)
```

#### Batch Operations

```rust
// Instead of individual inserts, use batch operations
pub async fn batch_insert_tags(
    pool: &PgPool,
    fic_url_id: &str,
    tag_names: &[String],
) -> Result<(), sqlx::Error> {
    for chunk in tag_names.chunks(100) {
        sqlx::query(
            r#"
            INSERT INTO tags (name, type)
            SELECT unnest($1::text[]), 'freeform'::tag_type
            ON CONFLICT (name) DO NOTHING
            "#,
        )
        .bind(chunk)
        .execute(pool)
        .await?;

        // Link tags to fic
        sqlx::query(
            r#"
            INSERT INTO fic_tags (fic_url_id, tag_id)
            SELECT $1, t.id
            FROM tags t
            WHERE t.name = ANY($2::text[])
            ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
            "#,
        )
        .bind(fic_url_id)
        .bind(chunk)
        .execute(pool)
        .await?;
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

#### Connection Pool Monitoring

```rust
pub async fn monitor_pool(pool: &PgPool) -> Result<(), sqlx::Error> {
    let stats = pool.options().get_stats();

    tracing::info!(
        active = stats.active_connections,
        idle = stats.idle_connections,
        max = stats.max_connections,
        "Pool statistics"
    );

    // Check for connection leaks
    if stats.active_connections > stats.max_connections * 80 / 100 {
        tracing::warn!(
            active = stats.active_connections,
            max = stats.max_connections,
            "Connection pool usage above 80%"
        );
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

# Chapter 22 Deep Dive: Database Performance

## Indexing Strategies

### When to Add an Index

```sql
-- Rule of thumb: Add an index when:
-- 1. A column is used in WHERE clauses frequently
-- 2. A column is used in JOIN conditions
-- 3. A column is used in ORDER BY or GROUP BY
-- 4. The table has more than 10,000 rows
-- 5. The query scans more than 10% of the table

-- Example: FicHub's fic_info table
-- Frequently queried columns:
--   url_id (primary key - already indexed)
--   title (ILIKE searches)
--   author (ILIKE searches)
--   words (range queries)
--   complete (boolean filter)
--   source (enum filter)
--   updated_at (sorting)

-- Add indexes for common queries
CREATE INDEX idx_fic_title_gin ON fic_info USING gin(to_tsvector('english', title));
CREATE INDEX idx_fic_author_gin ON fic_info USING gin(to_tsvector('english', author));
CREATE INDEX idx_fic_words ON fic_info(words);
CREATE INDEX idx_fic_complete ON fic_info(complete);
CREATE INDEX idx_fic_source ON fic_info(source);
CREATE INDEX idx_fic_updated_at ON fic_info(updated_at DESC);
```

### Index Types

```sql
-- B-tree (default): Good for equality and range queries
CREATE INDEX idx_fic_words ON fic_info(words);
-- Used for: WHERE words > 50000, WHERE words BETWEEN 10000 AND 100000

-- GIN (Generalized Inverted Index): Good for full-text search and JSONB
CREATE INDEX idx_fic_tags ON fic_info USING gin(tags);
-- Used for: WHERE tags @> '["harry potter"]'

-- GiST (Generalized Search Tree): Good for geometric data and range types
CREATE INDEX idx_fic_location ON stories USING gist(location);
-- Used for: WHERE location @> point '(1,1)'

-- BRIN (Block Range Index): Good for naturally ordered data
CREATE INDEX idx_fic_created ON fic_info USING brin(created_at);
-- Used for: Large tables with time-ordered data

-- Partial indexes: Index only rows matching a condition
CREATE INDEX idx_fic_complete ON fic_info(url_id)
WHERE complete = true;
-- Smaller index, faster queries for complete stories
```

### Index Maintenance

```sql
-- Check index usage
SELECT
    indexrelname,
    idx_scan,
    idx_tup_read,
    idx_tup_fetch,
    pg_size_pretty(pg_relation_size(indexrelid)) as index_size
FROM pg_stat_user_indexes
WHERE schemaname = 'public'
ORDER BY idx_scan DESC;

-- Find unused indexes
SELECT
    indexrelname,
    idx_scan,
    pg_size_pretty(pg_relation_size(indexrelid)) as index_size
FROM pg_stat_user_indexes
WHERE idx_scan = 0
AND schemaname = 'public';

-- Rebuild bloated indexes
REINDEX INDEX idx_fic_title_gin;
REINDEX TABLE fic_info;

-- Check index bloat
SELECT
    indexname,
    pg_size_pretty(pg_relation_size(indexname::regclass)) as size,
    (SELECT reltuples::bigint FROM pg_class WHERE oid = indexname::regclass) as estimated_rows
FROM pg_indexes
WHERE tablename = 'fic_info';
```

### Batch Operations

```rust
// Efficient batch insert
pub async fn batch_upsert(
    pool: &PgPool,
    records: &[NewRecord],
) -> Result<u64, sqlx::Error> {
    let mut total_affected = 0u64;

    for chunk in records.chunks(1000) {
        let affected = sqlx::query(
            r#"
            INSERT INTO records (name, value, created_at)
            SELECT * FROM UNNEST($1::text[], $2::int[], $3::timestamptz[])
            ON CONFLICT (name) DO UPDATE SET
                value = EXCLUDED.value,
                updated_at = NOW()
            "#,
        )
        .bind(chunk.iter().map(|r| &r.name).collect::<Vec<_>>())
        .bind(chunk.iter().map(|r| r.value).collect::<Vec<_>>())
        .bind(chunk.iter().map(|r| r.created_at).collect::<Vec<_>>())
        .execute(pool)
        .await?
        .rows_affected();

        total_affected += affected;
    }

    Ok(total_affected)
}
```

## Input Sanitization

### SQL Injection Prevention

```rust
// Always use parameterized queries
pub async fn search_fics(
    pool: &PgPool,
    query: &str,
    min_words: Option<i32>,
) -> Result<Vec<FicInfo>, sqlx::Error> {
    // SAFE: parameterized query
    sqlx::query_as::<_, FicInfo>(
        r#"
        SELECT * FROM fic_info
        WHERE to_tsvector('english', title || ' ' || author)
            @@ plainto_tsquery('english', $1)
        AND ($2 IS NULL OR words >= $2)
        ORDER BY updated_at DESC
        "#,
    )
    .bind(query)
    .bind(min_words)
    .fetch_all(pool)
    .await
}

// NEVER do this!
pub fn dangerous_search(query: &str) -> String {
    format!("SELECT * FROM fic_info WHERE title ILIKE '%{}%'", query)
    // If query is: '; DROP TABLE fic_info; --
    // The result is a catastrophic SQL injection!
}
```

```rust
    ammonia::Builder::new()
```

### Path Traversal Prevention

```rust
fn safe_cache_path(url_id: &str, export_type: &str, cache_dir: &PathBuf) -> Result<PathBuf, AppError> {
    // Validate url_id doesn't contain path separators
    if url_id.contains('/') || url_id.contains('\') || url_id.contains("..") {
        return Err(AppError::BadRequest(-5, "invalid URL ID".into()));
    }

    // Validate export_type
    if !["epub", "html", "meta"].contains(&export_type) {
        return Err(AppError::BadRequest(-5, "invalid export type".into()));
    }

    let path = cache_dir.join(export_type).join(format!("{}.{}", url_id, export_type));

    // Ensure the resolved path is within the cache directory
    if !path.starts_with(cache_dir) {
        return Err(AppError::BadRequest(-5, "path traversal detected".into()));
    }

    Ok(path)
}
```

## Authentication and Authorization

### API Key Authentication

```rust
use axum::middleware::{self, Next};
use axum::extract::Request;
use axum::response::Response;

async fn api_key_middleware(
    State(state): State<Arc<AppState>>,
    request: Request,
    next: Next,
) -> Result<Response, AppError> {
    // Skip auth for public endpoints
    let path = request.uri().path();
    if path.starts_with("/api/v0/search")
        || path.starts_with("/api/v0/tags")
        || path.starts_with("/opds/")
    {
        return Ok(next.run(request).await);
    }

    // Check for API key
    let api_key = request.headers()
        .get("X-API-Key")
        .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok());

    match api_key {
        Some(key) if key == &state.config.api_key => {
            Ok(next.run(request).await)
        }
        _ => Err(AppError::Unauthorized("invalid API key".into())),
    }
}
```

### Rate Limiting per User

```rust
pub struct UserRateLimiter {
    redis: MultiplexedConnection,
}

impl UserRateLimiter {
    pub async fn check(
        &self,
        user_id: &str,
        endpoint: &str,
        limit: u32,
        window: Duration,
    ) -> Result<bool, redis::RedisError> {
        let key = format!("ratelimit:{}:{}", user_id, endpoint);
        let now = std::time::SystemTime::now()
            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)?
            .as_secs();

        // Sliding window rate limiter
        let result: i32 = redis::Cmd::new()
            .arg("EVAL")
            .arg(RATE_LIMIT_SCRIPT)
            .arg(1)
            .arg(&key)
            .arg(now)
            .arg(window.as_secs())
            .arg(limit)
            .query_async(&mut self.redis.clone())
            .await?;

        Ok(result == 1)
    }
}
```

```rust
fn get_database_url() -> Result<String, ConfigError> {
    let url = std::env::var("DATABASE_URL")
        .map_err(|_| ConfigError::MissingVar("DATABASE_URL"))?;

    // Validate URL format
    if !url.starts_with("postgres://") && !url.starts_with("postgresql://") {
        return Err(ConfigError::InvalidUrl("DATABASE_URL must be a PostgreSQL URL".into()));
    }

    Ok(url)

// Best: With secret detection
fn load_secret(name: &str) -> Result<String, ConfigError> {
    let value = std::env::var(name)
        .map_err(|_| ConfigError::MissingVar(name))?;

    // Check if the value looks like it was accidentally committed
    if value.contains("password") || value.contains("secret") {
        tracing::warn!(
            var = name,
            "Secret variable contains suspicious keywords — verify it's not a placeholder"
        );
    }

    Ok(value)
}
```

## Security Headers

```rust
async fn security_headers(
    request: Request,
    next: Next,
) -> Response {
    let mut response = next.run(request).await;

    let headers = response.headers_mut();

    // Prevent MIME type sniffing
    headers.insert(
        "X-Content-Type-Options",
        "nosniff".parse().unwrap(),
    );

    // Prevent clickjacking
    headers.insert(
        "X-Frame-Options",
        "DENY".parse().unwrap(),
    );

    // Enable XSS protection
    headers.insert(
        "X-XSS-Protection",
        "1; mode=block".parse().unwrap(),
    );

    // Strict transport security (HTTPS only)
    headers.insert(
        "Strict-Transport-Security",
        "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains".parse().unwrap(),
    );

    // Content Security Policy
    headers.insert(
        "Content-Security-Policy",
        "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'".parse().unwrap(),
    );

    // Referrer policy
    headers.insert(
        "Referrer-Policy",
        "strict-origin-when-cross-origin".parse().unwrap(),
    );

    response
}
```

```rust
    State(state): State<Arc<AppState>>,
) -> Json<Value> {
    let mut checks = HashMap::new();

    // Database check
    let db_ok = sqlx::query("SELECT 1")
        .execute(&state.db)
        .await
        .is_ok();
    checks.insert("database", db_ok);

    // Redis check
    let redis_ok = redis::cmd("PING")
        .query_async::<String>(&mut state.redis.clone())
        .await

    checks.insert("redis", redis_ok);

    let all_healthy = checks.values().all(|&v| v);

        "checks": checks,
        "version": env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"),
        "uptime": start_time.elapsed().as_secs(),

}
```

# Chapter: Async Patterns in Rust

## Understanding the Tokio Runtime

Tokio is the async runtime that powers FicHub. Understanding how it works is crucial for writing efficient async code.

### The Executor Model

Tokio uses a work-stealing scheduler with a fixed thread pool:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              Tokio Runtime                   │
│                                             │
│  ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐      │
│  │Thread│ │Thread│ │Thread│ │Thread│      │
│  │  0   │ │  1   │ │  2   │ │  3   │      │
│  └──┬───┘ └──┬───┘ └──┬───┘ └──┬───┘      │
│     │        │        │        │            │
│     └────────┴────────┴────────┘            │
│                    │                        │
│              ┌─────┴─────┐                  │
│              │  Task Queue │                 │
│              └───────────┘                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

When you write `async fn`, Tokio doesn't execute it immediately. Instead, it creates a **task** that can be suspended and resumed. This is how thousands of concurrent connections can run on just 4 threads.

### How Async/Await Works

```rust
// This function doesn't execute immediately
async fn fetch_story(url: &str) -> Result<String, reqwest::Error> {
    // Tokio suspends here, allowing other tasks to run
    let response = reqwest::get(url).await?;

    // Tokio resumes here when the response arrives
    let body = response.text().await?;
    Ok(body)
}

// The .await points are where the function can be suspended
// Between .await points, other tasks can run
```

**Key insight:** An async function only runs until its first `.await` point. After that, it yields control back to the executor, which can run other tasks. When the awaited future completes, the executor resumes the function.

### Spawning Tasks

```rust
// Spawn a task that runs concurrently
let handle = tokio::spawn(async {
    // This runs on a separate task
    let result = fetch_story("https://example.com").await;
    result
});

// Do other work while the task runs
do_something_else().await;

// Wait for the spawned task to complete
let story = handle.await.unwrap();
```

### Join vs Spawn

```rust
// join! runs futures concurrently on the current task
let (metadata, chapters) = tokio::join!(
    fetch_metadata(&client, url),
    fetch_chapters(&client, url),
);

// spawn! creates a separate task on the thread pool
let handle = tokio::spawn(async move {
    fetch_metadata(&client, url).await
});
// Can do other work while spawned task runs
let metadata = handle.await.unwrap();
```

**When to use which:**
- `join!` — When you need both results before continuing
- `spawn!` — When the task can run independently (background work)

## Backpressure and Concurrency Control

### Semaphore for Concurrency Limits

```rust
use tokio::sync::Semaphore;

pub struct ConcurrencyLimiter {
    semaphore: Arc<Semaphore>,
}

impl ConcurrencyLimiter {
    pub fn new(max_concurrent: usize) -> Self {
        Self {
            semaphore: Arc::new(Semaphore::new(max_concurrent)),
        }
    }

    pub async fn run<F, T>(&self, operation: F) -> Result<T, Box<dyn std::error::Error>>
    where
        F: std::future::Future<Output = Result<T, Box<dyn std::error::Error>>>,
    {
        let _permit = self.semaphore.acquire().await?;
        operation.await
    }
}

// Usage: limit to 5 concurrent scrapes
let limiter = ConcurrencyLimiter::new(5);

let results: Vec<Result<String, _>> = urls
    .into_iter()
    .map(|url| {
        let limiter = limiter.clone();
        let client = client.clone();
        async move {
            limiter.run(async {
                let response = client.get(&url).send().await?;
                let body = response.text().await?;
                Ok(body)
            }).await
        }
    })
    .collect::<futures::stream::FuturesUnordered<_>>()
    .collect()
    .await;
```

### Rate Limiting with Token Buckets

```rust
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
use tokio::sync::Mutex;

pub struct TokenBucket {
    tokens: f64,
    max_tokens: f64,
    refill_rate: f64, // tokens per second
    last_refill: Instant,
}

impl TokenBucket {
    pub fn new(max_tokens: f64, refill_rate: f64) -> Self {
        Self {
            tokens: max_tokens,
            max_tokens,
            refill_rate,
            last_refill: Instant::now(),
        }
    }

    pub fn try_acquire(&mut self) -> bool {
        self.refill();

        if self.tokens >= 1.0 {
            self.tokens -= 1.0;
            true
        } else {
            false
        }
    }

    pub fn wait_time(&self) -> Duration {
        if self.tokens >= 1.0 {
            Duration::ZERO
        } else {
            Duration::from_secs_f64((1.0 - self.tokens) / self.refill_rate)
        }
    }

    fn refill(&mut self) {
        let now = Instant::now();
        let elapsed = now.duration_since(self.last_refill).as_secs_f64();
        self.tokens = (self.tokens + elapsed * self.refill_rate).min(self.max_tokens);
        self.last_refill = now;
    }
}
```

### Graceful Shutdown

```rust
use tokio::signal;

pub async fn run_server(config: Config) {
    let app = build_router(state).await;
    let listener = TcpListener::bind("0.0.0.0:3000").await.unwrap();

    // Run server until shutdown signal
    let server = axum::serve(listener, app);

    // Wait for Ctrl+C
    let shutdown = signal::ctrl_c();

    tokio::select! {
        _ = server => {
            tracing::info!("Server stopped");
        }
        _ = shutdown => {
            tracing::info!("Shutdown signal received, stopping gracefully...");
            // Perform cleanup here
            // - Close database connections
            // - Flush Redis
            // - Wait for in-flight requests
        }
    }
}
```

### Cancellation Safety

```rust
// This is NOT cancellation safe!
async fn process_items(items: Vec<Item>) {
    for item in items {
        // If this task is cancelled during process_item,
        // the item is lost!
        process_item(&item).await;
    }
}

// This IS cancellation safe
async fn process_items_safe(items: Vec<Item>) {
    let mut processed = 0;
    for item in items {
        process_item(&item).await;
        processed += 1;
        // If cancelled here, we know exactly which items were processed
    }
}
```

# Chapter: Advanced Rust Patterns for Web Services

## Ownership Deep Dive

### Lifetimes in Handler Functions

```rust
// This function borrows data from the request
async fn handler(
    State(state): State<Arc<AppState>>,
    Query(params): Query<HashMap<String, String>>,
) -> Result<Json<Value>, AppError> {
    // params is owned by the handler
    // state is borrowed (via Arc)

    let url = params.get("url")
        .ok_or_else(|| AppError::BadRequest(-1, "no query".into()))?;

    // url borrows from params
    // When handler returns, params (and url) are dropped
}
```

### Smart Pointers

```rust
// Box<T> — Heap allocation, single owner
let boxed: Box<dyn SiteScraper> = Box::new(Ao3Scraper);

// Arc<T> — Atomic reference counting, shared ownership
let shared: Arc<AppState> = Arc::new(state);

// Rc<T> — Reference counting, single-threaded only
let rc: Rc<RefCell<Vec<String>>> = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Vec::new()));

// Mutex<T> — Mutual exclusion
let mutex: Mutex<HashMap<String, String>> = Mutex::new(HashMap::new());

// RwLock<T> — Read-write lock (multiple readers OR one writer)
let rw: RwLock<Vec<String>> = RwLock::new(Vec::new());
```

### When to Use Each

| Type | Use Case | Thread Safe |
|------|----------|-------------|
| `Box<T>` | Single owner, heap allocation | No (but can be `Send`) |
| `Arc<T>` | Shared immutable state | Yes |
| `Rc<T>` | Shared state, single thread | No |
| `Mutex<T>` | Shared mutable state | Yes |
| `RwLock<T>` | Read-heavy shared state | Yes |

## Trait Objects and Dynamic Dispatch

### The ScraperRegistry Pattern

```rust
// Define the trait
#[async_trait]
pub trait SiteScraper: Send + Sync {
    fn can_handle(&self, url: &str) -> bool;
    async fn lookup(&self, client: &Client, url: &str) -> Result<FicMetadata, ScrapeError>;
    async fn fetch_chapters(&self, client: &Client, metadata: &FicMetadata) -> Result<Vec<Chapter>, ScrapeError>;
}

// Store as trait objects
pub struct ScraperRegistry {
    scrapers: Vec<Box<dyn SiteScraper>>,
}

// Dynamic dispatch: find the right scraper at runtime
pub fn find_scraper(&self, url: &str) -> Option<&dyn SiteScraper> {
    self.scrapers.iter()
        .find(|s| s.can_handle(url))
        .map(|s| s.as_ref())
}
```

### Static vs Dynamic Dispatch

```rust
// Static dispatch (monomorphized — faster, larger binary)
fn process_scraper<S: SiteScraper>(scraper: &S, url: &str) {
    scraper.can_handle(url);
}

// Dynamic dispatch (vtable lookup — slower, smaller binary)
fn process_scraper_dyn(scraper: &dyn SiteScraper, url: &str) {
    scraper.can_handle(url);
}

// When to use which:
// - Static: hot paths, performance-critical code
// - Dynamic: when you need heterogeneous collections
```

## Builder Pattern

### Configuration Builder

```rust
pub struct ServerConfigBuilder {
    host: String,
    port: u16,
    max_connections: usize,
    timeout: Duration,
    cors_origins: Vec<String>,
}

impl ServerConfigBuilder {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            host: "0.0.0.0".to_string(),
            port: 3000,
            max_connections: 100,
            timeout: Duration::from_secs(30),
            cors_origins: vec![],
        }
    }

    pub fn host(mut self, host: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.host = host.into();
        self
    }

    pub fn port(mut self, port: u16) -> Self {
        self.port = port;
        self
    }

    pub fn max_connections(mut self, max: usize) -> Self {
        self.max_connections = max;
        self
    }

    pub fn timeout(mut self, timeout: Duration) -> Self {
        self.timeout = timeout;
        self
    }

    pub fn allow_origin(mut self, origin: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.cors_origins.push(origin.into());
        self
    }

    pub fn build(self) -> ServerConfig {
        ServerConfig {
            host: self.host,
            port: self.port,
            max_connections: self.max_connections,
            timeout: self.timeout,
            cors_origins: self.cors_origins,
        }
    }
}

// Usage
let config = ServerConfigBuilder::new()
    .host("127.0.0.1")
    .port(8080)
    .max_connections(200)
    .timeout(Duration::from_secs(60))
    .allow_origin("https://example.com")
    .build();
```

```rust
    Generating { metadata: FicMetadata, chapters: Vec<Chapter> },
    Caching { path: PathBuf },
    Complete { path: PathBuf, duration: Duration },
    Error { message: String, retryable: bool },
}

impl ExportState {
    pub fn next(self) -> Self {
        match self {
            ExportState::Validating { url } => {
                if is_valid_url(&url) {
                    ExportState::Scraping { url, attempt: 1 }
                } else {
                    ExportState::Error {
                        message: "Invalid URL".into(),
                        retryable: false,
                    }
                }
            }
            ExportState::Scraping { url, attempt } if attempt < 3 => {
                // Try scraping
                ExportState::Scraping { url, attempt: attempt + 1 }
            }
            ExportState::Scraping { url, .. } => {
                ExportState::Error {
                    message: format!("Failed to scrape {}", url),
                    retryable: true,
                }
            }
            _ => self,
        }
    }
}
```

### Destructuring in Match Arms

```rust
enum ApiError {
    Network { url: String, status: u16 },
    Parse { url: String, message: String },
    Auth { realm: String },
}

fn handle_error(error: ApiError) {
    match error {
        ApiError::Network { url, status } if status == 404 => {
            println!("Not found: {}", url);
        }
        ApiError::Network { url, status } if status == 429 => {
            println!("Rate limited: {}", url);
        }
        ApiError::Network { url, status } => {
            println!("Network error: {} (status {})", url, status);
        }
        ApiError::Parse { url, message } => {
            println!("Parse error at {}: {}", url, message);
        }
        ApiError::Auth { realm } => {
            println!("Authentication required for realm: {}", realm);
        }
    }
}
```

## Concurrency Patterns

### Actor Pattern with Channels

```rust
use tokio::sync::mpsc;

pub struct ScraperActor {
    receiver: mpsc::Receiver<ScrapeCommand>,
    client: reqwest::Client,
    registry: Arc<ScraperRegistry>,
}

pub enum ScrapeCommand {
    Scrape {
        url: String,
        response: oneshot::Sender<Result<FicMetadata, ScrapeError>>,
    },
    Shutdown,
}

impl ScraperActor {
    pub fn new(
        client: reqwest::Client,
        registry: Arc<ScraperRegistry>,
    ) -> (Self, mpsc::Sender<ScrapeCommand>) {
        let (sender, receiver) = mpsc::channel(100);
        let actor = Self {
            receiver,
            client,
            registry,
        };
        (actor, sender)
    }

    pub async fn run(&mut self) {
        while let Some(command) = self.receiver.recv().await {
            match command {
                ScrapeCommand::Scrape { url, response } => {
                    let result = self.handle_scrape(&url).await;
                    let _ = response.send(result);
                }
                ScrapeCommand::Shutdown => {
                    tracing::info!("Scraper actor shutting down");
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    async fn handle_scrape(&self, url: &str) -> Result<FicMetadata, ScrapeError> {
        let scraper = self.registry.find_scraper(url)
            .ok_or_else(|| ScrapeError::UnsupportedSite(url.to_string()))?;

        scraper.lookup(&self.client, url).await
    }
}

// Usage
let (mut actor, sender) = ScraperActor::new(client, registry);
tokio::spawn(async move { actor.run().await });

// Send commands
let (response_tx, response_rx) = oneshot::channel();
sender.send(ScrapeCommand::Scrape {
    url: "https://archiveofourown.org/works/12345".into(),
    response: response_tx,
}).await.unwrap();

let result = response_rx.await.unwrap();
```

### Broadcast Channels for Event Distribution

```rust
use tokio::sync::broadcast;

pub struct EventBus {
    sender: broadcast::Sender<Event>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub enum Event {
    StoryExported { url_id: String },
    TagSubmitted { tag_id: i32 },
    RecommendationComputed { source: String },
}

impl EventBus {
    pub fn new(capacity: usize) -> Self {
        let (sender, _) = broadcast::channel(capacity);
        Self { sender }
    }

    pub fn publish(&self, event: Event) {
        let _ = self.sender.send(event);
    }

    pub fn subscribe(&self) -> broadcast::Receiver<Event> {
        self.sender.subscribe()
    }
}

// Usage
let bus = EventBus::new(100);

// Subscriber 1
let mut rx1 = bus.subscribe();
tokio::spawn(async move {
    while let Ok(event) = rx1.recv().await {
        match event {
            Event::StoryExported { url_id } => {
                println!("Story exported: {}", url_id);
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
});

// Subscriber 2
let mut rx2 = bus.subscribe();
tokio::spawn(async move {
    while let Ok(event) = rx2.recv().await {
        match event {
            Event::TagSubmitted { tag_id } => {
                println!("Tag submitted: {}", tag_id);
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
});

// Publish events
bus.publish(Event::StoryExported {
    url_id: "ao3-12345".into(),
});
```

# Chapter: Svelte 5 State Management Deep Dive

## Reactive State Patterns

### Nested Reactivity

Svelte 5 runes handle nested objects and arrays automatically:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  interface Story {
    id: string;
    title: string;
    author: string;
    tags: string[];
    metadata: {
      words: number;
      chapters: number;
      complete: boolean;
    };
  }

  let stories = $state<Story[]>([]);

  function addStory(story: Story) {
    stories.push(story); // Automatically triggers re-render
  }

  function updateWordCount(id: string, words: number) {
    const story = stories.find(s => s.id === id);
    if (story) {
      story.metadata.words = words; // Nested reactivity works!
    }
  }

  function removeTag(storyId: string, tag: string) {
    const story = stories.find(s => s.id === storyId);
    if (story) {
      story.tags = story.tags.filter(t => t !== tag); // Array mutation works!
    }
  }

  // Derived from nested state
  let totalWords = $derived(
    stories.reduce((sum, s) => sum + s.metadata.words, 0)
  );

  let completedStories = $derived(
    stories.filter(s => s.metadata.complete)
  );
</script>

<p>Total words: {totalWords.toLocaleString()}</p>
<p>Completed: {completedStories.length} / {stories.length}</p>
```

### State Machines with Runes

Model complex UI states:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  type DownloadState =
    | { status: 'idle' }
    | { status: 'validating'; url: string }
    | { status: 'downloading'; url: string; progress: number }
    | { status: 'complete'; result: DownloadResult }
    | { status: 'error'; message: string; retryable: boolean };

  let state = $state<DownloadState>({ status: 'idle' });
  let url = $state('');

  async function startDownload() {
    state = { status: 'validating', url };

    if (!isValidUrl(url)) {
      state = { status: 'error', message: 'Invalid URL', retryable: false };
      return;
    }

    state = { status: 'downloading', url, progress: 0 };

    try {
      // Simulate progress updates
      for (let i = 0; i <= 100; i += 10) {
        await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 100));
        state = { ...state, progress: i } as DownloadState;
      }

      const result = await fetchExport(url);
      state = { status: 'complete', result };
    } catch (e) {
      state = {
        status: 'error',
        message: e instanceof Error ? e.message : 'Download failed',
        retryable: true,
      };
    }
  }

  function retry() {
    if (state.status === 'error' && state.retryable) {
      startDownload();
    }
  }

  function reset() {
    state = { status: 'idle' };
    url = '';
  }
</script>

{#if state.status === 'idle'}
  <div class="input-group">
    <input bind:value={url} placeholder="Enter story URL" />
    <button onclick={startDownload} disabled={!url}>Download</button>
  </div>

{:else if state.status === 'validating'}
  <div class="loading">
    <p>Validating URL...</p>
  </div>

{:else if state.status === 'downloading'}
  <div class="progress">
    <p>Downloading... {state.progress}%</p>
    <progress value={state.progress} max="100"></progress>
  </div>

{:else if state.status === 'complete'}
  <div class="success">
    <h3>Download Complete!</h3>
    <p>{state.result.meta?.title} by {state.result.meta?.author}</p>
    <a href={state.result.epub_url} download class="btn">Download EPUB</a>
    <button onclick={reset}>Download Another</button>
  </div>

{:else if state.status === 'error'}
  <div class="error">
    <p>Error: {state.message}</p>
    {#if state.retryable}
      <button onclick={retry}>Retry</button>
    {/if}
    <button onclick={reset}>Try Different URL</button>
  </div>
{/if}
```

### Memoization with $derived

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  let items = $state<Item[]>([]);
  let filter = $state('');
  let sortField = $state<'name' | 'date' | 'size'>('name');

  // Memoized filtered and sorted list
  let processedItems = $derived(
    items
      .filter(item => item.name.toLowerCase().includes(filter.toLowerCase()))
      .sort((a, b) => {
        switch (sortField) {
          case 'name': return a.name.localeCompare(b.name);
          case 'date': return b.date - a.date;
          case 'size': return b.size - a.size;
        }
      })
  );

  // Memoized statistics
  let stats = $derived({
    total: items.length,
    filtered: processedItems.length,
    totalSize: processedItems.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.size, 0),
  });
</script>

<input bind:value={filter} placeholder="Filter items..." />

<p>Showing {stats.filtered} of {stats.total} items</p>

{#each processedItems as item (item.id)}
  <div class="item">{item.name}</div>
{/each}
```

### Virtual Scrolling for Large Lists

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { onMount } from 'svelte';

  let { items, itemHeight = 50, containerHeight = 400 } = $props();

  let scrollTop = $state(0);
  let container: HTMLDivElement;

  let startIndex = $derived(Math.floor(scrollTop / itemHeight));
  let endIndex = $derived(Math.min(
    startIndex + Math.ceil(containerHeight / itemHeight) + 1,
    items.length
  ));

  let visibleItems = $derived(
    items.slice(startIndex, endIndex).map((item, i) => ({
      ...item,
      top: (startIndex + i) * itemHeight,
    }))
  );

  let totalHeight = $derived(items.length * itemHeight);

  function handleScroll(e: Event) {
    scrollTop = (e.target as HTMLDivElement).scrollTop;
  }
</script>

<div
  bind:this={container}
  class="virtual-scroll"
  style="height: {containerHeight}px; overflow-y: auto;"
  onscroll={handleScroll}
>
  <div style="height: {totalHeight}px; position: relative;">
    {#each visibleItems as item (item.id)}
      <div
        class="virtual-item"
        style="position: absolute; top: {item.top}px; height: {itemHeight}px; width: 100%;"
      >
        {item.name}
      </div>
    {/each}
  </div>
</div>
```

# Chapter: Component Patterns Deep Dive

## Compound Components

Build complex components from simple, composable pieces:

```svelte
<!-- Accordion.svelte -->
<script lang="ts">
  import type { Snippet } from 'svelte';

  let {
    children,
    multiple = false,
  }: {
    children: Snippet;
    multiple?: boolean;
  } = $props();

  let openItems = $state<Set<number>>(new Set());

  function toggle(index: number) {
    if (multiple) {
      if (openItems.has(index)) {
        openItems.delete(index);
      } else {
        openItems.add(index);
      }
      openItems = openItems; // Trigger reactivity
    } else {
      openItems = openItems.has(index) ? new Set() : new Set([index]);
    }
  }

  // Provide context to child components
  import { setContext } from 'svelte';
  setContext('accordion', {
    openItems,
    toggle,
  });
</script>

<div class="accordion" role="region">
  {@render children()}
</div>

<!-- AccordionItem.svelte -->
<script lang="ts">
  import { getContext } from 'svelte';
  import type { Snippet } from 'svelte';

  let {
    title,
    index,
    children,
  }: {
    title: string;
    index: number;
    children: Snippet;
  } = $props();

  const { openItems, toggle } = getContext('accordion');
  let isOpen = $derived(openItems.has(index));
</script>

<div class="accordion-item" class:open={isOpen}>
  <button
    class="accordion-header"
    onclick={() => toggle(index)}
    aria-expanded={isOpen}
  >
    {title}
    <span class="chevron" class:rotated={isOpen}>▼</span>
  </button>

  {#if isOpen}
    <div class="accordion-content" role="region">
      {@render children()}
    </div>
  {/if}
</div>

<!-- Usage -->
<Accordion multiple={true}>
  <AccordionItem title="Chapter 1" index={0}>
    <p>Content for chapter 1...</p>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem title="Chapter 2" index={1}>
    <p>Content for chapter 2...</p>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
```

## Render Props Pattern

Pass rendering logic as props:

```svelte
<!-- DataList.svelte -->

  import type { Snippet } from 'svelte';

  let {
    data,
    renderItem,
    renderEmpty,
    keyFn,
  }: {
    data: any[];
    renderItem: Snippet<[any, number]>;
    renderEmpty?: Snippet;
    keyFn: (item: any) => string | number;
  } = $props();

{#if data.length === 0}

  {:else}

{:else}

      </li>
    {/each}

{/if}

  renderEmpty={emptyState}
>

</DataList>
```

Wrap components with additional functionality:
