# Chapter: Accessibility Patterns Deep Dive

## Keyboard Navigation

### Custom Keyboard Shortcuts

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { onMount, onDestroy } from 'svelte';

  let shortcuts = new Map([
    ['k', () => focusSearch()],
    ['d', () => startDownload()],
    ['Escape', () => clearSearch()],
  ]);

  function handleKeydown(event: KeyboardEvent) {
    // Don't trigger shortcuts when typing in inputs
    if (event.target instanceof HTMLInputElement || event.target instanceof HTMLTextAreaElement) {
      return;
    }

    const handler = shortcuts.get(event.key);
    if (handler) {
      event.preventDefault();
      handler();
    }
  }

  onMount(() => {
    window.addEventListener('keydown', handleKeydown);
  });

  onDestroy(() => {
    window.removeEventListener('keydown', handleKeydown);
  });

  let searchInput: HTMLInputElement;

  function focusSearch() {
    searchInput?.focus();
  }

  function startDownload() {
    // Trigger download
  }

  function clearSearch() {
    searchQuery = '';
    searchInput?.blur();
  }
</script>

<svelte:window on:keydown={handleKeydown} />

<input bind:this={searchInput} bind:value={searchQuery} placeholder="Search... (press K)" />
```

### Focus Management

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { tick } from 'svelte';

  let showModal = $state(false);
  let modalContent: HTMLDivElement;
  let previousFocus: HTMLElement | null = null;

  async function openModal() {
    previousFocus = document.activeElement as HTMLElement;
    showModal = true;
    await tick();
    modalContent?.focus();
  }

  function closeModal() {
    showModal = false;
    previousFocus?.focus();
  }

  function handleKeydown(event: KeyboardEvent) {
    if (event.key === 'Escape') {
      closeModal();
    }

    // Trap focus within modal
    if (event.key === 'Tab') {
      const focusable = modalContent?.querySelectorAll(
        'button, [href], input, select, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])'
      );
      if (!focusable?.length) return;

      const first = focusable[0] as HTMLElement;
      const last = focusable[focusable.length - 1] as HTMLElement;

      if (event.shiftKey && document.activeElement === first) {
        event.preventDefault();
        last.focus();
      } else if (!event.shiftKey && document.activeElement === last) {
        event.preventDefault();
        first.focus();
      }
    }
  }
</script>

<button onclick={openModal}>Open Modal</button>

{#if showModal}
  <div
    class="modal-overlay"
    onclick={closeModal}
    on:keydown={handleKeydown}
    role="dialog"
    aria-modal="true"
    aria-labelledby="modal-title"
  >
    <div
      class="modal-content"
      bind:this={modalContent}
      tabindex="-1"
      onclick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}
    >
      <h2 id="modal-title">Modal Title</h2>
      <p>Modal content goes here.</p>
      <button onclick={closeModal}>Close</button>
    </div>
  </div>
{/if}
```

## ARIA Patterns

### Live Regions for Dynamic Content

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  let searchResults = $state<SearchResult[]>([]);
  let loading = $state(false);
  let searchStatus = $state('');

  async function search(query: string) {
    loading = true;
    searchStatus = 'Searching...';

    try {
      const results = await searchFics(query);
      searchResults = results;
      searchStatus = `${results.length} results found`;
    } catch (e) {
      searchStatus = 'Search failed';
    } finally {
      loading = false;
    }
  }
</script>

<!-- Search input with live region -->

  <input
    id="search-input"
    type="search"
    oninput={(e) => search(e.target.value)}
    aria-describedby="search-status"
  />
  <div id="search-status" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true">
    {searchStatus}
  </div>
</div>

<!-- Results with proper ARIA -->

  <div role="region" aria-label="Search results">
    <h2 id="results-heading">Search Results</h2>
```

### Tablist Pattern

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  let activeTab = $state(0);
  let tabs = [
    { id: 'download', label: 'Download', icon: '📥' },
    { id: 'search', label: 'Search', icon: '🔍' },
    { id: 'recommendations', label: 'Recommendations', icon: '⭐' },
  ];

  function handleKeydown(event: KeyboardEvent, index: number) {
    switch (event.key) {
      case 'ArrowLeft':
        event.preventDefault();
        activeTab = Math.max(0, index - 1);
        focusTab(activeTab);
        break;
      case 'ArrowRight':
        event.preventDefault();
        activeTab = Math.min(tabs.length - 1, index + 1);
        focusTab(activeTab);
        break;
      case 'Home':
        event.preventDefault();
        activeTab = 0;
        focusTab(0);
        break;
      case 'End':
        event.preventDefault();
        activeTab = tabs.length - 1;
        focusTab(tabs.length - 1);
        break;
    }
  }

  function focusTab(index: number) {
    const tab = document.querySelector(`[role="tab"][data-index="${index}"]`) as HTMLElement;
    tab?.focus();
  }
</script>

<!-- Tab list -->
<div role="tablist" aria-label="Content sections">
  {#each tabs as tab, index}
    <button
      role="tab"
      id="tab-{tab.id}"
      data-index={index}
      aria-selected={activeTab === index}
      aria-controls="tabpanel-{tab.id}"
      tabindex={activeTab === index ? 0 : -1}
      onclick={() => activeTab = index}
      onkeydown={(e) => handleKeydown(e, index)}
    >
      <span aria-hidden="true">{tab.icon}</span>
      {tab.label}
    </button>
  {/each}
</div>

<!-- Tab panels -->
{#each tabs as tab, index}
  {#if activeTab === index}
    <div
      role="tabpanel"
      id="tabpanel-{tab.id}"
      aria-labelledby="tab-{tab.id}"
      tabindex="0"
    >
      {#if tab.id === 'download'}
        <DownloadTab />
      {:else if tab.id === 'search'}
        <SearchTab />
      {:else if tab.id === 'recommendations'}
        <RecommendationsTab />
      {/if}
    </div>
  {/if}
{/each}
```

## Screen Reader Optimization

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  let stories = $state<Story[]>([]);
  let sortField = $state<'title' | 'words' | 'date'>('title');
  let sortDirection = $state<'asc' | 'desc'>('asc');

  function toggleSort(field: typeof sortField) {
    if (sortField === field) {
      sortDirection = sortDirection === 'asc' ? 'desc' : 'asc';
    } else {
      sortField = field;
      sortDirection = 'asc';
    }
  }

  let sortedStories = $derived(
    [...stories].sort((a, b) => {
      const dir = sortDirection === 'asc' ? 1 : -1;
      switch (sortField) {
        case 'title': return dir * a.title.localeCompare(b.title);
        case 'words': return dir * (a.words - b.words);
        case 'date': return dir * (a.date - b.date);
      }
    })
  );

  let sortDescription = $derived(
    `Sorted by ${sortField}, ${sortDirection === 'asc' ? 'ascending' : 'descending'}`
  );
</script>

<!-- Visually hidden sort status for screen readers -->
<div class="sr-only" aria-live="polite">
  {sortDescription}. {stories.length} stories.
</div>

<!-- Sort controls with aria-sort -->
<div role="group" aria-label="Sort options">
  <button
    onclick={() => toggleSort('title')}
    aria-sort={sortField === 'title' ? sortDirection === 'asc' ? 'ascending' : 'descending' : 'none'}
  >
    Title {sortField === 'title' ? (sortDirection === 'asc' ? '↑' : '↓') : ''}
  </button>
  <button
    onclick={() => toggleSort('words')}
    aria-sort={sortField === 'words' ? sortDirection === 'asc' ? 'ascending' : 'descending' : 'none'}
  >
    Words {sortField === 'words' ? (sortDirection === 'asc' ? '↑' : '↓') : ''}
  </button>
</div>

<!-- Story list with proper semantics -->
<ul aria-label="Stories" aria-describedby="sort-status">
  {#each sortedStories as story (story.url_id)}
    <li>
      <article aria-labelledby="title-{story.url_id}">
        <h3 id="title-{story.url_id}">{story.title}</h3>
        <p>by {story.author}</p>
        <p>{story.words.toLocaleString()} words, {story.chapters} chapters</p>
        {#if story.complete}
          <span class="badge">Complete</span>
        {/if}
      </article>
    </li>
  {/each}
</ul>
```

## Property-Based Testing

Property-based testing generates random inputs and verifies properties hold true:

```rust
use proptest::preptest;

proptest! {
    #[test]
    fn test_slug_idempotent(input in ".*") {
        let slug1 = slugify(&input);
        let slug2 = slugify(&slug1);
        // Slugifying twice should give the same result
        prop_assert_eq!(slug1, slug2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_slug_no_uppercase(input in "[A-Z].*") {
        let slug = slugify(&input);
        // Slugs should never contain uppercase letters
        prop_assert!(!slug.chars().any(|c| c.is_uppercase()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_slug_no_spaces(input in ".*\s.*") {
        let slug = slugify(&input);
        // Slugs should never contain spaces
        prop_assert!(!slug.contains(' '));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_slug_alphanumeric(input in ".*") {
        let slug = slugify(&input);
        // Slugs should only contain alphanumeric chars and hyphens
        prop_assert!(slug.chars().all(|c| c.is_alphanumeric() || c == '-'));
    }
}
```

```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod async_tests {
    use super::*;
    use sqlx::PgPool;

    #[sqlx::test]
    async fn test_database_operations(pool: PgPool) {
        // Run migrations
        sqlx::migrate!("./migrations")
            .run(&pool)
            .await
            .expect("Failed to run migrations");

        // Test insert
        let url_id = "test-123";
        let title = "Test Story";
        let author = "Test Author";

        upsert_fic_info(&pool, url_id, title, author, 1000, 5, true, "test", &serde_json::json!([]))
            .await
            .expect("Failed to insert fic");

        // Test read
        let fic = get_fic_info(&pool, url_id)
            .await
            .expect("Failed to read fic")
            .expect("Fic not found");

        assert_eq!(fic.title, title);
        assert_eq!(fic.author, author);
        assert_eq!(fic.words, 1000);
        assert_eq!(fic.chapters, 5);
        assert!(fic.complete);

        // Test update
        upsert_fic_info(&pool, url_id, "Updated Title", author, 2000, 10, true, "test", &serde_json::json!(["updated"]))
            .await
            .expect("Failed to update fic");

        let fic = get_fic_info(&pool, url_id)
            .await
            .expect("Failed to read fic")
            .expect("Fic not found");

        assert_eq!(fic.title, "Updated Title");
        assert_eq!(fic.words, 2000);
    }

    #[sqlx::test]
    async fn test_concurrent_access(pool: PgPool) {
        sqlx::migrate!("./migrations")
            .run(&pool)
            .await
            .expect("Failed to run migrations");

        // Spawn multiple concurrent tasks
        let mut handles = Vec::new();

        for i in 0..10 {
            let pool = pool.clone();
            handles.push(tokio::spawn(async move {
                let url_id = format!("concurrent-{}", i);
                upsert_fic_info(&pool, &url_id, &format!("Story {}", i), "Author", 1000, 1, true, "test", &serde_json::json!([]))
                    .await
                    .expect("Failed to insert");

                let fic = get_fic_info(&pool, &url_id)
                    .await
                    .expect("Failed to read")
                    .expect("Not found");

                assert_eq!(fic.title, format!("Story {}", i));
            }));
        }

        // Wait for all tasks to complete
        for handle in handles {
            handle.await.expect("Task panicked");
        }

        // Verify all records exist
        let count: i64 = sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fic_info WHERE url_id LIKE 'concurrent-%'")
            .fetch_one(&pool)
            .await
            .unwrap();

        assert_eq!(count, 10);
    }
}
```

```rust
// tests/integration/mod.rs

// Shared test utilities
pub mod test_utils {
    use sqlx::PgPool;
    use std::sync::Mutex;

    static DB_MUTEX: Mutex<()> = Mutex::new(());

    pub async fn setup_test_db() -> PgPool {
        let _lock = DB_MUTEX.lock().unwrap();

        let database_url = std::env::var("TEST_DATABASE_URL")
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| "postgres://localhost/fichub_test".to_string());

        let pool = PgPool::connect(&database_url)
            .await
            .expect("Failed to connect to test database");

        // Create a unique schema for this test
        let schema_name = format!("test_{}", uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string().replace('-', ""));
        sqlx::query(&format!("CREATE SCHEMA {}", schema_name))
            .execute(&pool)
            .await
            .expect("Failed to create schema");

        sqlx::query(&format!("SET search_path TO {}", schema_name))
            .execute(&pool)
            .await
            .expect("Failed to set search path");

        // Run migrations
        sqlx::migrate!("./migrations")
            .run(&pool)
            .await
            .expect("Failed to run migrations");

        pool
    }

    pub async fn cleanup_test_db(pool: &PgPool, schema_name: &str) {
        sqlx::query(&format!("DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS {} CASCADE", schema_name))
            .execute(pool)
            .await
            .expect("Failed to drop schema");
    }
}
```

## Testing Search Syntax Parser

```typescript
// src/lib/search/syntax.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { parseSearchSyntax, tokensToQueryParams, defaultFilters } from './syntax';

describe('Search Syntax Parser', () => {
  describe('parseSearchSyntax', () => {
    it('parses bare words', () => {
      const tokens = parseSearchSyntax('harry potter');
      expect(tokens).toEqual([
        { type: 'word', value: 'harry' },
        { type: 'word', value: 'potter' },
      ]);
    });

    it('parses key:value pairs', () => {
      const tokens = parseSearchSyntax('author:jkr rating:t');
      expect(tokens).toEqual([
        { type: 'key_value', key: 'author', value: 'jkr' },
        { type: 'key_value', key: 'rating', value: 't' },
      ]);
    });

    it('parses quoted values', () => {
      const tokens = parseSearchSyntax('author:"JK Rowling"');
      expect(tokens).toEqual([
        { type: 'key_value', key: 'author', value: 'JK Rowling' },
      ]);
    });

    it('parses exclusions', () => {
      const tokens = parseSearchSyntax('harry potter -crossover');
      expect(tokens).toEqual([
        { type: 'word', value: 'harry' },
        { type: 'word', value: 'potter' },
        { type: 'exclusion', value: 'crossover' },
      ]);
    });

    it('parses ranges', () => {
      const tokens = parseSearchSyntax('words:50000..100000');
      expect(tokens).toEqual([
        { type: 'range', key: 'words', value: '50000..100000' },
      ]);
    });

    it('parses complex queries', () => {
      const tokens = parseSearchSyntax('author:"JK Rowling" words:10000..50000 complete:true -crossover');
      expect(tokens.length).toBe(4);
      expect(tokens[0]).toEqual({ type: 'key_value', key: 'author', value: 'JK Rowling' });
      expect(tokens[1]).toEqual({ type: 'range', key: 'words', value: '10000..50000' });
      expect(tokens[2]).toEqual({ type: 'key_value', key: 'complete', value: 'true' });
      expect(tokens[3]).toEqual({ type: 'exclusion', value: 'crossover' });
    });

    it('handles empty input', () => {
      const tokens = parseSearchSyntax('');
      expect(tokens).toEqual([]);
    });

    it('handles site shortcuts', () => {
      const tokens = parseSearchSyntax('ao3:harry potter');
      expect(tokens).toEqual([
        { type: 'key_value', key: 'source', value: 'ao3' },
        { type: 'word', value: 'harry' },
        { type: 'word', value: 'potter' },
      ]);
    });
  });

  describe('tokensToQueryParams', () => {
    it('converts bare words to q parameter', () => {
      const tokens = parseSearchSyntax('harry potter');
      const params = tokensToQueryParams(tokens);
      expect(params.get('q')).toBe('harry potter');
    });

    it('converts key:value to URL parameters', () => {
      const tokens = parseSearchSyntax('author:jkr');
      const params = tokensToQueryParams(tokens);
      expect(params.get('author')).toBe('jkr');
    });

    it('converts ranges to min/max parameters', () => {
      const tokens = parseSearchSyntax('words:50000..100000');
      const params = tokensToQueryParams(tokens);
      expect(params.get('min_words')).toBe('50000');
      expect(params.get('max_words')).toBe('100000');
    });

    it('converts exclusions to exclude parameter', () => {
      const tokens = parseSearchSyntax('-crossover');
      const params = tokensToQueryParams(tokens);
      expect(params.getAll('exclude')).toContain('crossover');
    });
  });

  describe('defaultFilters', () => {
    it('has correct defaults', () => {
      expect(defaultFilters.min_words).toBe(0);
      expect(defaultFilters.max_words).toBeUndefined();
      expect(defaultFilters.complete).toBe(false);
      expect(defaultFilters.sort).toBe('relevance');
    });
  });
});
```

# Chapter: OPDS Feed Implementation

## What Is OPDS?

OPDS (Open Publication Distribution System) is a standard for distributing ebooks. It allows e-readers and reading apps to browse and download content from FicHub directly.

OPDS feeds are XML documents that follow the Atom syndication format. Here's how FicHub implements them:

## The Catalog Feed

```rust
// src/routes/opds/feeds.rs
use axum::response::Response;
use axum::http::StatusCode;

pub async fn catalog_feed(
    State(state): State<Arc<AppState>>,
) -> Result<Response, AppError> {
    let base_url = format!("http://{}:{}", state.config.host, state.config.app_port);

    let xml = format!(r#"<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<feed xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom"
      xmlns:opds="http://opds-spec.org/2010/catalog">

    <title>FicHub Catalog</title>
    <subtitle>Self-hosted fanfiction downloader</subtitle>
    <link href="{}/opds/catalog" rel="self" type="application/atom+xml"/>
    <link href="{}/opds/catalog" rel="start" type="application/atom+xml"/>

    <entry>
        <title>Search</title>
        <link href="{}/opds/search" rel="subsection" type="application/atom+xml"/>
        <id>urn:fichub:search</id>
        <content>Search for fanfiction stories</content>
    </entry>

    <entry>
        <title>Tags</title>
        <link href="{}/opds/tags" rel="subsection" type="application/atom+xml"/>
        <id>urn:fichub:tags</id>
        <content>Browse stories by tag</content>
    </entry>

    <entry>
        <title>Recommendations</title>
        <link href="{}/opds/recommendations" rel="subsection" type="application/atom+xml"/>
        <id>urn:fichub:recommendations</id>
        <content>Get personalized recommendations</content>
    </entry>

</feed>"#, base_url, base_url, base_url, base_url, base_url);

    Ok((
        StatusCode::OK,
        [(axum::http::header::CONTENT_TYPE, "application/atom+xml; charset=utf-8")],
        xml,
    ).into_response())
}
```

## The Tags Feed

```rust
pub async fn tags_feed(
    State(state): State<Arc<AppState>>,
) -> Result<Response, AppError> {
    let base_url = format!("http://{}:{}", state.config.host, state.config.app_port);

    // Fetch tags from database
    let tags = sqlx::query_as::<_, Tag>(
        "SELECT * FROM tags WHERE NOT hidden ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT 100"
    )
    .fetch_all(&state.db)
    .await?;

    let mut entries = String::new();
    for tag in &tags {
        entries.push_str(&format!(r#"
    <entry>
        <title>{}</title>
        <link href="{}/opds/tags/{}" rel="subsection" type="application/atom+xml"/>
        <id>urn:fichub:tag:{}</id>
        <content>Tag: {} (score: {})</content>
    </entry>"#,
            escape_xml(&tag.name),
            base_url,
            tag.id,
            tag.id,
            escape_xml(&tag.name),
            tag.score,
        ));
    }

    let xml = format!(r#"<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<feed xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom">
    <title>Tags</title>
    <link href="{}/opds/tags" rel="self" type="application/atom+xml"/>
    <link href="{}/opds/catalog" rel="up" type="application/atom+xml"/>
    {}
</feed>"#, base_url, base_url, entries);

    Ok((
        StatusCode::OK,
        [(axum::http::header::CONTENT_TYPE, "application/atom+xml; charset=utf-8")],
        xml,
    ).into_response())
}
```

## The Search Feed

```rust
pub async fn search_feed(
    State(state): State<Arc<AppState>>,
    Query(params): Query<HashMap<String, String>>,
) -> Result<Response, AppError> {
    let query = params.get("q").unwrap_or(&String::new());
    let base_url = format!("http://{}:{}", state.config.host, state.config.app_port);

    // Perform search
    let results = sqlx::query_as::<_, FicInfo>(
        r#"
        SELECT * FROM fic_info
        WHERE to_tsvector('english', title || ' ' || author)
            @@ plainto_tsquery('english', $1)
        ORDER BY updated_at DESC
        LIMIT 50
        "#,
    )
    .bind(query)
    .fetch_all(&state.db)
    .await?;

    let mut entries = String::new();
    for fic in &results {
        let download_url = format!("{}/api/v0/export?url={}", base_url, urlencoding::encode(&fic.url));

        entries.push_str(&format!(r#"
    <entry>
        <title>{}</title>
        <author><name>{}</name></author>
        <link href="{}" rel="related" type="application/epub+zip"/>
        <link href="{}" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
        <id>urn:fichub:{}</id>
        <content type="text">{} words, {} chapters{}</content>
        <opds:price currency="USD">0.00</opds:price>
    </entry>"#,
            escape_xml(&fic.title),
            escape_xml(&fic.author),
            download_url,
            fic.url,
            fic.url_id,
            fic.words,
            fic.chapters,
            if fic.complete { " (Complete)" } else { "" },
        ));
    }

    let xml = format!(r#"<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<feed xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom"
      xmlns:opds="http://opds-spec.org/2010/catalog">
    <title>Search: {}</title>
    <link href="{}/opds/search?q={}" rel="self" type="application/atom+xml"/>
    <link href="{}/opds/catalog" rel="up" type="application/atom+xml"/>
    {}
</feed>"#, escape_xml(query), base_url, urlencoding::encode(query), base_url, entries);

    Ok((
        StatusCode::OK,
        [(axum::http::header::CONTENT_TYPE, "application/atom+xml; charset=utf-8")],
        xml,
    ).into_response())
}

fn escape_xml(s: &str) -> String {
    s.replace('&', "&amp;")
     .replace('<', "&lt;")
     .replace('>', "&gt;")
     .replace('"', "&quot;")
     .replace(''', "&apos;")
}
```

# Chapter: Tags System Deep Dive

## Tag Resolution

FicHub's tag system handles name → alias → new tag resolution:

```rust
// src/tags/resolve.rs

pub async fn resolve_tag(
    pool: &PgPool,
    tag_name: &str,
    tag_type: &str,
) -> Result<i32, sqlx::Error> {
    let normalized_name = normalize_tag_name(tag_name);

    // Step 1: Check if tag already exists
    if let Some(tag) = sqlx::query_as::<_, Tag>(
        "SELECT * FROM tags WHERE LOWER(name) = LOWER($1)"
    )
    .bind(&normalized_name)
    .fetch_optional(pool)
    .await?
    {
        return Ok(tag.id);
    }

    // Step 2: Check if there's an alias
    if let Some(alias) = sqlx::query_as::<_, TagAlias>(
        "SELECT ta.* FROM tag_aliases ta WHERE LOWER(ta.alias) = LOWER($1)"
    )
    .bind(&normalized_name)
    .fetch_optional(pool)
    .await?
    {
        return Ok(alias.tag_id);
    }

    // Step 3: Create new tag
    let tag = sqlx::query_as::<_, Tag>(
        r#"
        INSERT INTO tags (name, type)
        VALUES ($1, $2::tag_type)
        RETURNING *
        "#,
    )
    .bind(&normalized_name)
    .bind(tag_type)
    .fetch_one(pool)
    .await?;

    Ok(tag.id)
}

fn normalize_tag_name(name: &str) -> String {
    name.trim()
        .to_lowercase()
        .replace_whitespace(" ")
        .chars()
        .filter(|c| !c.is_control())
        .collect()
}
```

## Tag Voting System

```rust
// src/tags/voting.rs

pub async fn record_vote(
    pool: &PgPool,
    fic_url_id: &str,
    tag_id: i32,
    vote: i32, // 1 or -1
    voter_ip: &str,
) -> Result<i32, sqlx::Error> {
    // Upsert the vote
    sqlx::query(
        r#"
        INSERT INTO fic_tag_votes (fic_url_id, tag_id, vote, voter_ip)
        VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4::inet)
        ON CONFLICT (fic_url_id, tag_id, voter_ip)
        DO UPDATE SET vote = $3, created_at = NOW()
        "#,
    )
    .bind(fic_url_id)
    .bind(tag_id)
    .bind(vote)
    .bind(voter_ip)
    .execute(pool)
    .await?;

    // The trigger automatically updates the tag score
    // But we can also fetch the new score for the response
    let new_score: i32 = sqlx::query_scalar(
        "SELECT score FROM tags WHERE id = $1"
    )
    .bind(tag_id)
    .fetch_one(pool)
    .await?
    .unwrap_or(0);

    Ok(new_score)
}

pub async fn is_hidden(pool: &PgPool, tag_id: i32, threshold: i16) -> Result<bool, sqlx::Error> {
    let score: i32 = sqlx::query_scalar(
        "SELECT score FROM tags WHERE id = $1"
    )
    .bind(tag_id)
    .fetch_one(pool)
    .await?
    .unwrap_or(0);

    Ok(score < threshold as i32)
}

pub async fn compute_visibility(
    pool: &PgPool,
    tag_id: i32,
    hidden_threshold: i16,
    auto_delete_threshold: Option<i16>,
) -> Result<TagVisibility, sqlx::Error> {
    let score: i32 = sqlx::query_scalar(
        "SELECT score FROM tags WHERE id = $1"
    )
    .bind(tag_id)
    .fetch_one(pool)
    .await?
    .unwrap_or(0);

    if let Some(auto_delete) = auto_delete_threshold {
        if score <= auto_delete as i32 {
            return Ok(TagVisibility::AutoDelete);
        }
    }

    if score < hidden_threshold as i32 {
        Ok(TagVisibility::Hidden)
    } else {
        Ok(TagVisibility::Visible)
    }
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum TagVisibility {
    Visible,
    Hidden,
    AutoDelete,
}
```

## Tag Curator Actions

```rust
// src/tags/curator.rs

pub async fn create_alias(
    pool: &PgPool,
    alias: &str,
    tag_id: i32,
    curator_token: &str,
) -> Result<(), AppError> {
    // Verify curator token
    verify_curator_token(pool, curator_token).await?;

    // Create the alias
    sqlx::query(
        "INSERT INTO tag_aliases (alias, tag_id) VALUES ($1, $2)"
    )
    .bind(alias)
    .bind(tag_id)
    .execute(pool)
    .await?;

    Ok(())
}

pub async fn merge_tags(
    pool: &PgPool,
    source_tag_id: i32,
    target_tag_id: i32,
    curator_token: &str,
) -> Result<(), AppError> {
    verify_curator_token(pool, curator_token).await?;

    let mut tx = pool.begin().await?;

    // Move all fic_tag associations from source to target
    sqlx::query(
        r#"
        INSERT INTO fic_tags (fic_url_id, tag_id, submitted_by, created_at)
        SELECT fic_url_id, $2, submitted_by, created_at
        FROM fic_tags
        WHERE tag_id = $1
        ON CONFLICT (fic_url_id, tag_id) DO NOTHING
        "#,
    )
    .bind(source_tag_id)
    .bind(target_tag_id)
    .execute(&mut *tx)
    .await?;

    // Move all votes
    sqlx::query(
        r#"
        INSERT INTO fic_tag_votes (fic_url_id, tag_id, vote, voter_ip, created_at)
        SELECT fic_url_id, $2, vote, voter_ip, created_at
        FROM fic_tag_votes
        WHERE tag_id = $1
        ON CONFLICT (fic_url_id, tag_id, voter_ip) DO UPDATE SET vote = EXCLUDED.vote
        "#,
    )
    .bind(source_tag_id)
    .bind(target_tag_id)
    .execute(&mut *tx)
    .await?;

    // Move aliases
    sqlx::query(
        "UPDATE tag_aliases SET tag_id = $2 WHERE tag_id = $1"
    )
    .bind(source_tag_id)
    .bind(target_tag_id)
    .execute(&mut *tx)
    .await?;

    // Delete source tag
    sqlx::query("DELETE FROM tags WHERE id = $1")
        .bind(source_tag_id)
        .execute(&mut *tx)
        .await?;

    tx.commit().await?;

    Ok(())
}

pub async fn delete_tag(
    pool: &PgPool,
    tag_id: i32,
    curator_token: &str,
) -> Result<(), AppError> {
    verify_curator_token(pool, curator_token).await?;

    // Cascade deletes handle fic_tags, fic_tag_votes, tag_aliases
    sqlx::query("DELETE FROM tags WHERE id = $1")
        .bind(tag_id)
        .execute(pool)
        .await?;

    Ok(())
}

pub async fn list_flags(
    pool: &PgPool,
) -> Result<Vec<TagFlag>, sqlx::Error> {
    sqlx::query_as::<_, TagFlag>(
        r#"
        SELECT tf.*, t.name as tag_name
        FROM tag_flags tf
        JOIN tags t ON tf.tag_id = t.id
        WHERE tf.resolved = false
        ORDER BY tf.created_at DESC
        "#,
    )
    .fetch_all(pool)
    .await
}

pub async fn resolve_flag(
    pool: &PgPool,
    flag_id: i32,
    action: &str,
    curator_token: &str,
) -> Result<(), AppError> {
    verify_curator_token(pool, curator_token).await?;

    match action {
        "dismiss" => {
            sqlx::query("UPDATE tag_flags SET resolved = true WHERE id = $1")
                .bind(flag_id)
                .execute(pool)
                .await?;
        }
        "delete_tag" => {
            let tag_id: i32 = sqlx::query_scalar(
                "SELECT tag_id FROM tag_flags WHERE id = $1"
            )
            .bind(flag_id)
            .fetch_one(pool)
            .await?;

            delete_tag(pool, tag_id, curator_token).await?;

            sqlx::query("UPDATE tag_flags SET resolved = true WHERE id = $1")
                .bind(flag_id)
                .execute(pool)
                .await?;
        }
        _ => {
            return Err(AppError::BadRequest(-1, "invalid action".into()));
        }
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

# Chapter: Search Implementation Deep Dive

## Dynamic Query Building

FicHub's search uses SQLx QueryBuilder for dynamic SQL:

```rust
// src/search/builder.rs

use sqlx::QueryBuilder;

pub struct SearchQueryBuilder {
    conditions: Vec<String>,
    params: Vec<Box<dyn sqlx::Encode<'static, sqlx::Postgres> + Send + Sync>>,
    param_count: usize,
}

impl SearchQueryBuilder {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            conditions: Vec::new(),
            params: Vec::new(),
            param_count: 0,
        }
    }

    pub fn add_text_search(&mut self, query: &str) {
        if !query.is_empty() {
            self.param_count += 1;
            self.conditions.push(format!(
                "to_tsvector('english', f.title || ' ' || f.author) @@ plainto_tsquery('english', ${})",
                self.param_count
            ));
            self.params.push(Box::new(query.to_string()));
        }
    }

    pub fn add_min_words(&mut self, min_words: i32) {
        self.param_count += 1;
        self.conditions.push(format!("f.words >= ${}", self.param_count));
        self.params.push(Box::new(min_words));
    }

    pub fn add_max_words(&mut self, max_words: i32) {
        self.param_count += 1;
        self.conditions.push(format!("f.words <= ${}", self.param_count));
        self.params.push(Box::new(max_words));
    }

    pub fn add_complete_only(&mut self) {
        self.conditions.push("f.complete = true".to_string());
    }

    pub fn add_source(&mut self, source: &str) {
        self.param_count += 1;
        self.conditions.push(format!("f.source = ${}", self.param_count));
        self.params.push(Box::new(source.to_string()));
    }

    pub fn add_tag_filter(&mut self, tag_name: &str) {
        self.param_count += 1;
        self.conditions.push(format!(
            "f.tags @> ${}::jsonb",
            self.param_count
        ));
        self.params.push(Box::new(
            serde_json::json!([tag_name]).to_string()
        ));
    }

    pub fn build_where_clause(&self) -> String {
        if self.conditions.is_empty() {
            "WHERE true".to_string()
        } else {
            format!("WHERE {}", self.conditions.join(" AND "))
        }
    }

    pub fn build_count_query(&self) -> String {
        format!(
            "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fic_info f {}",
            self.build_where_clause()
        )
    }

    pub fn build_search_query(&self, order_by: &str, limit: i64, offset: i64) -> String {
        format!(
            "SELECT f.* FROM fic_info f {} ORDER BY {} LIMIT {} OFFSET {}",
            self.build_where_clause(),
            order_by,
            limit,
            offset
        )
    }
}
```

## Search Routes

```rust
// src/search/routes.rs

pub async fn search_handler(
    Query(params): Query<SearchParams>,
    State(state): State<Arc<AppState>>,
) -> Result<Json<Value>, AppError> {
    let query = params.q.unwrap_or_default();
    let page = params.page.unwrap_or(1).max(1);
    let per_page = params.per_page
        .unwrap_or(state.config.search_max_per_page as i32)
        .min(state.config.search_max_per_page as i32);
    let offset = ((page - 1) * per_page) as i64;

    // Build dynamic query
    let mut builder = SearchQueryBuilder::new();

    if !query.is_empty() {
        builder.add_text_search(&query);
    }

    if let Some(min_words) = params.min_words {
        builder.add_min_words(min_words);
    }

    if let Some(max_words) = params.max_words {
        builder.add_max_words(max_words);
    }

    if params.complete.unwrap_or(false) {
        builder.add_complete_only();
    }

    if let Some(ref source) = params.source {
        builder.add_source(source);
    }

    if let Some(ref tags) = params.tags {
        for tag in tags.split(',') {
            builder.add_tag_filter(tag.trim());
        }
    }

    // Determine sort order
    let order_by = match params.sort.as_deref() {
        Some("words") => "f.words DESC",
        Some("chapters") => "f.chapters DESC",
        Some("score") => "f.score DESC",
        _ => "f.updated_at DESC",
    };

    // Execute count query
    let count_query = builder.build_count_query();
    let total: i64 = sqlx::query_scalar(&count_query)
        .fetch_one(&state.db)
        .await?;

    // Execute search query
    let search_query = builder.build_search_query(order_by, per_page as i64, offset);
    let results = sqlx::query_as::<_, FicInfo>(&search_query)
        .fetch_all(&state.db)
        .await?;

    // Fetch tags for each result (batch)
    let url_ids: Vec<String> = results.iter().map(|r| r.url_id.clone()).collect();
    let all_tags = fetch_tags_for_fics(&state.db, &url_ids).await?;

    // Merge tags into results
    let results_with_tags: Vec<Value> = results.iter().map(|fic| {
        let tags = all_tags.get(&fic.url_id).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
        serde_json::json!({
            "url_id": fic.url_id,
            "title": fic.title,
            "author": fic.author,
            "words": fic.words,
            "chapters": fic.chapters,
            "complete": fic.complete,
            "source": fic.source,
            "tags": tags,
        })
    }).collect();

    Ok(Json(json!({
        "total": total,
        "page": page,
        "per_page": per_page,
        "results": results_with_tags,
    })))
}

async fn fetch_tags_for_fics(
    pool: &PgPool,
    url_ids: &[String],
) -> Result<HashMap<String, Vec<String>>, sqlx::Error> {
    if url_ids.is_empty() {
        return Ok(HashMap::new());
    }

    let rows = sqlx::query_as::<_, (String, String)>(
        r#"
        SELECT ft.fic_url_id, t.name
        FROM fic_tags ft
        JOIN tags t ON ft.tag_id = t.id
        WHERE ft.fic_url_id = ANY($1::text[])
        "#,
    )
    .bind(url_ids)
    .fetch_all(pool)
    .await?;

    let mut result: HashMap<String, Vec<String>> = HashMap::new();
    for (url_id, tag_name) in rows {
        result.entry(url_id).or_default().push(tag_name);
    }

    Ok(result)
}
```

### Structured Logging with Tracing

```rust
use tracing::{info, warn, error, debug, instrument};

// Instrumented function — logs entry/exit automatically
#[instrument(skip(state), fields(url_id = %url_id))]
async fn export_handler(
    State(state): State<Arc<AppState>>,
    url_id: String,
) -> Result<Json<Value>, AppError> {
    info!("Starting export");

    // ... export logic ...

    info!(duration_ms = start.elapsed().as_millis() as u64, "Export completed");

    Ok(result)
}
```

### Request Logging Middleware

```rust
async fn request_logging(
    request: Request,
    next: Next,
) -> Response {
    let method = request.method().clone();
    let uri = request.uri().clone();
    let start = Instant::now();

    let response = next.run(request).await;

    let status = response.status();
    let duration = start.elapsed();

    let level = if status.is_server_error() {
        tracing::Level::ERROR
    } else if status.is_client_error() {
        tracing::Level::WARN
    } else {
        tracing::Level::INFO
    };

    tracing::log!(
        level,
        method = %method,
        uri = %uri,
        status = status.as_u16(),
        duration_ms = duration.as_millis() as u64,
        "Request completed"
    );

    response
}
```

## Health Checks

```rust
pub async fn health_check(
    State(state): State<Arc<AppState>>,
) -> Json<Value> {
    let mut checks = HashMap::new();

    // Database check
    let db_ok = sqlx::query("SELECT 1")
        .execute(&state.db)
        .await
        .is_ok();
    checks.insert("database", db_ok);

    // Redis check
    let redis_ok = redis::cmd("PING")
        .query_async::<String>(&mut state.redis.clone())
        .await
        .is_ok();
    checks.insert("redis", redis_ok);

    // Disk cache check
    let cache_ok = std::fs::metadata(&state.config.cache_dir).is_ok();
    checks.insert("cache", cache_ok);

    let all_healthy = checks.values().all(|&v| v);

    Json(json!({
        "status": if all_healthy { "healthy" } else { "degraded" },
        "checks": checks,
        "version": env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"),
    }))
}
```

## Graceful Shutdown

```rust
use tokio::signal;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};

static SHUTDOWN: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);

pub async fn run_server(config: Config) {
    let app = build_router(state).await;
    let listener = TcpListener::bind(format!("0.0.0.0:{}", config.app_port))
        .await
        .unwrap();

    tracing::info!("Server starting on port {}", config.app_port);

    let server = axum::serve(listener, app)
        .with_graceful_shutdown(shutdown_signal());

    server.await.expect("Server error");
}

async fn shutdown_signal() {
    let ctrl_c = async {
        signal::ctrl_c()
            .await
            .expect("failed to install Ctrl+C handler");
    };

    #[cfg(unix)]
    let terminate = async {
        signal::unix::signal(signal::unix::SignalKind::terminate())
            .expect("failed to install signal handler")
            .recv()
            .await;
    };

    #[cfg(not(unix))]
    let terminate = std::future::pending::<()>();

    tokio::select! {
        _ = ctrl_c => {
            tracing::info!("Ctrl+C received, starting graceful shutdown");
        }
        _ = terminate => {
            tracing::info!("SIGTERM received, starting graceful shutdown");
        }
    }

    SHUTDOWN.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);

    // Give in-flight requests time to complete
    tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5)).await;

    tracing::info!("Server shut down gracefully");
}

pub fn is_shutting_down() -> bool {
    SHUTDOWN.load(Ordering::SeqCst)
}
```

# Chapter: Configuration Deep Dive

## Environment-Based Configuration

FicHub uses environment variables for configuration. Here's a comprehensive guide:

### Required Variables

```bash
# Database connection
DATABASE_URL=postgres://fichub:password@localhost/fichub

# Redis connection
REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1/

# Cache directory
CACHE_DIR=/var/lib/fichub/cache
```

### Optional Variables with Defaults

```bash
# Server
PORT=3000
NODE_NAME=orion

# Feature flags
DYNAMIC_RATE_LIMIT=true
EXPORT_VERSION=1

# Paths
TMP_DIR=/tmp/fichub
FRONTEND_DIR=./frontend/build

# Calibre (for EPUB conversion)
CALIBRE_CONTAINER=

# Recommender
REC_DEFAULT_DELAY_SECS=60
REC_MAX_RECOMMENDATIONS=20
REC_CACHE_TTL_HOURS=24
REC_PRECOMPUTE_ENABLED=false

# Tags
CURATOR_TOKEN=
TAG_HIDDEN_THRESHOLD=-5
TAG_SUBMIT_LIMIT_PER_HOUR=10
TAG_VOTE_LIMIT_PER_HOUR=30

# Search
SEARCH_MAX_PER_PAGE=50

# OPDS
OPDS_SHELF_TOKEN=

# Security
TRUSTED_PROXIES=127.0.0.1,::1
```

### Configuration Validation

```rust
impl Config {
    pub fn from_env() -> Self {
        let database_url = std::env::var("DATABASE_URL")
            .expect("DATABASE_URL must be set");

        // Validate database URL
        if !database_url.starts_with("postgres://") && !database_url.starts_with("postgresql://") {
            panic!("DATABASE_URL must start with postgres:// or postgresql://");
        }

        let redis_url = std::env::var("REDIS_URL")
            .expect("REDIS_URL must be set");

        let cache_dir = std::env::var("CACHE_DIR")
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| "./cache".to_string());

        // Validate cache directory is writable
        let cache_path = PathBuf::from(&cache_dir);
        if !cache_path.exists() {
            std::fs::create_dir_all(&cache_path)
                .expect("Failed to create CACHE_DIR");
        }

        let app_port = std::env::var("PORT")
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| "3000".to_string())
            .parse()
            .expect("PORT must be a valid port number");

        if app_port == 0 {
            panic!("PORT cannot be 0");
        }

        // Parse recommender settings
        let rec_default_delay_secs = std::env::var("REC_DEFAULT_DELAY_SECS")
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| "60".to_string())
            .parse()
            .unwrap_or(60);

        let rec_max_recommendations = std::env::var("REC_MAX_RECOMMENDATIONS")
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| "20".to_string())
            .parse()
            .unwrap_or(20);

        // Parse site-specific rate limits
        let rec_site_rate_limits = parse_site_rate_limits();

        Self {
            database_url,
            redis_url,
            cache_dir: cache_path,
            secondary_cache_dir: std::env::var("SECONDARY_CACHE_DIR")
                .ok()
                .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
                .map(PathBuf::from),
            export_version: std::env::var("EXPORT_VERSION")
                .unwrap_or_else(|_| "1".to_string())
                .parse()
                .unwrap_or(1),
            dynamic_rate_limit: std::env::var("DYNAMIC_RATE_LIMIT")
                .unwrap_or_else(|_| "true".to_string())
                .parse()
                .unwrap_or(true),
            node_name: std::env::var("NODE_NAME")
                .unwrap_or_else(|_| "orion".to_string()),
            calibre_container: std::env::var("CALIBRE_CONTAINER")
                .unwrap_or_default(),
            tmp_dir: PathBuf::from(std::env::var("TMP_DIR")
                .unwrap_or_else(|_| "./tmp".to_string())),
            app_port,
            frontend_dir: PathBuf::from(std::env::var("FRONTEND_DIR")
                .unwrap_or_else(|_| "./frontend/build".to_string())),
            trusted_proxies: std::env::var("TRUSTED_PROXIES")
                .unwrap_or_else(|_| "127.0.0.1,::1".to_string())
                .split(',')
                .map(|s| s.trim().to_string())
                .collect(),
            ip_tag_sources: parse_ip_tag_sources(),
            rec_default_delay_secs,
            rec_site_rate_limits,
            rec_max_favourite_pages: env_or("REC_MAX_FAVOURITE_PAGES", 10),
            rec_max_user_favourite_pages: env_or("REC_MAX_USER_FAVOURITE_PAGES", 5),
            rec_max_recommendations,
            rec_min_favouriters_for_collab: env_or("REC_MIN_FAVOURITERS_FOR_COLLAB", 3),
            rec_voting_boost_gamma: env_or_f64("REC_VOTING_BOOST_GAMMA", 0.5),
            rec_cache_ttl_hours: env_or("REC_CACHE_TTL_HOURS", 24),
            rec_suggest_limit_per_hour: env_or("REC_SUGGEST_LIMIT_PER_HOUR", 5),
            rec_vote_limit_per_hour: env_or("REC_VOTE_LIMIT_PER_HOUR", 30),
            rec_precompute_enabled: env_or_bool("REC_PRECOMPUTE_ENABLED", false),
            rec_precompute_interval_hours: env_or("REC_PRECOMPUTE_INTERVAL_HOURS", 24),
            rec_enable_cross_site: env_or_bool("REC_ENABLE_CROSS_SITE", true),
            curator_token: std::env::var("CURATOR_TOKEN").ok()
                .filter(|s| !s.is_empty()),
            tag_hidden_threshold: env_or_i16("TAG_HIDDEN_THRESHOLD", -5),
            tag_auto_delete_threshold: std::env::var("TAG_AUTO_DELETE_THRESHOLD")
                .ok()
                .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok()),
            tag_submit_limit_per_hour: env_or("TAG_SUBMIT_LIMIT_PER_HOUR", 10),
            tag_vote_limit_per_hour: env_or("TAG_VOTE_LIMIT_PER_HOUR", 30),
            search_max_per_page: env_or("SEARCH_MAX_PER_PAGE", 50),
            opds_shelf_token: std::env::var("OPDS_SHELF_TOKEN")
                .unwrap_or_else(|_| uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string()),
        }
    }

}

fn env_or(name: &str, default: u32) -> u32 {
    std::env::var(name)
        .ok()
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(default)
}

fn env_or_f64(name: &str, default: f64) -> f64 {
    std::env::var(name)
        .ok()
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(default)
}

fn env_or_bool(name: &str, default: bool) -> bool {
    std::env::var(name)
        .ok()
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(default)
}

fn env_or_i16(name: &str, default: i16) -> i16 {
    std::env::var(name)
        .ok()
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(default)
}

fn parse_site_rate_limits() -> HashMap<String, u64> {
    std::env::var("REC_SITE_RATE_LIMITS")
        .unwrap_or_default()
        .split(',')
        .filter_map(|pair| {
            let parts: Vec<&str> = pair.split('=').collect();
            if parts.len() == 2 {
                Some((parts[0].trim().to_string(), parts[1].trim().parse().ok()?))
            } else {
                None
            }
        })
        .collect()
}

fn parse_ip_tag_sources() -> Vec<(String, String, String)> {
    std::env::var("IP_TAG_SOURCES")
        .unwrap_or_default()
        .split(';')
        .filter_map(|entry| {
            let parts: Vec<&str> = entry.split(',').collect();
            if parts.len() == 3 {
                Some((
                    parts[0].trim().to_string(),
                    parts[1].trim().to_string(),
                    parts[2].trim().to_string(),
                ))
            } else {
                None
            }
        })
        .collect()
}
```

# Chapter: Error Handling Patterns

## Error Types in FicHub

FicHub uses a central error type that converts automatically to HTTP responses:

```rust
#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum AppError {
    BadRequest(i32, String),
    RateLimited(u64),
    NotFound(String),
    Internal(String),
    ScrapeError(String),
    ExportError(String),
    Database(String),
    CacheError(String),
}

impl std::fmt::Display for AppError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        match self {
            AppError::BadRequest(code, msg) => write!(f, "BadRequest({}): {}", code, msg),
            AppError::RateLimited(retry_after) => write!(f, "RateLimited: retry after {}s", retry_after),
            AppError::NotFound(msg) => write!(f, "NotFound: {}", msg),
            AppError::Internal(msg) => write!(f, "Internal: {}", msg),
            AppError::ScrapeError(msg) => write!(f, "ScrapeError: {}", msg),
            AppError::ExportError(msg) => write!(f, "ExportError: {}", msg),
            AppError::Database(msg) => write!(f, "Database: {}", msg),
            AppError::CacheError(msg) => write!(f, "CacheError: {}", msg),
        }
    }
}

impl IntoResponse for AppError {
    fn into_response(self) -> Response {
        let (status, body) = match self {
            AppError::BadRequest(code, msg) => (
                StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,
                json!({"err": code, "msg": msg}),
            ),
            AppError::RateLimited(retry_after) => (
                StatusCode::TOO_MANY_REQUESTS,
                json!({"err": -429, "msg": "rate limited", "retry_after": retry_after}),
            ),
            AppError::NotFound(msg) => (
                StatusCode::NOT_FOUND,
                json!({"err": -5, "msg": msg}),
            ),
            AppError::Internal(msg) => {
                tracing::error!("Internal error: {}", msg);
                (
                    StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
                    json!({"err": -1, "msg": "internal server error"}),
                )
            }
            AppError::ScrapeError(msg) => (
                StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY,
                json!({"err": -6, "msg": msg}),
            ),
            AppError::ExportError(msg) => {
                tracing::error!("Export error: {}", msg);
                (
                    StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
                    json!({"err": -5, "msg": "export failed"}),
                )
            }
            AppError::Database(msg) => {
                tracing::error!("Database error: {}", msg);
                (
                    StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
                    json!({"err": -1, "msg": "database error"}),
                )
            }
            AppError::CacheError(msg) => {
                tracing::error!("Cache error: {}", msg);
                (
                    StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
                    json!({"err": -1, "msg": "cache error"}),
                )
            }
        };

        (status, Json(body)).into_response()
    }
}

// From implementations for automatic error conversion
impl From<sqlx::Error> for AppError {
    fn from(err: sqlx::Error) -> Self {
        match err {
            sqlx::Error::RowNotFound => {
                AppError::NotFound("resource not found".into())
            }
            sqlx::Error::Database(ref db_err) => {
                if db_err.code() == Some("23505".into()) {
                    AppError::BadRequest(-2, "already exists".into())
                } else {
                    AppError::Database(db_err.message().unwrap_or("unknown").into())
                }
            }
            _ => AppError::Database(err.to_string()),
        }
    }
}

impl From<redis::RedisError> for AppError {
    fn from(err: redis::RedisError) -> Self {
        AppError::CacheError(err.to_string())
    }
}

impl From<reqwest::Error> for AppError {
    fn from(err: reqwest::Error) -> Self {
        if err.is_timeout() {
            AppError::ScrapeError("request timed out".into())
        } else if err.is_connect() {
            AppError::ScrapeError("connection failed".into())
        } else {
            AppError::ScrapeError(err.to_string())
        }
    }
}

impl From<std::io::Error> for AppError {
    fn from(err: std::io::Error) -> Self {
        AppError::Internal(err.to_string())
    }
}

impl From<serde_json::Error> for AppError {
    fn from(err: serde_json::Error) -> Self {
        AppError::Internal(format!("JSON error: {}", err))
    }
}
```

## Error Context

Add context to errors for better debugging:

```rust
use anyhow::{Context, Result};

async fn export_story(url: &str, state: &Arc<AppState>) -> Result<PathBuf> {
    let metadata = scrape_site(&state.http_client, url)
        .await
        .context("Failed to scrape story metadata")?;

    let chapters = fetch_chapters(&state.http_client, &metadata)
        .await
        .context("Failed to fetch chapters")?;

    let epub_path = generate_epub(&metadata, &chapters, &state.config)
        .context("Failed to generate EPUB")?;

    save_to_cache(&state.db, &metadata.url_id, &epub_path)
        .await
        .context("Failed to save to cache")?;

    Ok(epub_path)
}
```

## Error Recovery Strategies

```rust
pub async fn resilient_export(
    url: &str,
    state: &Arc<AppState>,
) -> Result<PathBuf, AppError> {
    let max_retries = 3;

    for attempt in 0..max_retries {
        match export_story(url, state).await {
            Ok(path) => return Ok(path),
            Err(AppError::ScrapeError(msg)) if msg.contains("timeout") && attempt < max_retries - 1 => {
                tracing::warn!(
                    url = url,
                    attempt = attempt + 1,
                    "Export timed out, retrying"
                );
                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(2u64.pow(attempt as u32))).await;
                continue;
            }
            Err(AppError::ScrapeError(msg)) if msg.contains("rate limited") && attempt < max_retries - 1 => {
                tracing::warn!(
                    url = url,
                    attempt = attempt + 1,
                    "Rate limited, retrying after delay"
                );
                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(30)).await;
                continue;
            }
            Err(e) => return Err(e),
        }
    }

    Err(AppError::Internal("max retries exceeded".into()))
}
```

# Chapter: Production Deployment Patterns

## Docker Compose Production Setup

```yaml
version: '3.8'

services:
  app:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    environment:
      - DATABASE_URL=postgres://fichub:${DB_PASSWORD}@db/fichub
      - REDIS_URL=redis://:${REDIS_PASSWORD}@cache/
      - CACHE_DIR=/home/fichub/cache
      - FRONTEND_DIR=/home/fichub/frontend/build
      - PORT=3000
      - RUST_LOG=info,fichub=debug
    volumes:
      - cache_data:/home/fichub/cache
      - tmp_data:/home/fichub/tmp
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
      cache:
        condition: service_healthy
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512M
          cpus: '0.8'
        reservations:
          memory: 256M
          cpus: '0.4'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:3000/api/v0/health"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 40s
    logging:
      driver: json-file
      options:
        max-size: "10m"
        max-file: "3"

  db:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_USER=fichub
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${DB_PASSWORD}
      - POSTGRES_DB=fichub
    volumes:
      - pg_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U fichub"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 256M

  cache:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    command: redis-server --requirepass ${REDIS_PASSWORD} --maxmemory 128mb --maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru
    volumes:
      - redis_data:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "-a", "${REDIS_PASSWORD}", "ping"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 128M

  nginx:
    image: nginx:alpine
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - ./nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf:ro
      - ./certs:/etc/nginx/certs:ro
    depends_on:
      - app
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  pg_data:
  redis_data:
  cache_data:
  tmp_data:
```

## Nginx Reverse Proxy Configuration

```nginx
worker_processes auto;
error_log /var/log/nginx/error.log warn;
pid /var/run/nginx.pid;

events {
    worker_connections 1024;
}

http {
    include /etc/nginx/mime.types;
    default_type application/octet-stream;

    log_format main '$remote_addr - $remote_user [$time_local] "$request" '
                    '$status $body_bytes_sent "$http_referer" '
                    '"$http_user_agent" "$http_x_forwarded_for"';

    access_log /var/log/nginx/access.log main;

    sendfile on;
    tcp_nopush on;
    tcp_nodelay on;
    keepalive_timeout 65;
    types_hash_max_size 2048;

    # Gzip compression
    gzip on;
    gzip_vary on;
    gzip_proxied any;
    gzip_comp_level 6;
    gzip_types text/plain text/css application/json application/javascript text/xml application/xml;

    # Rate limiting
    limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=api:10m rate=10r/s;
    limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=export:10m rate=1r/s;

    # Upstream
    upstream fichub {
        server app:3000;
    }

    # HTTP → HTTPS redirect
    server {
        listen 80;
        server_name fichub.example.com;
        return 301 https://$host$request_uri;
    }

    # HTTPS server
    server {
        listen 443 ssl http2;
        server_name fichub.example.com;

        ssl_certificate /etc/nginx/certs/fullchain.pem;
        ssl_certificate_key /etc/nginx/certs/privkey.pem;
        ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;
        ssl_ciphers HIGH:!aNULL:!MD5;
        ssl_prefer_server_ciphers on;

        # Security headers
        add_header X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN" always;
        add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always;
        add_header X-XSS-Protection "1; mode=block" always;
        add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains" always;

        # API endpoints
        location /api/ {
            limit_req zone=api burst=20 nodelay;
            proxy_pass http://fichub;
            proxy_set_header Host $host;
            proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
            proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
            proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
        }

        # Export endpoint (stricter rate limiting)
        location /api/v0/export {
            limit_req zone=export burst=5 nodelay;
            proxy_pass http://fichub;
            proxy_set_header Host $host;
            proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
            proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
            proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
            proxy_read_timeout 120s;
        }

        # OPDS feeds
        location /opds/ {
            proxy_pass http://fichub;
            proxy_set_header Host $host;
            proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        }

        # Cache files (long cache)
        location /cache/ {
            proxy_pass http://fichub;
            proxy_cache_valid 200 1y;
            add_header Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable";
        }

        # Static assets (immutable)
        location /assets/ {
            proxy_pass http://fichub;
            proxy_cache_valid 200 1y;
            add_header Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable";
        }

        # Everything else
        location / {
            proxy_pass http://fichub;
            proxy_set_header Host $host;
            proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
            proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
            proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
            add_header Cache-Control "no-cache, must-revalidate";
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
// Metrics endpoint
pub async fn metrics_handler() -> Response {
    let encoder = TextEncoder::new();
    let metric_families = prometheus::gather();
    let mut buffer = Vec::new();
    encoder.encode(&metric_families, &mut buffer).unwrap();

    Response::builder()
        .status(200)
        .header("Content-Type", encoder.format_type())
        .body(buffer.into())
        .unwrap()
}
```

## Backup Strategy

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# backup.sh — Daily backup script

set -e

BACKUP_DIR="/var/backups/fichub"
DATE=$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)
RETENTION_DAYS=30

# Create backup directory
mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR"

# Backup PostgreSQL
echo "Backing up PostgreSQL..."
pg_dump -U fichub fichub | gzip > "$BACKUP_DIR/db_$DATE.sql.gz"

# Backup Redis
echo "Backing up Redis..."
redis-cli BGSAVE
sleep 5
cp /var/lib/redis/dump.rdb "$BACKUP_DIR/redis_$DATE.rdb"

# Backup configuration
echo "Backing up configuration..."
tar czf "$BACKUP_DIR/config_$DATE.tar.gz"     /home/fichub/.env     /home/fichub/nginx.conf

# Backup cache manifest (not all files)
echo "Backing up cache manifest..."
find /home/fichub/cache -type f -name "*.epub" > "$BACKUP_DIR/cache_manifest_$DATE.txt"

# Clean up old backups
echo "Cleaning up old backups..."
find "$BACKUP_DIR" -name "*.gz" -mtime +$RETENTION_DAYS -delete
find "$BACKUP_DIR" -name "*.rdb" -mtime +$RETENTION_DAYS -delete
find "$BACKUP_DIR" -name "*.txt" -mtime +$RETENTION_DAYS -delete

echo "Backup complete: $DATE"
```

Add to cron:

```bash
# Daily backup at 3 AM
0 3 * * * /home/fichub/backup.sh >> /var/log/fichub-backup.log 2>&1
```

# Chapter: Advanced Web Scraping Techniques

## HTML Parsing Deep Dive

### Understanding the Scraper Crate

The `scraper` crate provides jQuery-like HTML parsing. Here's how to use it effectively:

```rust
use scraper::{Html, Selector};

fn parse_story_metadata(html: &str) -> Result<StoryMetadata, ScrapeError> {
    let document = Html::parse_document(html);

    // Parse title
    let title_selector = Selector::parse("h1.title")
        .map_err(|e| ScrapeError::Parse(e.to_string()))?;
    let title = document
        .select(&title_selector)
        .next()
        .map(|el| el.text().collect::<String>().trim().to_string())
        .unwrap_or_default();

    // Parse author
    let author_selector = Selector::parse("a.author")
        .map_err(|e| ScrapeError::Parse(e.to_string()))?;
    let author = document
        .select(&author_selector)
        .next()
        .map(|el| el.text().collect::<String>().trim().to_string())
        .unwrap_or_default();

    // Parse word count from metadata section
    let stats_selector = Selector::parse("span.stats .words")
        .map_err(|e| ScrapeError::Parse(e.to_string()))?;
    let words = document
        .select(&stats_selector)
        .next()
        .and_then(|el| el.text().next())
        .and_then(|t| t.trim().replace(',', "").parse::<i32>().ok())
        .unwrap_or(0);

    // Parse tags
    let tag_selector = Selector::parse("ul.tags li a")
        .map_err(|e| ScrapeError::Parse(e.to_string()))?;
    let tags: Vec<String> = document
        .select(&tag_selector)
        .map(|el| el.text().collect::<String>().trim().to_string())
        .filter(|t| !t.is_empty())
        .collect();

    // Parse chapter content
    let content_selector = Selector::parse("div.chapter-content")
        .map_err(|e| ScrapeError::Parse(e.to_string()))?;
    let content = document
        .select(&content_selector)
        .next()
        .map(|el| el.inner_html())
        .unwrap_or_default();

    // Parse completion status
    let status_selector = Selector::parse("span.status")
        .map_err(|e| ScrapeError::Parse(e.to_string()))?;
    let complete = document
        .select(&status_selector)
        .next()
        .and_then(|el| el.text().next())
        .map(|t| t.trim().to_lowercase() == "complete")
        .unwrap_or(false);

    Ok(StoryMetadata {
        title,
        author,
        words,
        tags,
        content,
        complete,
    })
}
```

### Handling Different HTML Structures

Different sites have different HTML structures. FicHub handles this with site-specific parsers:

```rust
pub struct SiteParser {
    title_selector: String,
    author_selector: String,
    content_selector: String,
    word_count_selector: Option<String>,
    chapter_selector: Option<String>,
}

impl SiteParser {
    pub fn parse(&self, html: &str) -> Result<StoryMetadata, ScrapeError> {
        let document = Html::parse_document(html);

        let title = self.extract_text(&document, &self.title_selector)?;
        let author = self.extract_text(&document, &self.author_selector)?;
        let content = self.extract_html(&document, &self.content_selector)?;
        let words = self.word_count_selector.as_ref()
            .and_then(|s| self.extract_number(&document, s))
            .unwrap_or_else(|| content.split_whitespace().count() as i32);

        Ok(StoryMetadata {
            title,
            author,
            words,
            content,
            tags: vec![],
            complete: false,
        })
    }

    fn extract_text(&self, document: &Html, selector: &str) -> Result<String, ScrapeError> {
        let sel = Selector::parse(selector)
            .map_err(|e| ScrapeError::Parse(e.to_string()))?;
        Ok(document
            .select(&sel)
            .next()
            .map(|el| el.text().collect::<String>().trim().to_string())
            .unwrap_or_default())
    }

    fn extract_html(&self, document: &Html, selector: &str) -> Result<String, ScrapeError> {
        let sel = Selector::parse(selector)
            .map_err(|e| ScrapeError::Parse(e.to_string()))?;
        Ok(document
            .select(&sel)
            .next()
            .map(|el| el.inner_html())
            .unwrap_or_default())
    }

    fn extract_number(&self, document: &Html, selector: &str) -> Option<i32> {
        let sel = Selector::parse(selector).ok()?;
        document
            .select(&sel)
            .next()
            .and_then(|el| el.text().next())
            .and_then(|t| t.trim().replace(',', "").parse::<i32>().ok())
    }
}
```

## Rate Limiting per Site

Different sites have different rate limits. FicHub implements per-site rate limiting:

```rust
pub struct SiteRateLimiter {
    limits: HashMap<String, RateLimitConfig>,
    state: HashMap<String, RateLimitState>,
}

struct RateLimitConfig {
    requests_per_second: f64,
    burst_size: u32,
}

struct RateLimitState {
    tokens: f64,
    last_refill: Instant,
}

impl SiteRateLimiter {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        let mut limits = HashMap::new();

        // AO3: 1 request per second, burst of 3
        limits.insert("ao3".to_string(), RateLimitConfig {
            requests_per_second: 1.0,
            burst_size: 3,
        });

        // FFNet: 2 requests per second, burst of 5
        limits.insert("ffnet".to_string(), RateLimitConfig {
            requests_per_second: 2.0,
            burst_size: 5,
        });

        // XenForo: 0.5 requests per second, burst of 2
        limits.insert("xenforo".to_string(), RateLimitConfig {
            requests_per_second: 0.5,
            burst_size: 2,
        });

        Self {
            limits,
            state: HashMap::new(),
        }
    }

    pub async fn wait_for_slot(&mut self, site: &str) {
        let config = self.limits.get(site).cloned().unwrap_or(RateLimitConfig {
            requests_per_second: 1.0,
            burst_size: 1,
        });

        let state = self.state.entry(site.to_string()).or_insert(RateLimitState {
            tokens: config.burst_size as f64,
            last_refill: Instant::now(),
        });

        // Refill tokens
        let elapsed = state.last_refill.elapsed().as_secs_f64();
        state.tokens = (state.tokens + elapsed * config.requests_per_second)
            .min(config.burst_size as f64);
        state.last_refill = Instant::now();

        // Wait if no tokens available
        if state.tokens < 1.0 {
            let wait_time = (1.0 - state.tokens) / config.requests_per_second;
            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs_f64(wait_time)).await;
            state.tokens = 1.0;
        }

        state.tokens -= 1.0;
    }
}
```

## Error Recovery in Scrapers

```rust
pub async fn resilient_scrape(
    client: &Client,
    url: &str,
    max_retries: u32,
) -> Result<String, ScrapeError> {
    let mut last_error = None;

    for attempt in 0..max_retries {
        match client.get(url).send().await {
            Ok(response) => {
                if response.status().is_success() {
                    return response.text().await.map_err(Into::into);
                }

                // Don't retry on client errors (4xx)
                if response.status().is_client_error() {
                    return Err(ScrapeError::Http(
                        reqwest::Error::from(response)
                    ));
                }

                // Server error (5xx) — retryable
                last_error = Some(ScrapeError::Parse(
                    format!("HTTP {}", response.status())
                ));
            }
            Err(e) => {
                if e.is_timeout() || e.is_connect() {
                    last_error = Some(ScrapeError::Http(e));
                } else {
                    return Err(ScrapeError::Http(e));
                }
            }
        }

        // Exponential backoff with jitter
        let base_delay = 2u64.pow(attempt);
        let jitter = rand::thread_rng().gen_range(0..base_delay);
        let delay = Duration::from_secs(base_delay + jitter);

        tracing::warn!(
            url = url,
            attempt = attempt + 1,
            max_retries = max_retries,
            delay_ms = delay.as_millis() as u64,
            "Retrying request"
        );
        tokio::time::sleep(delay).await;
    }

    last_error.ok_or_else(|| ScrapeError::Parse("max retries exceeded".into()))
}
```

## Chapter Content Formatting

### Cleaning HTML Content

Fanfiction content often contains invalid or messy HTML. Here's how to clean it:

```rust
fn clean_chapter_html(html: &str) -> String {
    // Parse the HTML
    let document = Html::parse_document(html);

    // Remove script and style tags
    let mut clean = html.to_string();
    let script_re = regex::Regex::new(r"<script[^>]*>.*?</script>").unwrap();
    let style_re = regex::Regex::new(r"<style[^>]*>.*?</style>").unwrap();
    clean = script_re.replace_all(&clean, "").to_string();
    clean = style_re.replace_all(&clean, "").to_string();

    // Remove comments
    let comment_re = regex::Regex::new(r"<!--.*?-->").unwrap();
    clean = comment_re.replace_all(&clean, "").to_string();

    // Fix common issues
    // 1. Unclosed tags
    let br_re = regex::Regex::new(r"<br\s*/?>").unwrap();
    clean = br_re.replace_all(&clean, "<br/>").to_string();

    // 2. Convert div to p for paragraphs
    let div_p_re = regex::Regex::new(r"<div[^>]*>(.*?)</div>").unwrap();
    clean = div_p_re.replace_all(&clean, "<p>$1</p>").to_string();

    // 3. Remove empty paragraphs
    let empty_p_re = regex::Regex::new(r"<p>\s*</p>").unwrap();
    clean = empty_p_re.replace_all(&clean, "").to_string();

    // 4. Normalize whitespace
    let space_re = regex::Regex::new(r"\s+").unwrap();
    clean = space_re.replace_all(&clean, " ").to_string();

    clean.trim().to_string()
}
```

### Custom Metadata

Add rich metadata to EPUBs:

```rust
fn set_epub_metadata(
    builder: &mut EpubBuilder<ZipLibrary>,
    metadata: &FicMetadata,
) -> Result<(), ExportError> {
    // Basic metadata
    builder.set_metadata("title", &metadata.title)?;
    builder.set_metadata("creator", &metadata.author)?;
    builder.set_metadata("language", "en")?;
    builder.set_metadata("publisher", "FicHub")?;

    // Description
    if !metadata.summary.is_empty() {
        builder.set_metadata("description", &metadata.summary)?;
    }

    // Rights notice
    builder.set_metadata("rights", &format!(
        "Fanfiction by {}. Original work belongs to the respective authors.",
        metadata.author
    ))?;

    // Unique identifier
    builder.set_metadata("identifier", &format!(
        "urn:fichub:{}",
        metadata.url_id
    ))?;

    // Dates
    let now = chrono::Utc::now().format("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ");
    builder.set_metadata("date", &now.to_string())?;

    // Source URL
    builder.set_metadata("source", &metadata.url)?;

    // Custom FicHub metadata
    builder.set_metadata("fichub:words", &metadata.words.to_string())?;
    builder.set_metadata("fichub:chapters", &metadata.chapters.to_string())?;
    builder.set_metadata("fichub:complete", &metadata.complete.to_string())?;
    builder.set_metadata("fichub:source", &metadata.source)?;

    Ok(())
}
```

# Chapter: Disk Cache Advanced Topics

## Cache Invalidation Strategies

### Time-Based Expiration

```rust
pub fn is_cache_expired(path: &PathBuf, max_age: Duration) -> bool {
    match std::fs::metadata(path) {
        Ok(metadata) => {
            if let Ok(modified) = metadata.modified() {
                modified.elapsed().unwrap_or(Duration::ZERO) > max_age
            } else {
                true // Assume expired if we can't get modification time
            }
        }
        Err(_) => true, // File doesn't exist — treat as expired
    }
}

// Check cache with expiration
pub async fn get_cached_export(
    url_id: &str,
    config: &Config,
) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    let cache_path = config.cache_dir.join(format!("epub/{}.epub", url_id));

    if !cache_path.exists() {
        return None;
    }

    // Check if cache is expired (24 hours)
    if is_cache_expired(&cache_path, Duration::from_secs(24 * 3600)) {
        tracing::info!(
            url_id = url_id,
            "Cache expired, re-exporting"
        );
        return None;
    }

    Some(cache_path)
}
```

### Content-Based Cache Keys

Use content hashing for cache keys instead of URL IDs:

```rust
use sha2::{Sha256, Digest};

fn compute_cache_key(url: &str, version: i32) -> String {
    let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
    hasher.update(url.as_bytes());
    hasher.update(version.to_string().as_bytes());
    let result = hasher.finalize();
    hex::encode(result)
}

// Usage
let cache_key = compute_cache_key(url, config.export_version);
let cache_path = config.cache_dir.join(format!("epub/{}.epub", cache_key));
```

### Cache Warming

Pre-populate the cache with popular content:

```rust
pub async fn warm_cache(
    state: &Arc<AppState>,
) -> Result<(), AppError> {
    // Get the most popular stories
    let popular = sqlx::query_as::<_, FicInfo>(
        r#"
        SELECT f.*
        FROM fic_info f
        JOIN (
            SELECT url_id, COUNT(*) as downloads
            FROM export_log
            WHERE created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days'
            GROUP BY url_id
            ORDER BY downloads DESC
            LIMIT 10
        ) e ON f.url_id = e.url_id
        "#,
    )
    .fetch_all(&state.db)
    .await?;

    for fic in &popular {
        let cache_path = state.config.cache_dir.join(format!("epub/{}.epub", fic.url_id));
        if !cache_path.exists() {
            tracing::info!(
                url_id = %fic.url_id,
                title = %fic.title,
                "Warming cache"
            );

            // Re-export the story to populate cache
            if let Err(e) = export_story(&fic.url, state).await {
                tracing::warn!(
                    url_id = %fic.url_id,
                    error = %e,
                    "Cache warming failed"
                );
            }
        }
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

## Cache Monitoring

```rust
pub fn cache_stats(cache_dir: &PathBuf) -> Result<CacheStats, std::io::Error> {
    let mut stats = CacheStats::default();

    for entry in std::fs::read_dir(cache_dir)? {
        let entry = entry?;
        let metadata = entry.metadata()?;

        if metadata.is_file() {
            let extension = entry.path()
                .extension()
                .and_then(|e| e.to_str())
                .unwrap_or("")
                .to_string();

            stats.total_files += 1;
            stats.total_size += metadata.len();

            *stats.by_extension.entry(extension).or_insert(0) += 1;

            if let Ok(modified) = metadata.modified() {
                if stats.oldest_file.is_none() || modified < stats.oldest_file.unwrap() {
                    stats.oldest_file = Some(modified);
                }
                if stats.newest_file.is_none() || modified > stats.newest_file.unwrap() {
                    stats.newest_file = Some(modified);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    Ok(stats)
}

#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct CacheStats {
    pub total_files: u64,
    pub total_size: u64,
    pub oldest_file: Option<SystemTime>,
    pub newest_file: Option<SystemTime>,
    pub by_extension: HashMap<String, u64>,
}
```
